copy_text: Home Services International SEO [ Services / International SEO ] International SEO services. Reach every market in its own language. International SEO makes sure search engines show the right language and country version of your site to each market, and that every version earns rankings of its own. Reinforce Lab's international SEO services plan the structure, implement hreflang, localize with native review and report market by market, following Google's own guidance. Get your free diagnostic → Site structures Market routing hreflang → right page Four language and market versions of one page are linked to each other with hreflang, and a searcher in each market is served the right version: right language, right market, right page. SEARCH EN · X-DEFAULT / DE /de/ FR-CA /fr-ca/ EN-GB /uk/ HREFLANG · EVERY VERSION LISTS EVERY OTHER RIGHT LANGUAGE · RIGHT MARKET · RIGHT PAGE RIGHT LANGUAGE · RIGHT MARKET · RIGHT PAGE [ Site structure ] Country domains, subdomains or subdirectories? Google lists four ways to structure a multi-regional site. Each has trade-offs; this is how Google describes them. Structure Example Strengths (per Google) Drawbacks (per Google) Country domain example.de Clear geotargeting and easy separation; "a strong signal" of the target country; server location irrelevant Targets one country only; more infrastructure; can be expensive or hard to get Subdomain de.example.com Easy to set up and separate; allows different server locations Users may not recognise the target country from the URL; separate sites to maintain Subdirectory example.com/de/ Lowest maintenance; easy to set up; same hosting Users may not recognise the target country from the URL; single server location URL parameter example.com?loc=de n/a Not recommended by Google; hard to segment Source: Google, Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites . Our default for most B2B sites: subdirectories on one strong domain, unless a legal, brand or market reason points elsewhere. [ hreflang ] How does hreflang work? hreflang tells Google which pages are language or regional versions of each other, so each searcher gets the right one. Small mistakes make Google ignore it. These are the rules. Every version lists every version Each page lists itself and all its alternates. If page X links to page Y, page Y must link back, or the annotations may be ignored. Use valid codes Language in ISO 639-1 (e.g. de ), with an optional region in ISO 3166-1 Alpha 2 (e.g. de-AT ). A region on its own is invalid. Set a fallback x-default is used when no other version matches the user's language or region, often a language selector or global page. Pick one method HTML tags, HTTP headers or the XML sitemap. Large sites usually manage hreflang in sitemaps. Example · HTML head of every version <!-- listed on /, /de/, /fr-ca/ and /uk/ alike --> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" en "    href="https://example.com/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" de "    href="https://example.com/de/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" fr-CA " href="https://example.com/fr-ca/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" en-GB " href="https://example.com/uk/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" x-default " href="https://example.com/" /> Source: Google, Tell Google about localized versions of your page [ Myths vs Google ] Which international SEO beliefs are wrong? Common assumptions, checked against Google's own documentation. Myth "The HTML lang attribute tells Google what language a page is in." Google says Google uses the visible content of the page to decide its language. It doesn't use code-level language information such as lang attributes, or the URL. Source → Myth "Redirect visitors to their country version automatically, by IP." Google says Avoid automatic redirects between language versions. Googlebot usually crawls from the USA, so redirects can stop users and search engines from reaching every version. Source → Myth "Just set the target country in Search Console." Google says The International Targeting report is deprecated and country targeting is no longer supported. Google still uses hreflang. Source → Myth "Machine-translate every page; it's the fastest way to scale." Google says Its spam policies list automated transformations, including translating, that add little value as scaled content abuse. Translation needs real localization and review. Source → Myth "Same-language pages for different countries will be penalised as duplicates." Google says For similar same-language pages across regions, pick a preferred version and use rel=canonical and hreflang so the right URL is served. Translated pages are not duplicates. Source → [ What we do ] What does international SEO involve? Nine workstreams, from deciding which markets are worth entering to proving each one pays back. 01 · Markets Market prioritisation Demand, competition and fit per country, so you enter the markets worth entering first. 02 · Structure Architecture decision Country domains, subdomains or subdirectories, chosen and documented with the reasons. 03 · hreflang Implementation & QA Reciprocal annotations, valid codes and x-default, validated across every version. 04 · Research Native keyword research How each market actually searches, not a translation of your English keywords. 05 · Localization Native review Pages adapted for language, culture, units and currency, and reviewed by native speakers. 06 · Authority Local signals Mentions, links and listings that matter in each market, not only at home. 07 · Technical Per-locale technical SEO Sitemaps per locale, canonicals, crawlable language selectors and speed in each region. 08 · Measurement Country-level reporting Search Console and analytics split by market, tied to enquiries and revenue. 09 · AI search AI answers per market What AI tools say about you in each language, observed and reported, not assumed. [ Process ] How does an international SEO engagement run? Market by market, so each launch is proven before the next one starts. 01 Prioritise markets Score countries on demand, competition and readiness, and agree the order. 02 Decide the structure Choose the URL structure and write it down, with a redirect plan if anything moves. 03 Build & hreflang Set up the versions, hreflang and sitemaps, then validate every pair before launch. 04 Localize & publish Research and adapt content per market, with native review before anything goes live. 05 Measure per market Report each market separately, fix what's served wrongly, and roll out the next one. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Market priority model : which countries to enter, in which order, and why. Architecture decision record : the chosen structure, alternatives and trade-offs. hreflang map : every page and its alternates, validated for return links and codes. Native keyword research : per market and language, mapped to pages. Localization briefs : what to adapt beyond the words, for each market. Redirect & migration plan : for any URL that changes, tested before launch. Per-locale sitemaps : clean, canonical and in sync with hreflang. Country dashboards : impressions, clicks, enquiries and revenue by market. [ Measurement ] How do we measure international SEO? Market by market, against the baseline taken before launch. Visibility per market Impressions and clicks in each country's search results. Right version served Share of searchers landing on the version meant for their market. hreflang health Missing return links, invalid codes and orphaned versions over time. Indexed pages per locale Whether each version's important pages are actually in the index. Enquiries & revenue by market What each market brings in: the reason to be there. AI answers per language How AI tools describe and recommend you in each market. [ Straight answer ] Translation isn't localization, and hreflang doesn't steer AI. A translated page that ignores how a market searches, buys and speaks rarely ranks. We research and adapt each market properly, with native review. And while Google documents how it uses hreflang, no AI company documents how its assistant picks a country version, so we don't promise it. We implement what Google documents and check what AI tools actually answer in each market. [ Who it's for ] Who is international SEO for? Companies selling in more than one country or language (or planning to) who need each market to perform on its own. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences Country-specific product information kept separate where approvals and labels differ HCP and patient content localized with medical and regulatory review in each market hreflang only between pages that are true equivalents Explore → 02 Healthcare Services and locations presented in the languages patients use Medical translations reviewed by native clinical reviewers Local contact details and terms for each country Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Localized landing pages, pricing and currency for each market Docs and help-centre language versions paired correctly Market-specific comparison and alternatives content Explore → 04 E-commerce Country stores with the right currency, shipping and returns Products and variants mapped correctly across locales Filter and sort URLs controlled in every language version Explore → 05 Manufacturing Spec sheets and datasheets in each buyer’s language Distributor and regional sites structured without duplicate content Units, standards and certifications localized for each market Explore → 06 Technology New regions launched market by market, not all at once Developer docs localized where adoption justifies it Product names kept consistent across languages Explore → 07 Professional Services Office and jurisdiction pages that reflect local rules Practice-area content adapted to each market’s business context Partner and expert profiles in the relevant languages Explore → 08 Education Programme pages for international applicants in their language Entry requirements and visa information by country Multi-campus and partner sites paired with correct hreflang Explore → [ Related services ] What works with international SEO? Explore → Local Local SEO Visibility in map results and local searches for every location you serve. Explore → [ Questions ] About international SEO. What is international SEO? International SEO makes sure search engines show the right language and country version of a website to each market, and that each version can rank on its own. It covers site structure, hreflang, localized content and keyword research per market, local authority, and reporting country by country. Should we use country domains, subdomains or subdirectories? Google compares the options: country-code domains send the clearest country signal but cost more to run; subdomains are easy to separate; subdirectories on one domain are the lowest maintenance; URL parameters are not recommended. For most B2B companies we recommend subdirectories on one strong domain, unless a legal, brand or market reason points to country domains. What does hreflang do? hreflang tells Google which pages are language or regional versions of each other, so searchers are shown the right one. Every version must list itself and all the others, using ISO language and region codes, and an x-default version can act as the fallback when no other version matches. Should we redirect visitors to their country version automatically? Google advises against automatically redirecting users to a different language version based on what you think their language is. Googlebot usually crawls from the USA, so automatic redirects can stop it (and users) from reaching every version. A visible language or country selector is the safer choice. Can we use machine translation? As a starting point, yes, but not as the finished page. Google’s spam policies list automated translation that adds little value, produced at scale, as scaled content abuse. We use translation tools for drafts and have native speakers review, adapt and localize every page that matters. Does hreflang control which version ChatGPT or Perplexity shows? copy_text: Home Services LLM Optimization [ Services / LLM Optimization ] LLM optimization services. Make AI describe your brand correctly. LLM Optimization shapes how large language models (the AI behind ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity) understand, describe and recommend your brand. Reinforce Lab's LLM optimization services make your brand facts consistent everywhere models learn from and look things up, then test what the models actually say. Get your free diagnostic → AI crawler guide Entity alignment Sources → model Six sources that describe your brand (website, schema, profiles, directories, reviews and press) move from inconsistent to consistent and connect to one brand entity, so the AI model describes the brand consistently, correctly and currently. WEBSITE ≠ = SCHEMA ≠ = PROFILES ≠ = DIRECTORIES ≠ = REVIEWS ≠ = PRESS ≠ = YOUR BRAND ONE ENTITY MODEL ANSWER "WHO IS YOUR BRAND?" CONSISTENT · CORRECT · CURRENT CONSISTENT · CORRECT · CURRENT [ How AI knows you ] How does an AI model know about your brand? There are two routes, and they need different fixes. The AI companies document both. Route 01 · Memory What it learned in training Models are trained on data up to a cut-off date. OpenAI's own help pages say its models "do not incorporate information about events beyond that, unless tools are used." Whatever the web said about you before that date is baked in. Fix Consistent, accurate facts about you across the web, so the next training round learns the right story. Route 02 · Lookup What it looks up live With search switched on, tools such as ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Gemini with Google Search grounding fetch current pages and cite them. Google says grounding lets Gemini cite "verifiable sources beyond its knowledge cutoff." Fix Clear, current, crawlable pages that state your facts plainly, and a crawler policy that lets search bots in. [ AI crawler guide ] Which AI crawlers should you allow? Not all AI crawlers do the same job. Some collect training data, some power AI search, and some fetch a page only when a person asks. Blocking the wrong one can remove you from AI answers. Company User agent Used for What the company says OpenAI GPTBot Training Collects content that may be used to train OpenAI’s models. Source OpenAI OAI-SearchBot AI search Surfaces sites in ChatGPT search. Sites that opt out are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. Source OpenAI ChatGPT-User User request Visits a page when a user’s question needs it; not an automatic web crawler. Source Anthropic ClaudeBot Training Collects web content that could contribute to training Claude models. Source Anthropic Claude-SearchBot AI search Crawls to improve the quality of Claude’s search results. Source Anthropic Claude-User User request Fetches pages when a user asks Claude a question. Source Perplexity PerplexityBot AI search Surfaces and links sites in Perplexity results; not used to train foundation models. Source Perplexity Perplexity-User User request Visits a page to answer a user’s question; not used for training. Source Google Google-Extended Training & grounding A control token for use in Gemini training and grounding. It does not affect inclusion or ranking in Google Search. Source Summarised from each company's own crawler documentation, checked 29 September 2026. Crawler names and rules change; we re-check them for every client. Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode use pages indexed for Google Search; Google-Extended does not control that. [ The problem ] Why do AI models get brands wrong? Models repeat what the web tells them. When the web is unclear, the answer is too. 01 · Inconsistency Different stories in different places Your site, profiles and directories describe you in different words, or list different services. 02 · Outdated facts Old information still online Past services, old prices or former addresses keep being repeated long after they changed. 03 · Name confusion Someone else shares your name Similar brand names get merged, and their facts end up in your description. 04 · No source of truth Nothing clearly states the facts Without a clear About page and structured data, models have to guess who you are and what you do. 05 · Thin coverage Few independent mentions When trusted third parties rarely mention you, models know little, or lean on competitors. 06 · Blocked access The wrong crawlers blocked A blanket block on "AI bots" can shut out the search crawlers that would have cited your current facts. [ Process ] How does LLM Optimization work? Five steps, starting with what the models say about you today. 01 Entity baseline Ask each model the questions buyers ask (who you are, what you do, how you compare) and record every answer. 02 Trace the errors For each wrong or missing fact, find the pages and profiles it most likely comes from. 03 Set the source of truth One clear description, a facts-rich About page, and Organization schema that links your official profiles. 04 Align the web Update profiles, directories and listings to match, correct outdated pages, and agree your AI-crawler policy. 05 Re-test & monitor Ask the same questions again on a schedule, and catch new errors before buyers do. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Model description report : how each AI model describes you today, answer by answer. Error log : every wrong, outdated or missing fact, with its likely source. Brand fact sheet : the agreed name, description, services and key facts, in one place. About page & schema : a facts-first About page and Organization markup linking your official profiles. Profile alignment : the profiles and listings to update, with the exact wording. AI-crawler policy : which crawlers to allow or block, set in your robots rules. llms.txt : an optional map of your key pages for AI agents. Re-test reports : what changed in each model's answers since the baseline. [ Measurement ] How do we measure LLM Optimization? By what the models say, on a fixed set of questions, over time. Description accuracy Share of answers that describe you correctly. Consistency across models Whether different AI tools tell the same, correct story. Entity recognition Whether models know you exist, and put you in the right category. Recommendation presence How often you are suggested for the needs you serve. Errors resolved Wrong facts traced, corrected at the source and no longer repeated. [ Straight answer ] Nobody can edit an AI model for you. No agency can change what a model learned or make it say something. What we can do is fix what models read: your own pages, your profiles and the sources that describe you, and keep the crawlers that fetch fresh facts able to reach you. AI tools that search the web pick those fixes up first; trained memory follows as models are retrained. [ Who it's for ] Who is LLM Optimization for? Brands that AI tools describe wrongly, vaguely or not at all, and teams in regulated fields, where a wrong description is a real risk. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences One consistent company, product and pipeline description across sites and registries Outdated or wrong product facts traced and corrected at the source Brand, generic and company names kept distinct to avoid confusion Explore → 02 Healthcare Practice, practitioner and location facts consistent across directories Wrong descriptions of services or specialisms traced and fixed at the source Organization and person markup linking official profiles Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Category and positioning stated identically on your site, review sites and profiles Old pricing, features and product names cleaned up across the web Clear separation from similarly named products Explore → 04 E-commerce Brand, product-line and retailer facts consistent across marketplaces and listings Outdated product information retired at the source Brand and reseller names made unambiguous Explore → 05 Manufacturing Company, plant, certification and capability facts aligned across directories Legacy brand and acquisition names mapped to the current company Product and part names kept consistent so models match them correctly Explore → 06 Technology Consistent descriptions of products, integrations and category Rebrands and renamed products connected so models don’t mix them up Founder, company and product clearly linked Explore → 07 Professional Services Firm, partner and practice-area facts consistent everywhere Mergers and name changes reflected across profiles and directories Named experts linked to the firm so models credit the right people Explore → 08 Education Institution, campus and programme names consistent across listings Discontinued courses and outdated facts removed at the source Accreditation and affiliations stated clearly so models describe you correctly Explore → [ Related services ] What works with LLM Optimization? LLM Optimization fixes the entity. These services make sure the pages and the program behind it are just as strong. Together they form an AI Growth System . The umbrella AI Search Optimization The full program for being visible, accurately described and recommended across AI search. Explore → Foundation Technical SEO Makes sure search engines and AI crawlers can reach and read every page that matters. Explore → Content SEO Content Systems Research-led, evidence-checked content produced as a system. Explore → Starting point SEO & AI Search Audit A full review of your Google and AI-search performance with a prioritised fix list. Explore → Always on AEO/GEO Optimization Agent The Search Authority OS agent that tracks where you appear in AI answers and strengthens entity signals. Explore → [ Questions ] About LLM Optimization. What is LLM Optimization? LLM Optimization is the work of shaping how large language models (the AI behind tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity) understand, describe and recommend a brand. It makes the facts about a brand consistent and easy to find everywhere models learn from and look things up, then checks what the models actually say. How is LLM Optimization different from GEO and AI Search Optimization? AI Search Optimization is the full program for being visible in AI search. GEO works on pages and passages so they get cited in answers. LLM Optimization works on the brand itself as an entity: who you are, what you do and who you serve, stated the same way everywhere, so models describe you correctly even when no page is cited. Can you fix wrong information ChatGPT or another AI says about us? Not by editing the model; no one outside the AI company can do that. We find where the wrong information comes from, correct it at the source, publish clear and current facts on your own site, and re-test. Tools that search the web can pick up corrections quickly; what a model learned in training changes only when it is retrained. Should we block AI crawlers? It depends on the crawler. Some collect data for training models, others fetch pages for AI search answers. OpenAI, for example, says sites that opt out of its search crawler will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, while its separate training crawler can be blocked without that effect. We help you set a policy per crawler, based on what you want. What is llms.txt, and do we need one? llms.txt is a proposal, published by Jeremy Howard in September 2024, for a plain-text file at a site’s root that points AI agents to a site’s most useful pages. It is not an official standard and no major AI company has said it relies on it, so we treat it as a low-cost extra, not a ranking factor. How long does LLM Optimization take? Corrections on your own site and profiles can be picked up quickly by AI tools that search the web. Changes to what a model learned during training take longer, because they depend on the next training cycle. We baseline how each model describes you first, then report changes against that baseline. What is LLM SEO? LLM SEO is another name for LLM optimization: the work of making large language models describe and recommend your brand accurately. Some agencies sell it as LLM SEO services. It builds on ordinary SEO, because the models learn from and search the same web pages, profiles and mentions that search engines use. How much do LLM optimization services cost? It depends on how many models and prompts are tracked and how much of your brand information needs correcting across the web. copy_text: Home Services Lead Generation Systems [ Services / Lead Generation ] B2B lead generation services. Turn demand into qualified pipeline, not form fills. Lead generation systems connect every step between a buyer's first search and a closed deal: the channels that attract them, the landing pages and forms that convert them, the qualification and routing that get the right leads to sales fast, and the closed-loop data that tells your ads which leads became revenue. Reinforce Lab's B2B lead generation services build and run the whole system, including PPC and Google Ads. Get your free diagnostic → PPC management Lead generation Attract · convert · qualify · close the loop Search, paid ads, content and referrals send visitors to a landing page and form; qualified leads go to sales and the rest to nurture; closed deals are fed back as conversion data to improve ad bidding. CHANNELS SEARCH PAID ADS CONTENT REFERRALS LANDING PAGE FORM FIT? YES NOT YET SALES CLOSED DEAL NURTURE CONVERSION DATA → AD BIDDING PAID ADS ATTRACT ATTRACT CONVERT CONVERT QUALIFY QUALIFY CLOSE THE LOOP CLOSE THE LOOP [ The system ] What is a lead generation system? Six parts that most businesses run separately, and lose leads between. We run them as one. 01 · Attract Channels Organic search, paid search, content and referrals, each chosen for where your buyers actually look. 02 · Convert Landing pages & CRO A page for each offer and audience, tested and improved on what converts to pipeline. 03 · Capture Forms & data Forms that ask only what sales needs, with consent recorded and sources captured. 04 · Qualify Qualification & routing Fit and intent checked, then leads routed to the right person, or to nurture. 05 · Handoff CRM & speed to lead Every lead in the CRM with its source, and sales alerted while the lead is warm. 06 · Close the loop Revenue feedback CRM outcomes fed back to your ad platforms and reports, so budget follows revenue. [ How B2B buyers buy ] How do B2B buyers want to be found? Mostly on their own terms. Gartner's survey of 632 B2B buyers shows why lead generation has to earn attention, not chase it. 61% Prefer self-service of B2B buyers prefer an overall rep-free buying experience. 73% Avoid irrelevant outreach actively avoid suppliers who send them irrelevant outreach. 69% Notice mixed messages report inconsistencies between a supplier's website and what its sellers say. Pages Landing pages Pages that match the ad and the search, one of the three signals Google uses to judge ad quality. Bidding Bidding on value Conversion values and CRM outcomes that teach bidding which leads matter. Tracking Tracking & consent Conversion tracking, enhanced conversions and Consent Mode set up correctly. [ Myths ] Which PPC habits cost you money? Four common habits, and what Google's own documentation says. Myth "Push Quality Score up and costs will fall." Google says Quality Score is a diagnostic tool, "not a key performance indicator", and "not an input in the ad auction". Source → Myth "The landing page is the website team's problem." Google says Landing page experience (how relevant and useful the page is) is one of the three components of Quality Score, alongside expected CTR and ad relevance. Source → Myth "A form fill is a conversion." Google says An ad often starts a path that ends in a sale offline. Importing offline conversions lets you measure what happens after the click or call. Source → Myth "Consent is just a cookie-banner job." Google says For users in the EEA, the ad_user_data consent type is required for measurement uses such as enhanced conversions and tag-based conversion tracking. Everything else depends on it. 01 Audit Channels, tracking, forms, CRM and where leads are lost today. 02 Define Ideal customer, offers, and what counts as a qualified lead, agreed with sales. 03 Build Tracking, landing pages, forms, routing and campaigns. 04 Launch Channels switched on in stages, with budgets capped until data arrives. 05 Optimise Budget moved weekly towards what creates qualified pipeline. Tracking plan : conversions, sources, consent and CRM fields. Landing pages & forms : built, tested and improved. Campaigns : PPC and other channels, set up and managed. Routing & alerts : the right lead to the right person, fast. Closed-loop setup : CRM outcomes fed back to ads and reports. Monthly report : cost per qualified lead, pipeline and revenue by channel. [ Measurement ] How do we measure lead generation? By what reaches sales and closes, not by the number of forms filled in. Qualified leads Leads that meet the definition you agreed with sales. Cost per qualified lead Spend divided by qualified leads, by channel and campaign. Lead-to-opportunity rate How many leads sales accepts and turns into opportunities. Speed to lead Time from enquiry to first contact. Pipeline & revenue Opportunities and revenue by source, from your CRM. Customer acquisition cost What it costs to win a customer, channel by channel. [ Straight answer ] Cheap leads are expensive. It is easy to lower cost per lead: loosen the targeting, shorten the form, offer something free. Sales then spends its week on people who were never going to buy. We optimise for qualified pipeline instead, which sometimes means fewer leads, a longer form and a higher cost per lead that is worth far more. [ Who it's for ] Who are lead generation systems for? A lead generation system connects every step between a buyer’s first search and a closed deal: the channels that attract them, the landing pages and forms that convert them, the qualification and routing that get the right leads to sales quickly, and the closed-loop data that shows which campaigns created revenue, so budget moves to what works. We structure campaigns, manage keywords and negatives, write and test ads, build the landing pages, set up conversion tracking and bid on the value of leads, using what happens in your CRM after the form fill. What is closed-loop reporting? Closed-loop reporting connects a lead’s source to what happened next in your CRM: qualified, opportunity, won or lost. Google Ads can import these offline conversions, so bidding learns which searches produce customers rather than just enquiries. Should we chase a better Quality Score? Not directly. Google describes Quality Score as a diagnostic tool, not a key performance indicator, and says it is not an input in the ad auction. Its three components (expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience) are useful clues about what to improve. Do we need Consent Mode? If you advertise to users in the European Economic Area and use Google’s measurement or personalisation features, Google requires consent signals to be collected and passed on. Consent Mode’s ad_user_data setting is required for measurement uses such as enhanced conversions. We set this up with your consent platform. How is lead generation priced? copy_text: Home Services Executive AI Consulting [ Services / Executive AI Consulting ] AI consulting services for executives. An AI strategy your board can act on. Executive AI consulting helps leadership teams decide where AI should (and shouldn't) go in their business: which use cases are worth funding, what data and governance they need, which regulations apply, and how the return will be measured. Date What applies What it means for you 1 Aug 2024 The AI Act enters into force The clock starts on every later deadline. 2 Feb 2025 Definitions, AI literacy and prohibited practices Banned practices must stop; organisations must act on AI literacy for staff using AI. 2 Aug 2025 Rules for general-purpose AI models; governance in place Mainly model providers, but it shapes the tools you buy. 27 Jul 2026 Digital Omnibus on AI amends the Act AI-literacy duty becomes: take measures to support it, no guaranteed individual level; some deadlines move. 2 Aug 2026 Most rules apply, including transparency (Article 50); enforcement starts Tell people when they're talking to a chatbot or seeing AI-generated content. 2 Dec 2027 Rules for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III Uses such as CV screening need risk management, documentation and human oversight. Get your free diagnostic → Listing rules Local search Relevance · distance · prominence A nearby customer searches; Google weighs relevance, distance and prominence; your business appears in the local results with a complete profile, genuine reviews and consistent citations. ACCOUNTANT NEAR ME LOCAL RESULTS COMPETITOR YOUR BUSINESS COMPETITOR YOUR BUSINESS + PROFILE + REVIEWS + CITATIONS RELEVANCE RELEVANCE DISTANCE DISTANCE PROMINENCE PROMINENCE GOOGLE’S THREE LOCAL FACTORS: RELEVANCE · DISTANCE · PROMINENCE [ How local ranking works ] How does Google rank local results? Google names three things. Two of them you can improve. One you can't, and anyone promising otherwise is guessing. 01 · Relevance Does your listing match the search? How well your profile and pages match what someone is looking for. We improve Categories, services, descriptions and location pages that say exactly what you do. 02 · Distance How far away are you? How close your business is to the searcher, or to the place they searched for. We can't change Your location, so we make sure every real location and service area is listed correctly. 03 · Prominence How well known are you? How recognised your business is, online and off, including links, articles and reviews. We improve Reviews, consistent citations, local links and mentions. [ Rules that protect your listing ] Which local SEO tactics break the rules? Some common tactics can get a profile suspended or break consumer law. Here is what Google and the FTC actually say. Myth "Add city and service keywords to your business name." Google says Your name should reflect your real-world business name. Adding unnecessary information isn't permitted and could result in suspension of your profile. Source → Myth "Offer a discount in exchange for a review." Google says Incentives for posting, changing or removing reviews are strictly prohibited. The US FTC's final rule (August 2024) also bans buying or selling fake reviews. Source → Myth "Only ask your happiest customers for reviews." Google says Businesses may not discourage negative reviews or selectively ask for positive ones. Source → Myth "Get a virtual office in every city you want to rank in." Google says You can't list a virtual office unless it is staffed during business hours. Service-area businesses get one profile with the areas they serve. Source → Myth "You can pay Google to rank higher on the map." Google says There's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. (Ads are separate and labelled as ads.) Source → FTC: Final rule banning fake reviews and testimonials , 14 August 2024 [ Process ] How does a local SEO engagement run? Foundations first, then the work that builds on them. 01 Local audit Profiles, citations, reviews, location pages and competitors, mapped across your service area. 02 Fix the foundations Claim and correct Google, Apple and Bing listings, and clean up inconsistent details. 03 Pages & schema Build useful location and service-area pages with matching structured data. 04 Reviews & authority Start a compliant review program and earn local links and mentions. 05 Measure & expand Track visibility and leads per location, then roll out to the next area. By what local visibility turns into, not by a single ranking check from one spot. Map visibility across your area Where you appear in local results across a grid of points around your area. Profile actions Calls, direction requests and website clicks from your profiles. Reviews Volume, rating and reply rate over time, per location. Citation accuracy Share of listings with correct, consistent business details. Location-page leads Enquiries and conversions from each location page. AI local answers Whether AI tools name you, and with correct details, for local prompts. [ Straight answer ] Distance is the one thing no one can change. Someone searching three streets from a competitor will often see that competitor first, whatever anyone promises. We work on what can move: how relevant and how well known you are, the accuracy of every listing, and the quality of your location pages. And we never use tactics that put your profile at risk. [ Who it's for ] Who is local SEO for? Businesses with real locations or service areas (offices, clinics, stores, plants or field teams) whose customers search nearby. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences Offices, sites and facilities listed accurately on every map Clinical-trial site and location pages kept compliant and current Company details consistent across medical and industry directories Explore → 02 Healthcare Practice and practitioner profiles set up within Google’s rules Review requests that respect patient privacy Location pages with services, hours and accessibility details Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Regional offices and city pages for teams that sell locally Company details consistent across software directories and maps Local partner, event and community mentions Explore → 04 E-commerce Store locator and store pages for every physical location Hours, stock and collection details consistent across maps Store-level reviews managed location by location Explore → 05 Manufacturing Plants, depots and showrooms listed accurately on every map Service-area profiles for field engineers and installers Consistent listings in industrial directories and trade associations Explore → 06 Technology Office and support-centre listings consistent across maps Service-area pages for on-site IT and installation work Local partner and reseller listings aligned with yours Explore → 07 Professional Services A profile for each real office: no virtual-office risk Practice-area pages for each city you serve Client reviews gathered within Google’s rules Explore → 08 Education Campus and admissions-office listings on Google, Apple and Bing Campus pages with directions, open days and contacts Consistent campus and department names across directories Explore → [ Related services ] What works with local SEO? Local SEO (local search engine optimization) makes a business visible when people nearby search for what it offers: in Google’s local results and Maps, on Apple Maps and Bing, and in AI answers. It covers the Google Business Profile and other map listings, consistent business details across directories, reviews, location and service-area pages, local structured data and local links. How does Google rank local results? Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and prominence: how well a profile matches the search, how far the business is from the searcher, and how well known it is, including links and reviews. Google also says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Can we add keywords to our Google Business Profile name? No. Google’s guidelines say the name should reflect your real-world business name, as used on signage and stationery, and that adding unnecessary information to it is not permitted and can lead to the profile being suspended. How should we get more reviews? Ask every customer, not only the happy ones, and make it easy for them. Google prohibits offering incentives for reviews and selectively asking for positive ones, and the US FTC’s rule on fake reviews, announced in August 2024, bans buying or selling fake reviews. Replying to reviews shows customers you value their feedback. We don’t have a shopfront. Can we still do local SEO? Yes. Google treats you as a service-area business: one profile for your central office with the areas you serve, and your address hidden from customers. You can’t list virtual offices unless they are staffed during business hours, so we build visibility through service-area pages, not fake locations. Does local SEO help in AI search? It can. OpenAI says ChatGPT search can use your location and sometimes works with other search providers for local results, and Google offers Gemini grounding with Google Maps data. Accurate, consistent listings and clear location pages give these tools correct facts to use, though no one controls what an AI answers. How much do local SEO services cost? copy_text: Home Services Digital PR & Link Building [ Services / Digital PR ] Digital PR services. Earn coverage and links that build authority. Digital PR is off-page SEO done in the open. Reinforce Lab's digital PR services build stories from original data and expert insight, pitch them to the journalists who cover your field, and earn the coverage, links and mentions that build your authority in Google and AI search, with no bought links and no keyword-stuffed press releases. Get your free diagnostic → Link rules Digital PR Story · coverage · links · citations An original-data story is pitched to news, trade and industry outlets; coverage links back to your site and AI answers cite your brand, so authority builds without bought links. ORIGINAL DATA NEWS SITE LINK → YOUR SITE TRADE PRESS LINK → YOUR SITE INDUSTRY BLOG LINK → YOUR SITE AI ANSWER CITED: YOUR BRAND YOUR SITE AUTHORITY PITCH PITCH COVERAGE COVERAGE LINKS LINKS CITATIONS CITATIONS [ Off-page SEO ] What is off-page SEO, and where does link building fit? Off-page SEO is what other sites say about you. Links are part of it; so are coverage, mentions and citations in AI answers. 01 · Links How Google finds and judges you Google uses links to discover pages and as a signal of how relevant they are. We earn Editorial links from relevant publications to the pages that matter commercially. 02 · Coverage Who is talking about you Coverage in the publications your buyers read builds trust (and branded search) with or without a link. We earn Features, quotes and mentions in news, trade and industry media. 03 · Citations What AI answers say AI search tools lean on independent sources. Brands that trusted publications cover are easier to cite. We track Whether AI answers mention and cite you, alongside links. Source: Google, Link best practices · SEO Starter Guide [ What journalists want ] What makes journalists cover a story? Relevance, first and by a distance. Cision's 2026 survey of 1,899 journalists in 19 markets is the brief we work to. 79% Relevance wins are most likely to engage with a pitch relevant to their beat, audience or coverage area. 82% Irrelevance loses reject a pitch that isn't relevant to their audience or coverage, the top reason for deleting one. 47% Data is in demand want PR teams to send them more data or research, the most-requested resource. 66% PR feeds the news rely on PR-provided content (press releases, pitches, media kits) for story ideas. 53% No sales pitches reject pitches that are too promotional or sales-focused. 97% Email, short, once prefer pitches by email; 64% say follow up once, and no more. Source: Cision, 2026 State of the Media Report (survey January to February 2026) [ What we do ] What does our digital PR and link building cover? Nine ways to earn links and coverage, each chosen for your pages, your market and your budget. 01 · Data Original data studies Surveys, analysis of your own data and public datasets, turned into findings journalists can report. 02 · Reactive Expert commentary Your experts offered to journalists on breaking news in your field, often the same day. 03 · News Press releases done right Releases for real news, written for journalists, never as a vehicle for keyword links. 04 · Assets Linkable resources Tools, guides, indexes and visual data that people cite and link to over time. 05 · Product Product & brand stories Launches, milestones and behind-the-scenes angles pitched to the right beats. 06 · Reclaim Link reclamation Unlinked brand mentions and broken links to your site turned back into working links. 07 · Partners Partner & industry links Associations, suppliers, events and partners, where a link reflects a real relationship. 08 · Targets Links to the right pages Campaigns planned around the service, product and category pages you need to rank. 09 · AI search Citations in AI answers Coverage in the sources AI search tools draw on, tracked for mentions and citations. [ Link rules ] Which link building tactics break Google's rules? Cheap link building usually means one of these. Here is what Google actually says. Myth "Buy links in bulk; it's cheaper per link." Google says Buying or selling links for ranking purposes is link spam: "creating links to or from a site primarily for the purpose of manipulating search rankings." Source → Myth "Paid placements have to be hidden." Google says Paying for advertising and sponsorship is normal. It isn't a violation when the links are qualified with rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow". Source → Myth "Put your keywords in the press release links." Google says Links with optimised anchor text in articles, guest posts or press releases distributed on other sites are listed as link spam. Source → Myth "Run a guest-posting campaign at scale." Google says Large-scale article marketing or guest-posting campaigns with keyword-rich anchor text links are listed as link spam. Source → Myth "Anchor text should be your exact keyword." Google says Good anchor text is descriptive, reasonably concise and relevant, written naturally, without keyword stuffing. Source → Source: Google, Spam policies for Google web search [ Process ] How does a digital PR campaign run? From the pages you need to rank to the journalists who can help them. 01 Discover Target pages, competitors' links and coverage, and the beats of the journalists who matter. 02 Develop The story and the data behind it, fact-checked, then approved by you. 03 Pitch Short, beat-specific emails to a researched list, with one follow-up. 04 Verify Every piece of coverage logged, with its link, target page and link attribute checked. 05 Report & reuse What landed, what it changed, and the next angle from what journalists responded to. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Link & coverage audit : your links and mentions against competitors', by target page. Campaign plan : story angles, target pages and target outlets. Research & data asset : the findings, charts and methodology journalists need. Press materials : release, pitches, expert quotes and visuals. Media list : journalists and outlets chosen by beat and audience. Outreach : personalised pitching and follow-up. Coverage log : every placement with link status, attribute and target page. Monthly report : coverage, links, referral traffic, rankings and AI citations. [ Measurement ] How do we measure digital PR? By relevance and results, not by a raw count of links. Relevant coverage Pieces in publications your buyers actually read, by outlet and topic. Referring domains New, relevant sites linking to you, and the share that are editorial. Links to target pages Links reaching the pages you need to rank, beyond the home page. Referral traffic & leads Visits and conversions from coverage. Rankings & brand search Movement for target pages and growth in searches for your name. AI citations Whether AI answers mention and cite you, and which sources they use. [ Straight answer ] Nobody honest can guarantee coverage. Journalists decide what they write and what they link to. An agency that guarantees a number of links is either guessing or paying for placements, and paid links that pass ranking credit are exactly what Google's spam policies target. We guarantee the work: a story worth covering, pitched to the right people, with every result reported. [ Who it's for ] Who is digital PR for? Brands with expertise or data worth sharing, in markets where authority decides who ranks and who gets cited. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences Research and disease-area data stories for trade and health media Expert commentary reviewed by medical and legal teams Congress, trial and launch news pitched to specialist press Explore → 02 Healthcare Clinician experts offered for health and local news Patient-safe data stories from anonymised, aggregate insight Coverage that builds trust signals for health searches Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Original product-usage and industry data reports Founder and expert commentary for tech and trade press Links to product, integration and comparison pages Explore → 04 E-commerce Product and trend stories for consumer and lifestyle media Seasonal data campaigns timed to buying peaks Links earned to category and product pages Explore → 05 Manufacturing Trade-press coverage for innovations, plants and contracts Engineering experts for industry features Industry-body and supplier links, not bought placements Explore → 06 Technology Research reports and benchmarks journalists can cite Reactive expert comment on breaking tech news Coverage in the publications buyers actually read Explore → 07 Professional Services Thought leadership turned into quotable data Partners and experts placed in business and trade media Reactive comment on regulation, tax and market news Explore → 08 Education Faculty experts offered for news and features Research findings pitched to education and national press Links to course, research and department pages Explore → [ Related services ] What works with digital PR? Coverage builds authority. These services make sure it lands on pages that can rank and get cited. Together they form an AI Growth System . Scale Enterprise SEO Strategy One SEO standard across teams, templates, releases and markets. Explore → AI search AI Search Optimization Visibility and accurate recommendations across AI search. Explore → Citations GEO Content structured so AI engines can quote and cite it. Explore → Entity level LLM Optimization One consistent description of your brand across the sources AI models learn from. Explore → Content SEO Content Systems The pages your coverage links to, produced as a system. Explore → Starting point SEO & AI Search Audit A full review of your Google and AI-search performance, including authority. Explore → [ Questions ] About digital PR and link building. What is digital PR? Digital PR is earning coverage, links and mentions from online publications by giving journalists something worth reporting: original data, expert commentary, useful resources or genuine news. For SEO, it is the safest way to build links, because each one is an editorial choice by the publication rather than a placement someone paid for. What is off-page SEO? Off-page SEO is everything outside your own website that affects how search engines and AI tools judge it: mainly links from other sites, mentions of your brand, coverage in the press and citations in AI answers. Google uses links to find pages and to judge how relevant they are. Is affordable link building safe? Cheap links are usually sold per link, as placements that pass ranking credit, and Google lists buying or selling links for ranking purposes as link spam. Paid placements are fine for exposure if they are qualified with rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow". On a smaller budget we focus on link reclamation, partner links and expert commentary, which cost less and carry no policy risk. Do you guarantee a number of links? No. Journalists and editors decide what they cover and link to, so any guaranteed link count is either a guess or a paid placement. We agree targets for relevant outlets and pages, report every piece of coverage and its link status, and adjust the campaign on what journalists respond to. Do press releases help SEO? A press release helps when it carries real news that journalists pick up and write about. Links inside distributed releases should not pass ranking credit. Google lists optimised anchor-text links in press releases distributed on other sites as link spam. We write releases for journalists, not for links. How long does a digital PR campaign take? A data-led campaign usually needs several weeks of research, writing and approval before outreach begins; reactive commentary can go out the same day. Coverage arrives after launch, and its effect on rankings builds over months rather than days. How much do digital PR services cost? It depends on whether you need one data-led campaign, ongoing reactive commentary or both, and on how much original research each story needs. After a first conversation you get a written scope and price. We do not price by the link, because earned coverage cannot be promised in advance. How do I choose a digital PR agency? Ask to see the stories, not only the link counts. A good digital PR agency builds campaigns on real data or expertise, pitches journalists who cover your field, never buys links, and reports coverage, links and mentions honestly, including the campaigns that did not land. Be careful with off-page SEO services or link building services that promise a fixed number of links: buying links breaks Google’s spam policies. copy_text: Home Services Search Engine Optimization [ Services / SEO ] Search engine optimization services. SEO services that build lasting authority. Search engine optimization (SEO) services help search engines find, understand and trust your website, so the right customers reach you from Google and from AI answers. Reinforce Lab runs all four pillars (technical SEO, on-page SEO, content and authority) as one system, built to Google's own guidelines and measured in leads and revenue, not rankings alone. [ How search works ] How does Google decide what to show? Google works in three stages, and not every page makes it through each one. SEO makes sure yours does. 01 · Crawling Can Google find the page? Google discovers pages mainly through links and sitemaps, then downloads and renders them. We make sure Important pages are linked, reachable and rendered, and junk URLs don't waste the crawl. 02 · Indexing Does Google understand it? Google analyses the content, picks a canonical version from duplicates, and decides whether to store it. Indexing isn't guaranteed. We make sure Each page is unique, clearly canonical and worth indexing. 03 · Serving Is it the best answer? For each search, Google returns what it judges most relevant and highest quality, using hundreds of factors. We make sure The page answers the search better than the alternatives, and is trusted. "Google doesn't accept payment to crawl a site more frequently, or rank it higher. If anyone tells you otherwise, they're wrong." Google Search Central Source: Google, In-depth guide to how Google Search works [ On-page SEO ] What is on-page SEO? On-page SEO is everything on the page itself that helps search engines and people understand it. These are the elements we optimise on every page we touch. Titles Title links A title unique to the page, clear and concise, that accurately describes its content. Snippets Meta descriptions A short, relevant summary that helps people decide to click from the results. Structure Headings & readability Well-organised, easy-to-read content broken into sections with helpful headings. Language How people search The words your customers actually use (beginners and experts alike), written naturally, never stuffed. Links Internal links & anchor text Descriptive links that connect related pages and tell search engines what each one covers. Schema URLs & structured data Descriptive URLs and structured data that match what the page shows. Source: Google, SEO Starter Guide [ Myths ] Which SEO beliefs can you stop worrying about? Google's own starter guide lists things it believes you shouldn't focus on. Here are five we still hear every week. Myth "You need the meta keywords tag." Google says Google Search doesn't use the keywords meta tag. Source → Myth "Pages need at least 2,000 words to rank." Google says Content length alone doesn't matter for ranking; there's no magical word count target. Source → Myth "E-E-A-T is a ranking factor you can score." Google says E-E-A-T isn't a ranking factor. Showing real experience and expertise still helps people trust your content. Source → Myth "Duplicate content gets you penalised." Google says Duplicate content isn't a violation of its spam policies, but it can waste crawling and confuse users, so we still fix it. Source → Myth "This agency can guarantee you the #1 spot." Google says No one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google. Beware of anyone who claims to, or claims a "special relationship" with Google. Source → [ Method ] How does Reinforce Lab run an SEO programme? Nine stages, in order. Protecting what already ranks comes before building anything new. 01 · Discover Baseline Search Console, analytics, crawl and competitors: what ranks, what doesn't, and why. 02 · Preserve Protect what works Every URL with traffic, links or impressions is kept or redirected deliberately. 03 · Architect Site structure Pillars, supporting pages and internal links mapped to how customers search. 04 · Content Helpful pages People-first content that answers each search better than the alternatives. 05 · AI search Answer-ready Clear, citable answers and consistent entity facts for AI search. 06 · Build Implement Technical fixes, templates, schema and pages built to one standard. 07 · QA Check before launch Indexing, redirects, schema, speed and mobile checked page by page. 08 · Launch Release safely Changes shipped in steps, not in one risky batch. 09 · Monitor Measure & iterate Rankings, traffic, leads and AI visibility tracked, then the next priority. [ B2B SEO ] How is B2B SEO different? Fewer searches, bigger deals, longer decisions. B2B SEO is judged by pipeline, not traffic. Buying groups Several people decide Content for each role in the decision: the user, the budget holder and the technical evaluator. Intent Low volume, high value Searches with a few dozen impressions can be worth more than thousands of casual visits. Pipeline Measured in revenue Organic leads followed into your CRM, so SEO is judged by the deals it helps create. [ Consultant or agency ] Do you need an SEO consultant or an SEO agency? It depends on who will do the work. We work both ways. SEO consulting You have the team We set the strategy, standards and priorities, review what your team ships, and train them. Best when you have developers and writers who can implement. Managed SEO You need the work done We do the technical fixes, content and outreach, and report on results. Best when SEO has no owner in-house. "If you run a small local business, you can probably do much of the work yourself." Google, Do you need an SEO? [ Deliverables ] What you get. [ Why it matters ] Why does WordPress need regular maintenance? Because the risk is in the add-ons, and it moves fast. Patchstack's analysis of 2025 shows the scale. 11,334 New vulnerabilities found in the WordPress ecosystem in 2025, a 42% increase on 2024. 91% In plugins of them were in plugins and 9% in themes. Only six were in WordPress core. 5 hrs To mass exploitation the median time for heavily exploited vulnerabilities to be attacked at scale. "Fundamentally, security is not about perfectly secure systems… What security is though is risk reduction, not risk elimination." WordPress.org, Hardening WordPress Sources: Patchstack, State of WordPress Security in 2026 (updated 25 February 2026) · WordPress.org, Hardening WordPress [ Schedule ] What happens every day, week and month? A fixed routine, so nothing depends on someone remembering. How often What we do Why it matters Continuously Uptime monitoring, vulnerability alerts and protection rules Problems are caught before your customers find them. Quarterly User and access review, plugin audit Old accounts and unused plugins are removed before they become a risk. [ Myths ] Is it enough to turn on automatic updates? Four assumptions that leave WordPress sites exposed, and what the evidence says. Myth "Automatic updates keep us safe." Patchstack found 46% of vulnerabilities had no fix from the developer by the time they were made public, so there was nothing to update to. Source → Myth "Our host takes care of security." The evidence WordPress.org notes hosts are responsible for the infrastructure, not the application you install. In Patchstack's test of hosting companies, only 26% of vulnerability attacks were blocked. Source → Myth "We have backups, so we're covered." WordPress.org says Verify the backups you created are there and usable: "This is essential." A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a plan. Source → Myth "Premium plugins are safer than free ones." Patchstack found Premium components had three times more known exploited vulnerabilities than free ones in 2025. Source → [ Process ] How does website maintenance start? An audit first, so we know exactly what we're looking after. 01 Onboard Access, a full backup and a record of how the site is set up. 02 Audit Updates, plugins, security, speed, SEO health and forms checked. 03 Stabilise Anything urgent fixed before the routine begins. 04 Maintain The daily, weekly and monthly schedule runs. 05 Report A monthly report on what was done, found and recommended. Website maintenance services keep a website secure, fast and working. They cover software updates for WordPress core, plugins and themes; off-site backups and restore tests; security and vulnerability monitoring; uptime monitoring; speed and Core Web Vitals; SEO health such as broken links, redirects and indexing errors; form and checkout testing; small content changes; and support when something goes wrong, with a monthly report. How often should a WordPress site be updated? Security fixes should be applied as soon as they are available and tested, because attackers move fast: Patchstack found that heavily exploited WordPress vulnerabilities reached mass exploitation in a median of 5 hours. Routine updates are best applied on a regular schedule, tested on a staging copy first so nothing breaks on the live site. Aren’t automatic updates enough? No. Updates only help once a fix exists, and Patchstack reports that 46% of WordPress vulnerabilities in 2025 had no fix from the developer by the time they were made public. Maintenance adds vulnerability monitoring, protection rules, tested backups and someone accountable when something breaks. Doesn’t our web host handle security? Only part of it. WordPress’s own hardening guide notes that hosts are responsible for the infrastructure, not the application you install on it: your plugins, themes and settings. In Patchstack’s large-scale test of hosting companies, only 26% of vulnerability attacks were blocked. Do you maintain websites you didn’t build? Yes. Every new site starts with an onboarding audit: we take a full backup, check updates, plugins, security, speed and SEO health, fix anything urgent, and then move the site onto the regular maintenance schedule. How much does website maintenance cost? It depends on the size and complexity of the site: a brochure site needs less than a busy online store with many plugins and integrations. After the onboarding audit you get a monthly plan with the scope written down. What is included in website maintenance packages? Website maintenance packages differ by site, but every plan from Reinforce Lab follows the same routine: uptime and security monitoring, daily off-site backups, weekly updates tested on a staging copy, a monthly speed and SEO health check, and a monthly report. The size and complexity of the site set the price. How do I choose a website maintenance company? Ask what happens when an update breaks something and how often backups are tested. A good website maintenance company tests updates on a copy of your site first, keeps backups off the server, restores one regularly to prove it works, and tells you each month what was done. For WordPress maintenance services, also ask who checks plugins for known vulnerabilities. [ Start here ] When was your website last backed up, and tested? Our flagship, Search Authority OS , runs search authority as one loop: research, verify, write, audit, monitor. See all services Search Authority OS Packages and pricing [ Who we work with ] Who is Reinforce Lab for? Growth-stage founders and B2B companies that need search to produce customers, not only traffic, and want less manual work behind it. Most fit one of three situations. 01 Search has stopped producing leads Traffic is falling, or the leads have dried up, and nobody can say why. 02 Missing from AI answers They rank on Google but not in ChatGPT, Perplexity or AI Overviews, or AI tools describe them wrongly. 03 Too much repetitive work Their team spends hours on marketing and reporting work that a system could do. In pharmaceuticals and healthcare a wrong claim can do harm, so evidence checking is built into how we write for every client: claims carry a source, conflicting sources are investigated, and anything unverified goes to a person before it is published. [ How we work ] How does an engagement with Reinforce Lab work? It starts with a diagnostic, not a proposal. 01 Diagnostic The free Search Authority Diagnostic sets your real baseline and shows what to fix first. 02 Scope and proposal A plan and price fitted to your goals. No template retainer. 03 Build and onboard The system is set up for your market, your buyers and your evidence sources. 04 Run and improve Work ships, performance is monitored, and the system is adjusted as results come in. There is no cart and no self-checkout: work at this level is scoped on a call after the diagnostic. The nine-stage method behind every project 01 Discover Audit what you have: search data, indexation, content and technical health. 02 Preserve Protect every page that already earns traffic, links or trust before anything changes. 03 Architect Design the site structure, URLs and internal links around how buyers search. 04 Content Plan and write evidence-led content for each stage of the buying journey. 05 AI search Make your facts clear and consistent for AI answers as well as blue links. 06 Build Build the pages, schema and automation to a written quality standard. 07 QA Check every page against that standard before it goes live. 08 Launch Go live with redirects mapped and tested, URL by URL. 09 Monitor Track visibility, leads and revenue, and fix what the data shows. [ Principles ] What do we stand for? Six rules we work by. 01 Evidence before claims We cite our sources and never invent metrics, rankings or results, for our clients or for ourselves. 02 Preserve what already works Pages that earn traffic, links or trust are protected before anything is redesigned, moved or merged. 03 One system, not separate tactics Website, content, search and automation are planned together so each one strengthens the others. 04 People review the AI AI speeds up the work; a person checks what it produces before anything is published or delivered. 05 Measured on business results We report enquiries, pipeline and revenue next to rankings and traffic. 06 You own the work Everything we produce for you is yours. Jamil Ahmed Founder and CEO, Reinforce Lab Education B.Pharm, East West University, Dhaka Pharma career From 2012: international business, Square Group, Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) Markets Sri Lanka, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritania, Puerto Rico, Cuba Today SEO and AI search consultant · Semrush Ambassador Jamil on LinkedIn → 2018 interview → From pharmaceutical marketing to AI Growth Systems Jamil Ahmed founded Reinforce Lab and leads it as CEO.
