title: How to Write SEO Friendly Blog Posts: 12 Steps
meta: How to write SEO friendly blog posts in 12 steps: topic, intent, title, original value, links and images, plus Ahrefs data, a checklist and a worked example.
h1_text: How to Write SEO Friendly Blog Posts: 12 Steps That Work
lede: Twelve steps to write SEO friendly blog posts, with data on why most pages get no search traffic, Google's guidance on titles, links and AI content, a pre-publish checklist and a worked example.
copy_text: Home Blog Content Marketing How to Write SEO Friendly Blog Posts: 12… Guide Content Marketing How to Write SEO Friendly Blog Posts: 12 Steps That Work Twelve steps to write SEO friendly blog posts, with data on why most pages get no search traffic, Google's guidance on titles, links and AI content, a pre-publish checklist and a worked example. Jamil Ahmed Published 1 Feb 2025 Updated 15 Nov 2026 12 Chapters 11 Min read A to Z Glossary 01 What is an SEO friendly blog post? 1 min 02 Why do most blog posts get no search traffic? 1 min 03 12 steps to write SEO friendly blog posts 6 min 04 How do you make a post useful for AI answers too? 1 min 05 Should you use AI to write blog posts? 1 min 06 How often should you update a post? 1 min 07 A copyable checklist before you publish 1 min 08 A 90-minute workflow 1 min 09 Common mistakes to avoid 1 min 10 Worked example (illustrative, not a client result) 1 min 11 Our interest in this topic 1 min 12 Final thoughts 1 min Chapter 01 of 12 0% read Chapters 0% 01 What is an SEO friendly blog post? 02 Why do most blog posts get no search traffic? 03 12 steps to write SEO friendly blog posts 04 How do you make a post useful for AI answers too? 05 Should you use AI to write blog posts? 06 How often should you update a post? 07 A copyable checklist before you publish 08 A 90-minute workflow 09 Common mistakes to avoid 10 Worked example (illustrative, not a client result) 11 Our interest in this topic 12 Final thoughts About 11 min in total Short answer To write SEO friendly blog posts, pick one topic people search for, check what already ranks and what it misses, then write a clear, original answer with a unique title, short sections, proof, useful links and a plain description. Put the answer first, name the author, cite sources you have read, and update the post when facts change. 01 Pick one topic and one primary keyword that match a real search need, then read the top 10 results to see what they cover and what they miss. 02 Ahrefs, a software vendor, found that 96.55% of about 14 billion pages in its index get no Google traffic. It notes its sample and estimates have limits. 03 Google says a good title is unique, clear and accurate. In an Ahrefs study Google rewrote titles 33.4% of the time, so make your H1 and title agree. 04 Add original value: first-hand experience, examples or data. Google says it has no preferred word count. 05 Ahrefs found Google showed the meta description only 37.22% of the time. Write a good one anyway. 06 Use AI for drafts if you like, but fact-check everything and add your own value. Using it to mass-produce pages may break Google's spam policy. 07 Update posts when facts change. Google lists changing a date to look fresh, without real changes, as a warning sign. To write SEO friendly blog posts, pick one topic that a real person searches for, check what already ranks and what it misses, then write a clear, original answer with a unique title, short sections, proof, useful links and a plain description. Put the answer first, name the author, cite sources you have read, and update the post when the facts change. Search engines reward content made for people, so the best SEO step is to be more useful than what is already there. This guide gives you 12 steps in the order we use them, the data on why most posts get no search traffic, a checklist you can copy, and a worked example. It replaces our older post on the same topic. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we say where a figure is a vendor’s own study. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is an SEO friendly blog post? It is a post that is useful to a reader and easy for a search engine to find, read and understand. The two goals fit together. Google says SEO can be a helpful activity when it is applied to people-first content, but not when the content is made mainly to attract search visits. An SEO friendly post has six traits: One clear topic and one primary keyword that match a real search need. A unique, accurate title and a direct answer near the top. Original value: first-hand experience, examples or data that other pages lack. Clear headings, short sentences and easy-to-scan sections. Honest signals of trust: an author, sources and a date that means something. Good links, useful images and a page that loads fast on a phone. End of chapter 1 Next: Why do most blog posts get no search traffic? → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min Why do most blog posts get no search traffic? Ahrefs, an SEO software vendor, studied about 14 billion pages in its own index. It found that 96.55% of pages get no traffic from Google, and 1.94% get one to ten visits a month. Ahrefs notes that the sample leans toward the quality side of the web and that its traffic numbers are estimates, so the real share may differ. Its newer statistics roundup says only 1.74% of newly published pages reach the top 10 for at least one keyword within a year, and that 72.9% of pages in the top 10 are more than three years old. These figures do not mean blogging is pointless. They mean that publishing alone is not enough. Posts that earn traffic usually match what people want, add something new, and get links and time. That is the aim of the steps below. End of chapter 2 Next: 12 steps to write SEO friendly blog posts → Reinforce Lab service · SEO Content Systems Want posts that rank and convert? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. Get your free diagnostic → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 6 min 12 steps to write SEO friendly blog posts Step 1: Choose a topic with real value Start with your customers, not a keyword list. Ask: Is this a question my audience has? Can I add something that others have not? If I rank, will it help my business? Then use keyword research to check demand and to choose the words people use. Pick one primary keyword for each post and two or three related phrases or questions. A tool such as Semrush or Ahrefs helps, and free sources such as Google Search Console, autocomplete and “People also ask” are a good start. Step 2: Check search intent and study the top results Search your keyword and read the top 10 pages on the search engine results page (SERP). Note what kind of page ranks: a how-to, a list, a comparison, a tool or a definition. Note what each page covers and what it leaves out. Your post must fit the intent. If everyone ranking is a step-by-step guide, a long opinion piece will struggle. Then plan what you can add: a fresher statistic, a worked example, a table, an expert view or a question the others skip. We run this check on every post before we write. Step 3: Write a unique, accurate title Google’s guidance says a good title is unique to the page, clear and concise, and accurately describes the content. Put the primary keyword near the front and aim for about 60 characters so it is less likely to be cut off. Avoid exaggeration. Google’s quality questions ask whether the main heading avoids being shocking or overstated. Do not expect your title to show exactly as written. Ahrefs found that Google rewrote title tags 33.4% of the time in its study, and that it was more likely to rewrite titles that were too long. When Google ignored the title tag, it used the H1 about half the time, so make your H1 and title agree. Step 4: Start with the answer Give the main answer in the first two or three sentences, then explain. Readers get what they need fast. Search engines and AI answer tools can also pull a clean answer from the page. Semrush recommends starting each section with a direct answer for the same reason. Skip long warm-ups that say nothing new. Step 5: Outline with one H1 and clear H2 and H3 headings Use one H1 for the title. Use H2 headings for the main sections and H3 headings for the parts within them. Write headings that say what the section answers, and where it fits, use a question that people ask, such as “How long should a blog post be?” This helps people scan, and it shows search engines how the page is organized. Do not skip levels or use headings only for style. Step 6: Add original value This step matters most. Google asks whether content provides original information, reporting, research or analysis, and whether it adds substantial value when compared with other pages in the results. If you mainly summarize others, you add little. Add what only you can: results from your own work, photos you took, a process you follow, a mistake you made, a price you quote, or a clear opinion with reasons. Add a table, a checklist or a worked example when it helps. Do not write to a target word count. Google says it has no preferred word count. Write as long as the topic needs. Step 7: Write so people can read it Use short sentences and short paragraphs of two to three sentences. Choose everyday words, and explain a term the first time you use it. Use bullet points for lists and numbered steps for procedures. Use active voice. Say who does what. Read the draft out loud, then cut anything that does not help. A note on scores: tools that grade reading level can help you write plainly, but Ahrefs found no correlation between Flesch Reading Ease and ranking position. Use them to help readers, not to chase a ranking. We aim for grade 8 or lower because most people read faster that way. Step 8: Show who wrote it and why you can be trusted Google’s “Who, How and Why” test is a good checklist. It ties to what Google calls E-E-A-T: experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, with trust the most important. Who wrote this? Put a byline that links to a short bio with real credentials. How was it made? Say so if you used automation or AI in a major way. Why was it made? The answer should be to help people. Cite the sources you used and link to them. Only quote a statistic that you have read at the source, and say how old it is and what its limits are. Do not fake an author, use made-up credentials or hide how the post was made. Step 9: Write a plain meta description The meta description is a short summary that may appear under your title in search results. Google says a good one is short, unique to the page and includes the most relevant points. Keep it to about 140 to 160 characters, include the keyword once and say what the reader will get. Do not expect it to show every time. Ahrefs found that Google showed the meta description in results only 37.22% of the time and rewrote it 62.78% of the time, and that 25.02% of top-ranking pages had none. Write one anyway. It costs little, and it is your best shot at controlling the snippet. Step 10: Use a short, clear URL Use a slug that names the topic in a few words, such as /how-to-write-seo-friendly-blog-posts/. Use lowercase letters and hyphens. Leave out dates, extra words and IDs. Once a URL is live and earning traffic, do not change it without a redirect plan. Step 11: Add useful links Internal links: link to related posts and to the page that serves the reader’s next step. Google says every page you care about should have a link from at least one other page on your site, and that there is no magic number of links. Use descriptive link text, also called anchor text, not “click here.” External links: link to the primary source for each statistic or claim. Link only to pages you trust. If you do not trust a page but still want to link to it, add a nofollow or similar attribute. For example, see our guide to SEO mistakes to avoid for a checklist of problems that block good posts, and our best SEO practices for the wider picture. Step 12: Add images with alt text Use sharp, relevant images near the text they relate to. Add short, descriptive alt text that explains what the image shows and how it relates to the page. Leave out stuffed keywords. Compress files so the page loads quickly on a phone. Add a featured image that fits the topic, and keep each image’s file name plain, such as seo-checklist-table.png. End of chapter 3 Next: How do you make a post useful for AI answers too? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min How do you make a post useful for AI answers too? The same habits help AI answer tools, since they pull clear, well-sourced passages. Lead each section with a direct answer, keep one idea per paragraph, use headings that match real questions, name the author, cite primary sources and show the date of the last real update. Semrush cites an AirOps study that found fresh content was one of the strongest predictors of AI visibility. That is a vendor-cited study, so treat it as a signal, not a rule. Our guide to ranking in AI Overviews goes deeper. End of chapter 4 Next: Should you use AI to write blog posts? → 05 Chapter 5 · 1 min Should you use AI to write blog posts? You can, with care. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines. Using AI mainly to manipulate rankings is. Its guidance on scaled content abuse says that generating many pages without adding value for users may break its spam policy. Google also says generative models predict likely words and do not retrieve facts, so you must fact-check everything, including titles, meta descriptions and alt text. A safe approach: Use AI for outlines, rewording and first drafts, not as the final author. Add your own experience, examples, numbers and photos. Check every fact and statistic at the source. Have a named person review and own the post. Do not publish dozens of near-identical pages. See our review of AI content writing tools for options. End of chapter 5 Next: How often should you update a post? → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min How often should you update a post? Update a post when its facts change, when a better source appears, or when it starts to lose traffic. A real update means new data, new steps or a corrected claim, and a date that reflects it. Google’s guidance lists changing the date of a page to make it look fresh, when the content has not substantially changed, as a warning sign. It also says that adding or removing a lot of content just to seem fresh will not help. Show the last-updated date only when you earned it. End of chapter 6 Next: A copyable checklist before you publish → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min A copyable checklist before you publish Check What good looks like Topic and intent One primary keyword. Matches what the top results offer. Title Unique, accurate, keyword near the front, about 60 characters. Opening Answers the main question in two or three sentences. Headings One H1. Clear H2 and H3 headings. No skipped levels. Original value At least one example, data point or experience others lack. Readability Short sentences and paragraphs. Plain words. Trust Byline, bio, sources linked, honest date. Meta description 140 to 160 characters. Unique. Says what the reader will get. URL Short, lowercase, keyword in it. Links Descriptive internal links. Primary-source external links. Images Relevant, compressed, with plain alt text. Page experience Loads fast and reads well on a phone. End of chapter 7 Next: A 90-minute workflow → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min A 90-minute workflow 15 minutes: choose the keyword, read the top 10 and list what is missing. 10 minutes: write the title, the answer and an outline. 40 minutes: write the draft with your own examples and sources. 15 minutes: edit for short sentences, add links and images, and write the meta description. 10 minutes: run the checklist, preview on a phone and publish. After publishing, check Google Search Console in a few weeks. Look at impressions, clicks and the queries that bring people. Improve the post based on what you see. End of chapter 8 Next: Common mistakes to avoid → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Common mistakes to avoid Writing for the keyword, not the reader. Stuffing a phrase into every line hurts readability and trust. Copying the top results. If you add nothing new, there is no reason to rank above them. Publishing thin posts. Short, vague pages rarely earn traffic. Skipping the byline and sources. They are quick trust signals. Faking freshness. Changing the date without changing the content can backfire. Ignoring mobile. A slow, cramped page loses readers. Not measuring. Without data, you cannot improve. End of chapter 9 Next: Worked example (illustrative, not a client result) → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min Worked example (illustrative, not a client result) Take a hypothetical accounting firm that wants to rank for “how to track small business expenses.” It reads the top 10 results and finds mostly generic lists with no examples. It chooses a how-to format, adds a downloadable sheet, a worked example with sample numbers it can support, and a short section on mistakes it sees with new clients. The title is “How to Track Small Business Expenses: A Simple 5-Step Method.” The post opens with the answer, names the partner who wrote it, links to the tax authority’s rules and to two of the firm’s own pages, and adds a clear call to book a review. No traffic numbers are claimed, because this is a template. The point is the process: study the results, add original value, then build the page cleanly. End of chapter 10 Next: Our interest in this topic → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells SEO and content services. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . Our SEO content systems service follows these steps, and you can get your free diagnostic . End of chapter 11 Next: Final thoughts → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min Final thoughts SEO friendly blog posts are not a formula. They are useful posts with clean signals. Choose a topic worth your reader’s time, check what already ranks, add something new, and make the page clear and trustworthy. Measure what happens, and keep the post true as things change. Back matter Glossary A to Z A Alt text A short description of an image for screen readers and search engines. I Internal link A link from one page on your site to another page on your site. M Meta description A short summary of the page that may appear under the title in search results. P Primary keyword The main phrase a post is built to rank for. S Search intent What a person wants to do when they type a search, such as learn, compare or buy. Questions FAQs What is an SEO friendly blog post? It is a post that helps a reader and is easy for search engines to find and understand: one clear topic, a unique title, a direct answer, original value, clear headings, trust signals, good links and images, and a fast page. How long should an SEO friendly blog post be? Google says it has no preferred word count. Write as long as the topic needs, and check the top results to see how deep they go. Depth and usefulness matter more than length. How many keywords should a blog post target? Choose one primary keyword for each post, plus a few related phrases and questions that fit naturally. Do not repeat a keyword to force it. Does reading level affect SEO? Ahrefs found no correlation between Flesch Reading Ease scores and ranking position. Plain writing still helps readers, so use short sentences and everyday words. Is a meta description a ranking factor? We found no Google statement that it is. It can shape the snippet. Ahrefs found Google showed the written meta description 37.22% of the time, so write a good one but expect rewrites. Will Google use my title exactly as I write it? Not always. Ahrefs found Google rewrote title tags 33.4% of the time in its study, and was more likely to rewrite long titles. Write a clear, accurate title and keep the H1 consistent with it. Can I use AI to write blog posts? Yes, with care. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines, but using it to mass-produce pages without value may violate its spam policy. Fact-check everything and add original value. How often should I update blog posts? Update when facts change, a better source appears or traffic drops. Make real changes and show a date that reflects them. Google lists changing dates without substantial changes as a warning sign. How many internal links should a blog post have? Google says there is no magic number. Every page you care about should have a link from at least one other page, with descriptive link text. If it feels like too many, it probably is. Why does my blog post get no traffic? Common causes are a topic with no real search demand, content that does not match the search intent, little original value, no links, and a page that is not indexed. Check Search Console and compare your post with the top results. meta: Having creative ideas for personal website content can go a long way to progress your career as a website is more unique than a CV or resume.
h1_text: Best 5 Ideas for Personal Website Content 2025
lede: About 10 min in total
copy_text: Home Blog Web Design Best 5 Ideas for Personal Website Content 2025 Guide Web Design Best 5 Ideas for Personal Website Content 2025 R Reinforce Lab team Published 3 Feb 2025 Updated 15 Apr 2025 12 Chapters 10 Min read 01 What is a Personal Website? 2 min 02 Ideas for Personal Website Content 1 min 03 Homepage 1 min 04 About Page 1 min 05 Contact Info 1 min 06 Portfolio 1 min 07 Resume 1 min 08 Professional Blogs 1 min 09 Testimonials 1 min 10 Case Studies 1 min 11 What type of Content to Avoid for A Personal Website? 1 min 12 Wrapping Up – Ideas for Personal Website Content 1 min Chapter 01 of 12 0% read Chapters 0% 01 What is a Personal Website? 02 Ideas for Personal Website Content 03 Homepage 04 About Page 05 Contact Info 06 Portfolio 07 Resume 08 Professional Blogs 09 Testimonials 10 Case Studies 11 What type of Content to Avoid for A Personal Website? 12 Wrapping Up – Ideas for Personal Website Content About 10 min in total Having creative ideas for personal website content can go a long way to progressing your career, as a website is more unique than a CV or resume. Whether you are hunting for work, trying to run a business, or selling a product, a website of your own can provide you with a healthy online presence and more credibility. Anyone can open a page on a social media platform or business/employment platforms that are readily available. However, having your own website would indicate that you are more serious. So with all the business and industry websites around us, let’s get to know about – 01 Chapter 1 · 2 min What is a Personal Website? A personal website is a website created to showcase an individual’s work and persona. Unlike the majority of internet web pages, it does not pertain to any particular corporation, institution, or organization. You can denote it as a group of web pages where only your personal features, works, achievements, and contact information will be. Additionally, it lets you showcase your work in your creative structure. WorkItDaily states that nearly 56% of employers and recruiters are more impressed by an individual’s website. On the other hand, according to Forbes , only 7% of the general population has a personal website. For millennials, the percentage is 15%. Of course, the percentages have increased by today. Nonetheless, it indicates that a personal website can give you a great chance to stand out from the crowd. Having a personal website might sound difficult at first, however, once you get the hang of it, it is pretty straightforward. Furthermore, when you develop some personal website content ideas and implement them in a well-planned way, it creates a beautiful online presence for you. To implement that more effectively, you can look into some simple personal website examples for ideas. You will be able to see how creatively people have already managed to showcase their features. Usually, you will find many colorful and vibrant features in their web content design. Moreover, if you are more serious about your work and focusing on a professional presence, you can look into some professional personal website examples. Checking these out will give you a more in-depth idea about web content personalization in a more professional manner. At the end of the day, you want to create a healthy online presence and attract people who are more aligned or appreciative of your work. Your personal website design and personal website content allow you to do just that. It is a great source of personal branding. With those in mind, we are here to provide you with some amazing ideas for personal website content. End of chapter 1 Next: Ideas for Personal Website Content → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min Ideas for Personal Website Content The more decorated, organized, and personalized your personal website content is, the more attractive it will feel. You will even feel good about yourself when your website is full of quality content. So, with a focus on web content personalization, here are the sections and content you must have on your website for proper optimization. End of chapter 2 Next: Homepage → 03 Chapter 3 · 1 min Homepage Your website homepage should greet people according to your persona and profession. Decorate your homepage with your signature style, font, and colors. If your homepage layout is strong, so will your website. Personal websites do not need a lot of links and sub-links. We will explain which sections and pages will add more to your website. However, make it so that your homepage itself will catch the eyes of the hiring managers. Add attractive feature photos of you or content related to you. You can also include an image of your workstation if you make it visually organized and pleasing. Look out for the color scheme. Choosing an aesthetically pleasing color scheme for your website will highly appeal to the visual memory of your potential clients. Include your elevator pitch statement on your homepage. It means mentioning your passion, profession, and goal in your way. On your homepage, do it as shortly and impactfully as possible. This, when done effectively, will lead your visitors to be interested to learn more about you. Needless to say, your homepage is the most integral part of your personal website design. It will define the template of your website and lead site visitors to more of your personalized website content. End of chapter 3 Next: About Page → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min About Page Having a crafty, short, and sweet About page will give people just what they need. An idea of you and your work. Oftentimes, it would be the home page or landing page of your website, so make a good first impression. Don’t make the mistake of making your about page too long. It may have worked in the early stages on the internet. In today’s day and age, just having a short greeting, having a bit of personal touch, and showcasing your work and background would be enough. Just feature these: What do you work on Your educational/professional background A mentionable work achievement Your latest project and current passion All these pieces of information can make your About Page good to go. This page is another sector where you are endorsing your elevator pitch. So, make your passion and profession known to your site visitors. Let them know what you are looking for and aiming for. All these can make your about page much stronger. End of chapter 4 Next: Contact Info → 05 Chapter 5 · 1 min Contact Info So now that people know about you, where can they contact you, or how can they hire you? It is essential to let people connect with you and contact you. In that regard, attach your email and contact number if you feel comfortable. Link your social or professional profiles as required. It is a good idea to attach appropriate icons with the contacts. This makes the contact content look more familiar, professional, and attractive. A great piece of content you can create for your website is a contact form. People can leave text messages directly there or if they have any inquiries. It is always best to let people choose multiple options to contact you. Whether they want to email you, text you, or contact you directly, they should have the option. So craft your contact information content section accordingly. End of chapter 5 Next: Portfolio → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min Portfolio Your portfolio will need to feature your best work samples. This gives your viewer a hands-on experience of your work. Visual content creator like graphic designers or photo/video editors can make their best impression in this sector. So, if you are a graphic designer or editor, do not forget to put in your best work here to showcase to the world. If you are a content writer or web developer, you can link your best articles and web pages here. If you send your website to your possible employers, this is where they would focus most. So it is very necessary to make your personal website’s portfolio section well-crafted and organized. End of chapter 6 Next: Resume → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min Resume Forwarding a regular resume through email or hand-to-hand has become a common experience nowadays. However, if you pass your website to your potential client or employer, it creates a different experience when they see your resume on your website. You can take help from resume websites. From there, you can easily form and share your resume using proper templates. Make sure these sections are visible in your resume: Your education/ qualifications Your skillsets and expertise Your work experiences Your notable achievements These pieces of content are very necessary for your resume, which adds to your site too. Usually, you would add specific changes to your resume according to the need of the job you are applying for. Since on your website, anyone from any sector can visit your resume, you can make your resume a bit more elaborate. Try to include all your noteworthy educational and professional qualifications in your resume so that it can seem multipurpose and cover multiple grounds. End of chapter 7 Next: Professional Blogs → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min Professional Blogs Blogs should be included in your personal website content ideas. Blogs contain a lot of useful information and, if presented well, also generate a lot of traffic. So whether you write your article or feature some blog articles related to your profession, it would surely enrich your personal website and make it look well-established. Link your WordPress with your website. Learn how to function and operate WordPress well. Through that, you will easily be able to process, update, write, and re-write articles to your liking. People regularly visit blogs for updates, tips, information, and fun. So when you have well-crafted, relevant, and engaging blogs on your website, your personal website quality and viewership will automatically skyrocket. People often comment in blog comment sections. Look after those. Interact with them, and you will also find possible new ideas for newer content. End of chapter 8 Next: Testimonials → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Testimonials Positive word of mouth is always a plus for any personal or business venture. When clients or employers check your website and see authentic reviews and words from people who have worked with you or people you have worked for, it is sure to create a positive impact. Beyond what you write about yourself, if people agree that you have a strong work ethic, you are skilled and expert in your sector, and all the related adjectives relevant to your sector, it can give you increased credibility. To garner authentic testimonials, you can ask your formal clients and or employers to mention a brief comment about yourself and how helpful your work or skillset has been. If they struggle to write properly, use a formal LinkedIn comment that goes with you and ask for their approval or modification. All in all, testimonials are surely very useful among your ideas for personal website content. End of chapter 9 Next: Case Studies → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min Case Studies Case studies analyze the reports of your products or services in a more detailed manner than testimonials. So these can be even more effective than mere reviews. Case studies can make your website and personal profile even more credible and influence your site visitors to work with you. It is a kind of social proof that eliminates any of your hiring managers’ doubt or trust issues. In conclusion, case studies can be pretty effective. End of chapter 10 Next: What type of Content to Avoid for A Personal Website? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min What type of Content to Avoid for A Personal Website? It is to be mentioned that while you already have some idea about what to do and not to do, it is good to be reminded so that you are aware. Pay close attention to these points- Make your about page too lengthy and uneventful Don’t overwhelm your viewer or site visitors with too many collections of your work and history details. Keep some things to yourself, and focus on featuring the best ones. Avoid mentioning social media platforms that are unrelated to your work and profession. Do not post images that are low in resolution or stolen from stock photos. Do not post blogs that are poorly researched or misleading. Do not be inconsistent with your blog posts. Regularly updating them would make your website seem more active and fresh. Do not post vague testimonials that might be full of mistakes and overly flattering. Make sure they are written accordingly with approval. Keep them work-specific and simple. If you feel like you can not write updated, thought-provoking blogs free of many mistakes, it is better to avoid them. If a visitor comes to your site and sees that your last post was two years ago, they can automatically assume that your website is outdated. End of chapter 11 Next: Wrapping Up – Ideas for Personal Website Content → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min Wrapping Up – Ideas for Personal Website Content It can understandably seem hard to establish a personal website at first. However, with these ideas for personal website content, you will start to feel more confident about what you can post. The world is open to you on the internet, and through your personal website, you can connect and engage more people than ever before. So utilize these personal website content ideas, and make your progress come to you. Liked what you read? There’s more to be learned! Read more from our blog . copy_text: Home Blog Search Engine Optimization 5 Reasons Why You Should Invest In SEO… Opinion Search Engine Optimization 5 Reasons Why You Should Invest In SEO For Small Business By Reinforce Lab team Published 26 Feb 2025 Updated 13 Apr 2025 14 min read Contents (11) What Is SEO? What Is Small Business SEO? Is SEO Good For Small Businesses? Why SEO Matters for Small Businesses? 5 Reasons Why Your Business Should Invest In SEO Why SEO Is A Great Investment. Not just A Cost How Much Should You Invest In SEO? Should I Invest More In SMO Relative To SEO? Why Hire An SEO Services Company Wrapping Up – 5 Reasons Why You Should Invest In SEO For Small Business FAQs You may get more than 500% ROI from making SEO investment. So, you must invest in SEO for your small business and skyrocket your business. Are you confused about this? If you are, no problem. I’m here to describe. According to a survey conducted by Clutch in 2019, “ 55% of small businesses are currently investing in SEO.” And YahooFinance said in 2022, “ 63% of Small Businesses Invest in SEO.” We see here that investment in SEO is increasing in small businesses. Should we be blown away by the tide? Instead, we should know the benefits of the invest in SEO. It will be helpful to remove your confusion. A study by Moz found that the first page of Google search results captures 71% of search traffic clicks, and the top five results on the first page capture 67% of all clicks. In a survey conducted by BrightLocal in 2020, 93% of consumers used the internet to find a local business, and 34% searched for local businesses daily. A case study by SEO.com showed that a small business could increase its organic search traffic by 195% within one year of implementing an SEO strategy. I think, from these stats, you are clear about the necessity of the invest in SEO. We can also see how helpful we will be from SEO investment. But, if you are not a believer in stat or you have still confused about SEO for small businesses, I will request you to keep with this blog. In this blog, I will explain to you the 5 most important reasons for the invest in SEO for small businesses. Let’s dive into the main topic. What Is SEO? Simply, SEO, or search engine optimization, is a process. This is optimizing your website to improve its ranking and visibility on search engine results pages (SERPs). SEO involves changing your website’s design, content, and structure to make it more attractive to search engines like Google, Bing, and Yahoo. Optimizing your website for relevant keywords and phrases can increase the likelihood that it will appear at the top of search results. So when potential customers search for a product or service related to your business, they can find your website. Besides, this can help drive more traffic to your website. Along with this, it will increase brand awareness and ultimately boost the sales and revenue of your small business. What Is Small Business SEO? Small companies With the help of search engine optimization SEO, you may increase the visibility of your small business website on Google’s search engine results pages (SERPs). You can also rank well for products related to what you sell. Moreover, it’s crucial to distinguish between small company SEO and local SEO since local SEO promotes firms to appear in location-based search results rather than overall results. Nonetheless, some small firms could want to take advantage of local traffic; in this case, your small business strategy will contain local measures. We’ll talk more about this below. Is SEO Good For Small Businesses? For small businesses, SEO is essential since it enables you to get organic traffic without investing in paid marketing in SERPs or other channels. As your website appears in search results, you become more competitive and attract more visitors. So, it helps you increase engagement, close deals, and establish a clientele. On the other hand, you don’t optimize your site. Then your competitors may be the only ones appearing in search results. As a result, your target audience may not even be aware that you exist. Let’s discuss SEO for small businesses details now. Why SEO Matters for Small Businesses? SEO is an excellent part of a business. It produces a huge number of qualified leads for the business. For small businesses, SEO matters a lot. There are some reasons: Search Engines Have A Massive User Base SEO is crucial if you want to reach billions of searches on search engines, as over 93% of online encounters start with one. Internet users won’t be able to find your goods and services without SEO. Here, you may choose a rival that appears higher in the search results. To Rank Heigher In Organic Search, You Need Not Pay You need not pay any search engine to rank your website higher in the organic search results. But here is an exception to pay-per-click (PPC) advertising that appears at the top of the search results page. Thus, SEO is crucial for outranking your rivals an ranking highly on search engines. You Can Use SEO TO Respond To Consumer Queiries Positively It very is essential for SEO to provide answers to customer questions and search intent. Additionally, you’ll start producing material and experiences that users will find helpful as you optimize your website. As a result, you’ll establish a reliable and respectable reputation for your business. And it will draw customers in regularly. There is no other good option without SEO if you want an online presence for your business. It will help you to market your products and services successfully. SEO is a crucial digital marketing strategy to increase your business. 5 Reasons Why Your Business Should Invest In SEO We are in the main section of our blog. I know you are eagerly waiting for that. Already you know that SEO can be highly beneficial for your business. Besides, it can boost your business growth in the long term. Okay, no more waiting. Here are 5 reasons why you should invest in SEO. I think it will remove all your confusion. 1. SEO Raises Reputation And Brand Awareness At the very beginning, you have to create your brand’s recognition, awareness, and credibility. The reason is it will make your firm develop a devoted customer base of repeat consumers and draw in new potential clients. In this situation, SEO may assist you in producing educational and practical material. As a result, it will appeal to readers with so many SEO tactics concentrating on your content marketing. Customers are more likely to perceive your company as an industry authority when they find that your content and website solve their problems or answer their questions. Besides, it will increase the authority and credibility of your brand. Additionally, SEO makes your business more visible online. In the meantime, it encourages customers to interact with your brand and raises brand recognition. 2. Your Digital Marketing ROI Increases Due To SEO When developing a digital marketing plan, you should select your ultimate objective as the best return on investment (ROI) for your marketing activities. Thankfully, SEO can be useful. SEO can complement other forms of digital marketing greatly Content marketing and online advertising are effective weapons in this case. When you can make great use of technical SEO tactics, it may ensure that visitors can locate your online marketing initiatives. Here, newly developed content is a good mechanism. Again I emphasize that to increase your marketing effectiveness and draw in more customers via online channels, SEO helps other digital marketing techniques on a large scale. You’ll consequently see higher sales and money, enabling you to finally raise your digital marketing ROI. 3. SEO Increases Your Quality Website Traffic The most important thing is your qualified leads from your website. Quality traffic is essential to find the targeted audience of your business. Besides, it will ensure the customers who are most interested in your items find your brand online. Additionally, considering that 80% of consumers conduct their product research online. SEO may assist you in making sure that customers looking for your products and services online can discover you. Since SEO will help you rank higher on results pages, more potential clients interested in your items will find your brand. Undoubtedly it will boost the quality traffic to your website for your company or business. 4. SEO Boosts User Experience One of the most important things is creating a seamless user experience for your website. It will increase your retaining customers on your website. Besides, it will allow them to browse your products until they are ready to purchase. A study says 89% of customers shop with a rival after a bad experience on a website. So, imagine how vital SEO investment is in your small business. Moreover, search engines frequently consider user experience when determining which websites and contents to rank highest on the results page. As a result, these SEO techniques will ensure users get the relevant content they seek. And then, it may notify search engines that your website has a good user experience. It will help you rank high in the results. So we can say SEO helps improve user experience by implementing strategies that raise your website. 5. SEO Ensures Your Business’s Long-term Success Undoubtedly, the finest advantage of SEO or the greatest ability of SEO is to increase your company’s long-term prosperity. SEO is a sustained, long-term strategy. On the contrary, it is unlike many other traditional marketing operations. Regular investment in SEO enables you to stay on top of search engines regularly. Even regularly invest in SEO to optimize your website and create content to attract visitors. The most important thing is years after investing in your SEO strategy, you can still see results from it. This indicates that when you engage in SEO, your company can grow and reach your target audience. As well as your business can increase sales and revenue, enabling your company to expand and achieve new heights. After seeing these 5 reasons, I think there is no need for any words to describe the importance of investing in SEO. I firmly believe you will not make any late to invest in SEO. Why SEO Is A Great Investment. Not just A Cost Businesses consistently make investments. Each investment has the goal of providing current funding for a future return. Why therefore does SEO, for example, lack the necessary investment? My hypothesis, The essence of investments in SEO is compounding. Increased traffic and income might be difficult to “notice” because the growth is considerably more apparent when measured over time, frequently up to a year later. But who wants to retake the reins after a year and declare, “Hey, look, we did it!” Unfortunately, it is how organic results work They are labor-intensive to make. So, in nature, it is one kind of investment. The most important thing is if you take SEO as an investment, it will be better to keep enough patience. Because you already know SEO is a long-term process. How Much Should You Invest In SEO? Now we are discussing another vital aspect of SEO. From this, you will be more clear about your SEO investment. And to do that, you must set aside money from your marketing budget for it. But precisely how much? Fix smartly. You’re not the only one who doesn’t know how to respond to this. Unfortunately, there isn’t a simple solution. There is much variation depending on where you are beginning from and where you want to reach. One thing is sure: You get what you pay for, just like with beds and vehicle batteries. You’ll probably get budget results if you try to proceed in that direction. If you work with one of the many SEO consultant artists who promise “Guaranteed First Page Results,” you risk being the victim of several black hat SEO techniques. It will lead to penalties and effectively erase your site’s exposure. In another aspect, there is no problem if you don’t have a massive budget for SEO. Still, you can get a good result. On the other hand, SMO focuses on optimizing your social media profiles and content to increase engagement and build relationships with your audience. copy_text: Home Blog Search Engine Optimization Latest SEO update 2025 : 14 Search Engine… Update Search Engine Optimization Latest SEO update 2025 : 14 Search Engine Updates R Reinforce Lab team Published 9 Feb 2025 Updated 15 Apr 2025 Do you know the latest SEO updates for 2025? How often do Search Engine Updates occurs? or when for natural google update SEO or google local SEO update? For Search Engine updates, you are in the right place. We often get questions, how often does google update SEO? According to Search Engine Land, in 2025. Google came up with 3 core updates and 2 product review updates ( one of them is on 1st December). But that’s not all. The answer to How often Google updates SEO is- 500/600 times per year. Though not all of them are significant updates, acknowledging them is essential for SEO strategy. Search engines bring various changes that are connected to SEO and ranking factors. There is no alternative to staying updated with the latest news and changes in search engines. That is why we make your task easier by posting the monthly updates together. We have gathered all the search engine updates for December 2025. Let’s see what they are: Latest SEO Update 2025: 14 Search Engine Updates In December month, there were 14 mentionable updates. Here they are sorted by date: 1. Product Review Updates On 1st December 2024, google brought a new update on product reviews. This google algorithm update SEO is for affiliate marketers and significantly impacts SEO and blog post writing style. Google puts emphasis on genuine reviews that actually help the consumers, not only structured data. Must avoid intrusive interstitials. They suggested focusing on two points: 1. Add proof to your review 2. Add More than 1 seller 2. Shopping integration with photoshop On 2nd December Google announced that they would integrate with Photoshop. Previously, you had to use Google merchant center to show products on search results. This was a little bit of a complicated process. From this update, you can easily upload your products. 3. Google Ads API update On 3rd December, Google ads API announced that it would support recommendations, performance max campaigns and keyword planners. But these tools are not going to be free, as the way Google API Isn’t. For every 25,000 operations, it charges one dollar. 4. Political Content Policy Update On 6th December, Google updated its political content policy, which will be activated from 15th February. One of the mentionable changes is that political content will be no more national. You can select your target audience worldwide. 5. Image extension Update On 7th December, Google launched an image extension for desktops as well. Previously this was only for mobile phones. However, this update launched in the USA a few months ago, and finally, it started worldwide. 6. Ethical shopping hub Launch On 8th December, Microsoft launched an ethical shopping hub. Previously it was only available for the UK region, but now everyone can use the Facility. 7. Google news feed Update On 9th December, Google revised its internal system to collect impressions by Google news feed. 8. YouTube Vlog Update YouTube announced places mentioned in the video. Now it will help the travel vloggers to show the location better and also will be helpful for the user to find the place. 9. Google Map change On 10th December,  Google Changed the map for local searches. Though the change is so tiny, it improves the user experience for map search queries. 10. Redirect Issue Announced On 13th December, Google accepted redirect error bugs in the google search console of google business profiles. Many pages were redirected previously, and that is not your issue; it’s official now. 11. Google Search Console Update On 14th December, Google changed the way it reports rich results in the Google search console. No, you cannot give the star only; you must also post text. This page experience update will help to find reliable reviews. 12. GA4 linked with Search Console From 15th December, you can link GA4 and Google search console web properties. This update is targeted to make the user experience better. 13. Google local SEO update On 16th December, Google casually informed us about a massive 2025 local search update that rolled out Between 30th November and 8th December. It Rebalanced various factors, and reduced area coverage. From November 2021, local search it has introduced. So this has become another factor we consider in generating local search results. 14. Product Entity Update On 28th December, Google announced a change in product entity evaluation in the Google search console. Google will not show all the problems as errors like before; it will show the problems as warnings. Interestingly Google has updated its algorithm this year again! And the update occurred in May 2025. So let’s get to know about the brand new update of Google now. Google’s overall recommendation about core changes is as follows: Expect widely apparent impacts, such as spikes or dips in search ranks. Core updates are “broad” because they don’t target anything particular. Rather, they aim to enhance Google’s systems overall. Pages that tumble in ranks aren’t being punished; they’re being appraised against other online material that has been released since the previous update. The top advised approach to cope with the effect of a core algorithm modification is to create the most excellent possible content. Broad core upgrades occur every several months. Sites may not recover from one upgrade until the next one comes out. Improvements may not ensure recovery. However, deciding not to adopt any modifications will nearly assure no recovery.
