24 Common mistakes 25 A quick checklist 26 Final thoughts About 16 min in total Short answer Keyword difficulty (KD) is a score, usually 0 to 100, that estimates how hard it is to reach page one of Google for a search term. Tools such as Semrush and Ahrefs calculate it from the strength of the pages that already rank, so scores differ by tool. Use it to compare keywords, then read the real results page to decide. 01 Keyword difficulty is an estimate made by SEO tools. Google does not publish it. 02 Scores differ between tools, so compare keywords inside one tool only. 03 New sites should start with keywords in the 0 to 30 range and move up as links and trust grow. 04 Always check search intent and the real top 10 results before you choose a keyword. 05 Counting the links the lower-ranking pages have gives a more useful target than the score alone. 06 Recheck your target keywords every three to six months. Keyword difficulty (KD) is a score that estimates how hard it is to rank on the first page of Google for a search term. A low score means it is easier. A high score means you face strong competition. This guide explains what keyword difficulty is, how tools work it out, what a “good” score is for your site, and how to check a keyword yourself in 10 minutes. It also shows how to turn the score into a content plan. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is keyword difficulty in SEO? Keyword difficulty is a number, usually from 0 to 100, that tells you how competitive a search term is. It is also called keyword competition or SEO difficulty. The higher the number, the harder it is to reach page one. Two facts matter before you use it: Google does not publish it. KD is not a Google metric. SEO tools such as Semrush, Ahrefs and Moz make their own estimate. It is an estimate. Every tool uses its own method, so the same keyword can get different scores in different tools. Use KD to compare keywords inside one tool. Do not compare a Semrush score with an Ahrefs score. End of chapter 1 Next: Why does keyword difficulty matter? → 02 Chapter 2 · 2 min Why does keyword difficulty matter? Time and money for content are limited. KD helps you choose where to spend them. It saves effort. A new site that targets a very hard keyword can wait a year and still rank nowhere. It finds quick wins. Easier keywords can bring visits sooner, which gives you data and links to build on. It sets honest goals. It tells you whether you need one good page or a page plus many links. It balances your plan. You can mix easy keywords for early traffic with harder ones for later. The numbers show why the choice matters. Ahrefs studied about 14 billion pages in its Content Explorer database in 2023. It estimated that 96.55% of them got no traffic from Google, and 1.94% got between one and ten visits a month. Ahrefs says its traffic numbers are estimates and that the sample leans toward the “quality side of the web”, so the real figure may differ. The point still holds: most pages never reach the searchers they were written for. Position matters too. Backlinko analyzed about 4 million Google results and found that the first result had an average click rate of 27.6%, that the top three results took 54.4% of clicks, and that only 0.63% of searchers clicked anything on page two. That study came before AI answers, so treat the exact figures as a historical baseline. A hard keyword where you land on page two earns almost nothing, which is why picking a keyword you can reach comes first. End of chapter 2 Next: How is keyword difficulty calculated? → Reinforce Lab service · Search Engine Optimization Want help choosing keywords you can win? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See SEO services → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 2 min How is keyword difficulty calculated? Each tool looks at the pages that rank in the top 10 for the keyword and scores how strong those pages are. The tools publish more detail than many people think. Here are two of them, as the vendors describe their own scores: Tool Scale What goes into the score Ahrefs 0 to 100 How many websites link to each of the top 10 pages. It does not use your own site’s authority. Semrush 0 to 100% A weighted formula. The median number of referring domains to the ranking pages carries 41.22% of the weight. The median Authority Score of the ranking domains carries 16.99%. Search volume carries 9.47%. The ratio of dofollow to nofollow links carries 9.17%. Search result features such as featured snippets (4.74%), local packs (3.39%) and “People also ask” boxes (1.36%) carry the rest, and keywords with no features score lower. Semrush says it built its formula by studying the movement of results for 120,000 keywords and more than 100 parameters. It uses the median of the top 10 so that one very strong page does not inflate the score. Both tools lean mostly on links. That is why a keyword can look easy to a tool when the content on page one is weak, or hard when the content is good but old. Scores also differ between tools, because each one uses its own formula and its own link data. Other input What it tells you Content quality and fit Whether the top pages match what searchers want and cover the topic well. Tools score this little or not at all, so check it by hand. Search intent Whether results are guides, product pages or tools. Your page must fit the same type. End of chapter 3 Next: What do the score ranges mean? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min What do the score ranges mean? Each tool labels its own scale. Semrush publishes six levels. Your own site’s strength changes how you read them. Semrush KD Label What Semrush says it takes 0 to 14 Very easy The best chance to rank a new page with the least effort. 15 to 29 Easy Some competition, but achievable even for a new domain with quality content that fits the intent. 30 to 49 Possible Quality, well-structured, optimized content. 50 to 69 Difficult Quality content plus some quality backlinks. 70 to 84 Hard A lot of effort to win better backlinks to support strong content. 85 to 100 Very hard Content, link building, on-page work and promotion, all at a high level. Ahrefs describes its scale in terms of links. A KD of 0 to 5 means the top pages barely have any backlinks. Around KD 50, the top pages have a couple of hundred backlinks. At KD 90 and above, they have thousands. In one example on its page, a KD of 6 is labeled easy, with about 7 referring domains needed to reach the top 10. A new site should start in the easy bands and move up as it earns links and trust. An older site with many links can aim higher. End of chapter 4 Next: What is a good keyword difficulty score to target? → 05 Chapter 5 · 1 min What is a good keyword difficulty score to target? There is no single good score. It depends on your site’s strength. Here is a simple way to choose: Find a keyword you already rank for on page two or three. Note its KD. Look at the KD of the keywords you rank for on page one. The highest of these is your “reach.” Aim for keywords at or a little above that reach. Mix in some easier ones for quick wins. If you have no rankings yet, start at 0 to 30 and move up as your pages gain traffic and links. End of chapter 5 Next: Keyword difficulty vs search volume → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min Keyword difficulty vs search volume Search volume is how many times a month people search for a term. KD is how hard it is to rank. You need both. Mix What to do High volume, low KD Best target. Check intent, then build a strong page. High volume, high KD A long-term goal. Build supporting pages and links first. Low volume, low KD A quick win, especially if the searcher is ready to buy. Low volume, high KD Usually skip it. For a business that sells to other businesses, a small search can be worth a lot. A term searched 50 times a month by buyers may beat one searched 5,000 times a month by students. Volume and KD do not show this. Look at intent too. End of chapter 6 Next: How to check keyword difficulty step by step → 07 Chapter 7 · 2 min How to check keyword difficulty step by step You can read the tool’s score in seconds. A good check takes about 10 minutes more. Follow these steps. Step 1: Get the tool’s score Enter the keyword in a tool such as Semrush, Ahrefs, Moz or a free checker. Write down the KD and monthly volume. Step 2: Read the first page of results Search the keyword in Google. Look at the top 10 results. Ask: Are they big brands or small sites? Are they guides, product pages, lists or tools? Is there an AI answer, video or map above them? Step 3: Match the intent Search intent is the reason behind the search. If every result is a how-to guide, a sales page will not rank. Plan a page of the same type, then make it better. Step 4: Look for weak spots Signs that a keyword may be easier than its score: Old pages that have not been updated in years Thin pages that skim the topic Small or little-known sites in the top 10 Forum threads or social posts ranking on page one Step 5: Count the links needed Open the top few pages in a link tool. See how many sites link to each. If the top pages have only a handful of links, you may need few. If they have hundreds, plan for outreach. Step 6: Decide Choose the keyword, or pick a more specific version of it (a long-tail keyword). A long-tail keyword is a longer, narrower phrase, such as “keyword difficulty for new websites” instead of “keyword difficulty.” These usually have lower scores and clearer intent. End of chapter 7 Next: A worked example → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min A worked example This example is illustrative. The numbers are made up to show the method. A small software company wants to write about “email scheduling.” It checks three keywords in its SEO tool. Keyword Monthly searches KD What the first page shows email scheduling 9,000 68 Large software brands and a news site email scheduling for small teams 800 35 Mix of guides and a few product pages how to schedule emails in a shared inbox 300 18 Help pages and small blogs The company has a young site with few links. It picks the third keyword first. It writes a clear how-to guide with screenshots. Once that page earns visits and a few links, it writes the second guide and links the two pages. Later it can take on the main keyword. This is the usual pattern: win the easy keywords, build trust, then move up. End of chapter 8 Next: Strategies for each difficulty level → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Strategies for each difficulty level Low difficulty (0 to 30) Write a complete, accurate page that fits the intent. Add a clear title and headings. Link to it from your other pages. Often this is enough. Medium difficulty (31 to 60) You need a page that is clearly better than what ranks: more detail, fresh examples, original images or data. Then earn some links with outreach, guest articles or a useful free tool. High difficulty (61 to 100) Treat it as a project. Build a group of pages around the topic, a topic cluster, so the site shows depth. Earn strong links over time. Do not expect fast results. End of chapter 9 Next: How accurate is keyword difficulty? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min How accurate is keyword difficulty? It is a useful guide, not a promise. Reasons it can mislead you: Tools disagree. Each uses its own formula and data. It leans on links. A page with few links but excellent content can still win. It ignores your site. Ahrefs says its score shows how hard it is for the average site and does not account for your own site’s authority. A site with strong authority in a topic ranks more easily than the score suggests. Semrush offers a separate personal keyword difficulty score for this reason. Results change. Rankings and scores move, so recheck before you commit. Intent can matter more. A page that does not fit what people want will fail at any score. Results are personal. Location and search history can change what you see. Use KD to shortlist. Use your own reading of the results to decide. End of chapter 10 Next: Which tools show keyword difficulty? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Which tools show keyword difficulty? Most keyword tools show a KD score next to each term. They differ in name, scale and method, so pick one and stay with it when you compare keywords. Type of tool Examples Good to know Full SEO suites Semrush, Ahrefs, Moz, Similarweb Paid. They show KD, volume, the top pages and link counts in one place. Free checkers Free tiers and keyword tools from the same brands, plus other small tools Limited searches a day, and fewer details. Fine for a first look. Google Search Console Google’s free tool for site owners It does not show KD. It shows the searches you already get impressions for, which helps you spot keywords you almost rank for. Names also differ. Some tools call the score “keyword difficulty,” some “keyword competition,” and some “SEO difficulty.” Check the tool’s help page to see what it counts. End of chapter 11 Next: Does Google use keyword difficulty? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min Does Google use keyword difficulty? No. Keyword difficulty is not a Google metric. Semrush says so on its own page: it is an estimate created by SEO tools to help you compare keywords. Google does not publish a difficulty score, and its ranking systems do not use one. The score only summarizes what a tool can see about the pages that rank today. End of chapter 12 Next: Why do Ahrefs and Semrush give different scores? → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min Why do Ahrefs and Semrush give different scores? They measure different things. Ahrefs looks at referring domains to the top 10 pages. Its scale is not linear: each value on it matches an estimated number of referring domains a page needs to reach page one, so the jump from KD 60 to KD 70 costs far more links than the jump from 10 to 20. Semrush blends links with domain authority, link type, search volume and search result features, and it uses medians. Search Engine Land’s guide to keyword difficulty adds that Moz uses its own authority scores together with expected click-through rates. The result is that one keyword can score 20 in one tool and 60 in another, and each can be reasonable for what it measures. Pick one tool and compare keywords inside it. Do not compare a score from one tool with a score from another. End of chapter 13 Next: Can you still rank for a high-difficulty keyword? → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min Can you still rank for a high-difficulty keyword? Yes, but plan for it. Ahrefs says its score is meant to help you estimate the resources needed, not to discourage you, and that if a keyword is vital to your business you may still pursue it. A hard keyword needs a stronger page, more links and more time. It can also hide weak spots. Ahrefs notes that an average of referring domains can mask problems in the results, such as old content, brands with low authority or thin pages, and these are openings you can use. A practical approach is to win the easier keywords around the topic first. They build links, traffic and proof of expertise. Then take on the hard head term from a stronger position. There is no standard time frame. We found no reliable public study on how long a high-difficulty keyword takes, so we do not quote one. Track your own rankings and learn your own pace. End of chapter 14 Next: Keyword difficulty, keyword competition and paid competition → 15 Chapter 15 · 1 min Keyword difficulty, keyword competition and paid competition These terms get mixed up. They are not the same. Keyword difficulty: how hard it is to rank in the normal (organic) results. Paid competition: how many advertisers bid on the term in Google Ads. A term can have many bidders and still be easy to rank for. Cost per click (CPC): what advertisers pay for one click. A high CPC often means the term has commercial value. Use all three together. A keyword with low KD and a high CPC is often a strong target, because it is winnable and buyers search for it. End of chapter 15 Next: What is personal keyword difficulty? → 16 Chapter 16 · 1 min What is personal keyword difficulty? The score in a tool does not know your site. Your own chance depends on: Your site’s links and trust. Strong sites can rank for harder terms. Your topic fit. A site that covers a topic in depth ranks more easily for related terms. Your content. A page with real examples, clear answers and good structure beats a thin page. Your resources. Link building takes time and budget. A simple way to adjust: compare your site’s strength to the sites in the top 10. If your site looks like the weaker ones, you have a fair chance. If every result is a giant brand, the real difficulty for you is higher than the score. End of chapter 16 Next: How to build a keyword plan from KD → 17 Chapter 17 · 1 min How to build a keyword plan from KD Use difficulty to sort your list into waves. This turns a long list of keywords into a calendar. Collect 50 to 100 keywords for one topic, from your tool, Search Console, customer questions and competitor pages. Add volume and KD for each in a spreadsheet. Mark the intent as learn, compare or buy. Group by topic. Put similar keywords in one group. One page can often serve a whole group. Sort into waves. Wave 1 is easy and relevant. Wave 2 is medium. Wave 3 is hard but valuable. Write wave 1 first , link the pages together, then review results after two to three months. Here is a small example of the sheet: Keyword Volume KD Intent Wave what is a content audit 2,400 28 Learn 1 content audit template 1,300 31 Learn / Buy 1 content audit checklist 880 22 Learn 1 content audit tools 720 46 Compare 2 content audit services 390 52 Buy 2 content strategy 12,000 71 Learn 3 The numbers in this table are made up to show the layout. Use your own data from your tool. End of chapter 17 Next: A second worked example: counting the links you need → 18 Chapter 18 · 1 min A second worked example: counting the links you need This example is also illustrative. Say you want to rank for a phrase with KD 45. You open the top five results in a link tool and note how many different sites link to each page. Rank Type of site Sites linking to the page 1 Large brand 140 2 Mid-size blog 60 3 Software company 35 4 Small agency 12 5 Niche blog 9 The lower results have 9 to 12 linking sites. That suggests you may reach page one with a better page and roughly 10 good links. Reaching the first spot would need far more. This reading is a rough guide, not a rule, but it is more useful than the score alone because it shows the target in real numbers. Plan how you will earn those links: a useful tool or template, original data from your own work, expert quotes, or guest articles on relevant sites. Do not buy links. Google’s spam policies treat buying links to pass ranking signals as link spam. End of chapter 18 Next: How to improve your odds on a hard keyword → 19 Chapter 19 · 1 min How to improve your odds on a hard keyword You cannot change the score, but you can change your chances. Cover the topic fully. Answer the main question, then the follow-up questions people ask next. Add what others lack. A worked example, a checklist, a template, a simple diagram or your own data. Show your experience. Say who wrote the page and why they know the topic. Google’s guidance on helpful content asks for first-hand experience and expertise where it fits. Build topic depth. Publish related pages and link them to each other so the site looks like a reliable source on the topic. Fix the basics. Fast loading, a clear title, short paragraphs and working mobile layout. Refresh it. Update examples and facts every few months. End of chapter 19 Next: Keyword difficulty for local and B2B businesses → 20 Chapter 20 · 1 min Keyword difficulty for local and B2B businesses The score works differently outside big consumer topics. Local searches such as “dentist in Leeds” show a map and local listings. Your Google Business Profile, reviews and location pages matter more than the KD number. B2B searches often have low volume and low KD, but high value. A page that answers a buyer’s detailed question can bring in a few strong enquiries a month. New products or topics may have no volume data. Use customer questions and sales calls to find terms, and test with one page. End of chapter 20 Next: Keyword difficulty and AI search → 21 Chapter 21 · 1 min Keyword difficulty and AI search Many searches now show an AI answer above the normal results. This changes what a ranking is worth. A page may rank well and still get fewer clicks if the AI answer satisfies the searcher. Two studies show the size of the effect, with limits. The Pew Research Center tracked 900 US adults in March 2025. Users clicked a regular result in 8% of visits to pages with an AI summary and 15% of visits to pages without one. GrowthSRC studied more than 200,000 keywords on 30 or more sites and reported that the click rate for position 1 fell from 28% to 19% between 2024 and 2025. That is a sample of client sites, not all of Google, so use it as a direction and not as a rule. Two things help. First, aim for questions where people want more than a short answer, such as comparisons, checklists and worked examples. Second, write clear, direct answers near the top of your page. These can be picked up by AI tools as well as by Google’s own features. End of chapter 21 Next: How to check keyword difficulty for free → 22 Chapter 22 · 1 min How to check keyword difficulty for free You do not need a paid tool to get a useful first answer. Try this: Use a free checker. Many keyword tools give a few free searches a day with a KD score and volume. Read the results page. Count the big brands in the top 10. Seven or more large sites is a hard page. Check the page titles. If few titles use your exact phrase, you may have room to win with a clear, matching title. Use “People also ask” and related searches. They show the follow-up questions you can answer to beat thinner pages. Use Search Console. If your site already shows impressions for a phrase at positions 8 to 20, a small update may lift it. This is the cheapest win, because Google already links the page to the topic. The free route gives you a rough read in 10 minutes. A paid tool saves time when you have a long list. End of chapter 22 Next: How often should you recheck keyword difficulty? → 23 Chapter 23 · 1 min How often should you recheck keyword difficulty? Scores and results change. Recheck your target keywords every three to six months, and before you update an older page. If new big brands have entered the results, or the page types have changed, adjust the plan. Also track your own rankings after you publish. If a page sits on page two for several months, look at the top results again. You may need more depth, better links or a closer match to intent. Keyword difficulty is where you begin, not the whole job. End of chapter 23 Next: Common mistakes → 24 Chapter 24 · 1 min Common mistakes Choosing only by volume. A big number means big competition. Trusting one score. Check the real results page. Ignoring intent. The wrong page type will not rank. Chasing only easy keywords. Some easy terms have no value for your business. Never rechecking. Review your targets every few months. End of chapter 24 Next: A quick checklist → 25 Chapter 25 · 1 min A quick checklist Note the KD and monthly volume in one tool. Read the top 10 results and note the page types. Check how strong the ranking sites are. Look for old, thin or weak pages. Count the links the top pages have. Pick a long-tail version if the main term is too hard. Match the intent, then write a better page. End of chapter 25 Next: Final thoughts → 26 Chapter 26 · 1 min Final thoughts Keyword difficulty will not tell you whether you will rank. It tells you how steep the climb looks. Pair it with search volume, intent and a look at the real results, and you can choose keywords that fit your site today. Start with the ones you can win, and build from there. Back matter Glossary A to Z B Backlink A link from another website to your page. K Keyword difficulty (KD) A score, usually 0 to 100, that estimates how hard it is to rank on page one for a keyword. L Long-tail keyword A longer, narrower search phrase with lower volume and usually lower difficulty. S Search intent The reason behind a search: to learn, to compare or to buy. T Topic cluster A group of related pages that link to one another to show depth on a subject. Questions FAQs What is keyword difficulty in SEO? Keyword difficulty is a score, usually from 0 to 100, that estimates how hard it is to rank on the first page of Google for a keyword. Higher means more competition. It is calculated by SEO tools, not by Google. What is a good keyword difficulty score? It depends on your site. New sites do best with scores of 0 to 30. Sites with more links and trust can aim for 31 to 60 or higher. Check the keywords you already rank for to find your own reach. How is keyword difficulty calculated? Each tool studies the pages that rank in the top 10 and scores how strong they are, often using backlinks, domain and page authority, content quality and search results features. The formulas are private and differ by tool. Is keyword difficulty accurate? It is a useful estimate, not a promise. Tools disagree, many lean heavily on links and none know your own site. Use it to make a shortlist and then read the real results. Is a low keyword difficulty always better? No. Some easy keywords bring visitors who will never buy. Pick keywords that are winnable and relevant to your business, and check the search intent. What is the difference between keyword difficulty and search volume? Search volume is how many times a month people search for a term. Keyword difficulty is how hard it is to rank for it. You need both to choose a keyword. Can I check keyword difficulty for free? Yes. Free checkers show a score and volume for a few searches a day. You can also read the top 10 results yourself and use Google Search Console to find phrases you almost rank for. How do I rank for a high-difficulty keyword? Build a group of related pages, make the main page clearly better than those that rank, earn links from relevant sites, and expect it to take months. Start with easier related keywords to build trust. What is long-tail keyword difficulty? Long-tail keywords are longer, more specific phrases. They usually have lower difficulty and clearer intent, which makes them a good starting point for newer sites. How often should I recheck keyword difficulty? Every three to six months, and before you update an older page. Results and scores change as new pages are published and links are earned. Does Google use keyword difficulty? No. Keyword difficulty is an estimate created by SEO tools. Google does not publish a difficulty score. Semrush says on its own page that it is not an official Google metric. Why is keyword difficulty different in Ahrefs and Semrush? They measure different things. Ahrefs scores referring domains to the top 10 pages. Semrush blends referring domains, authority, link type, search volume and search result features. Compare keywords inside one tool, not across tools. Evidence Sources Semrush: How Keyword Difficulty is calculated and what the scores mean Semrush: What is keyword difficulty (KD%) and the six levels Semrush: Semrush Keyword Difficulty, now more accurate than any other tool (formula weights, 2021) Ahrefs: Keyword Difficulty, how to estimate your chances to rank Ahrefs: 96.55% of content gets no traffic from Google (December 2023) Backlinko: We analyzed 4 million Google search results, organic CTR Pew Research Center: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears (July 2025) GrowthSRC: Google organic CTR 2025, a study of 200K keywords Google Search Central: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content Google Search Central: Spam policies for Google web search Search Engine Land: Keyword Difficulty Explained, How to Win Ahrefs: Free Keyword Difficulty Checker (how the score scale works) Jamil Ahmed Founder and CEO, Reinforce Lab SEO & AI Search Consultant, Founder & CEO of Reinforce Lab. h1_text: What Is Martech? Why Need Digital Marketing Technology Stack?
lede: If you run a business, you may be familiar with Marketing Technology Stack or know What Martech Is.
copy_text: Home Blog Digital Marketing What Is Martech? Why Need Digital Marketing Technology… Explainer Digital Marketing What Is Martech? Why Need Digital Marketing Technology Stack? R Reinforce Lab team Published 3 Jan 2025 Updated 16 Apr 2025 If you run a business, you may be familiar with Marketing Technology Stack or know What Martech Is. And if you don’t know but want to, this blog is for you. I will walk you through the entire process to make technology and marketing strategy less complex for you. Digital marketing technology stack is a process that every company owner has to follow when their business grows, and the company expands. Because it becomes difficult to manage all the business operations and tasks at the same time. Marketing Technology solutions or mar-tech allows you to maintain and manage all the company tasks and run the marketing campaigns smoothly. When the team of your company and business scales, it is essential to have a Marketing Tech Stack that simplifies your daily operations. According to ZDNET , the number of marketing professionals using AI martech grew 186% from 2018 to 2021 . Research from American Marketing Association shows that about 70% of sales-as-a-service (SaaS) and technology companies use integrated martech tools. So, you may realize the value of this martech technology. Imagine that this is your genie from Aladdin who will oversee all of the tasks if you want to expand your company in a better and more well-maintained manner. In this blog, I will cover all you need about marketing technology (martech) and show you how to create a marketing technology stack that will grow with your company. What Is Martech? Why Need Digital Marketing Technology Stack? What is a martech stack? Or what does martech mean? Before knowing the answers, let’s check if you see the definition of technology. Technology is the application of scientific knowledge to improve and modify the human environment and way of living. After answering the definition of technology, it is required to understand the value of technology and marketing strategy in our life and business. In today’s world, we are surrounded by technology. You can see technology everywhere. Even we are unable to do any work on our own without the help of technology. Because they have made our life easier and simpler. We can manage to complete multiple tasks with the help of tech products. The same goes for the professional sector. The business field is no different from our daily life. Martech marketing technology is the professional term for implementing software technology or AI in business and managing the official tasks by marketing and sales. Marketing team uses numerous numbers of Marketing technology tools to save time, as these tools frequently automate and streamline operations. They also help to analyze and track the success of their efforts. Marketing tech tools like SEMRush for keyword research, CMS hub for content management, Hootsuite for social media marketing, Mediasmart for advertising, and many others. Marketers use these technology and marketing strategies in order to make their tasks easy to complete and done perfectly. The collection of these tools is called mar tech stack. That means the collection of software technologies and martech platforms that marketers and sales teams use to maintain, track and optimize their marketing and information technology strategies and tactics is mar tech stack or marketing technology stack. In the next topic, I will show you some marketing technology solutions that will help you to learn about martech software companies and martech industry. Marketing Technology Examples You have got the technology and marketing technology definition. Also, I have told you about the digital marketing technology stack. Now, how about showing you the martech categories with martech products? You will get to know the tools and their usage from these examples. So, let’s go for it! Martech tools of the digital marketing technology stack- 1. Management Tools Company management covers a broad area with product management, content management, customer relationships management, team management, and many more. So, it becomes difficult to handle all this management when a company expands. Data management tools, data integration tools, data asset management, etc., and different martech tools are used to manage a company’s data. Companies also use SQL-based query tools to manage the customer database, where they gather and maintain all the information collected from their customers. ClickUp, Wrike, monday.com, Smartsheet, and Teamwork, are the marketing tools that most companies use for their marketing-related tasks. For example, If you want to manage marketing campaigns, documents and clients, then you can use ClickUp. You can use Teamwork software if you want collaboration and budget management. 2. Social Media Management Tools Modern martech stack includes different tools to manage, maintain and monitor social media posts and activities. These tools help you schedule posts, record customers’ responses and manage all the social media posts in one place. Buffer, Hootsuite, sprout social, and agora pulse are some social media post-management tools. These tools help simplify managing all the content on social media platforms and engaging the users. You just need to prepare the content plan and structure then these tools will maintain the calendar. 3. Analytic tools In today’s world, organizations rely on analytic tools more than any other martech. Because they won’t be able to increase business growth until they research correctly. So, this is the most critical and challenging task for a company. If this analysis is incorrect, no other technology and marketing strategy will work. Google analytics, web analytics tools, customer analytics tools, etc., and different types of marketing technology solutions or tools are available to do the task for you. Google analytic tool is a free website provided by Google. You can use this for tracking your audience. You can Identify your website’s visitors’ origins, how they found you online, how long they stayed on your site, etc. 4. Automation Tools With marketing automation solutions, you may gather helpful information that you can utilize to customize marketing efforts and boost conversion rates. Streamlining their procedures, also supports businesses in becoming more efficient. HubSpot, ManyChat, Omnisend, Marketo, Drip, etc., are some marketing automation tools. Suppose you have an eCommerce website and want to offer powerful workflows with pre-built templates. Omnisend will help you to handle multiple channels within the same automated workflow. SMS, Facebook messenger, push notifications, and others. Omnisend employs templates and a user-friendly visual builder to make it simple and quick to create workflows, forms, landing pages, pop-ups, and emails. 5. Content Management Tools The content martech landscape is expanding yearly. There are numerous tools for content marketing. Some are cheap, and some are pretty inexpensive. These tools also fulfill a wide variety of needs, including content creation, promotion, and optimization. Though content creation is not a job that tools can do only without humans. But content technology marketing solutions can help you do the job more efficiently. Semrush, Ahref, and Ubersuggest are some examples of content management tools. In today’s world, creating only essential content won’t work. You have to do proper research before starting to write. You can take help from ahref. It will provide you with complete keyword research on the specific topic you want to write on. After seeing all these tools, I know you became perplexed and believed it would be simpler to create your business strategy plans and workflows and execute activities independently. But if you try to get involved in every firm’s management, it will get quite crowded. Therefore, using these tools to manage things is always preferable. Now let us move to our next topic so that you can learn how to market a tech company. Technology And Marketing Strategy According to research, the number of martech solutions grew from 150 in 2011 to 9,500 in 2021 — a 6,000%+ increase . From this data, you can guess how drastically the Martech stack is increasing daily. But why? Why are individuals using these tools so frequently? Because they are familiar with how marketing technology martech completes all official responsibilities flawlessly and quickly. They also monitor the development of martech marketing. Do you know what role a CRM can play in an effective martech stack? In the Martech world, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is a top-rated martech tool. CRM is a martech software that is used to manage the relationship with the customer. If you integrate with your crm software, then you will be able to locate your leads in the funnel. This tool is very common in B2B martech stacks focusing on lead generation. Like this CRM software, there are many other martech solutions for different martech platforms. These tools are also used to market tech companies. Let me explain this part a little more elaborately so you can understand it clearly. 5 Marketing strategies with martech tools to market a tech company- 1. Content marketing with CMS System Tech companies usually produce products to solve the problems that people face in daily life. In this case, content is king. From videos, podcasts to guides and blogs, content is the main ingredient that finds out people’s pain points and solves them. So, high quality content is a must thing for tech companies. To ensure the quality you can use a content management system (CMS). CMS helps marketers to create, optimize, manage and update all types of content like web content, blog, email content, etc. Even CMS also tests the content before and after publishing the content. 2. Email Marketing It is one of the oldest marketing strategies that still works great for many companies. It is a way of direct communication with both existing and new prospects and customers. Email enables tech companies to reach clients directly and advertise new products or notify them of significant updates. If you want to implement an email marketing strategy for your company or product then you can use ESP or an email service provider. ESP will allow you to deliver email marketing campaigns to specific recipients. 3. Social Media Marketing Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and LinkedIn these social media networks have huge potential audiences and are completely free to use. Building an audience, creating connections, and utilizing content from other platforms, like your website, are all possible here. However, it is very challenging to perfectly maintain all of a company’s social media sites and posts. Because of this, the digital marketing technology stack includes tools for managing and keeping an eye on social media posts and activity. 4. Influencer marketing Influencer marketing is a way of letting people know about your product or service through a public figure who they trust. People like to follow these faces and take their advice before purchasing any product. So, it can help in generating more traffic and increase credibility. To maintain this strategy more efficiently, you can use user-generated content (UGC) and customer relationship management (CRM) system to manage customers’ information and data. 5. Pay-Per-Click (PPC) Ads PPC is an advertising strategy that helps you to get a higher ranking in Google and other search engines. Companies bids for specific keywords to generate more website visitors and clicks on their website or landing page. If you want to apply this strategy to your business, ensure you have researched customers’ needs properly. For that, you need a tool that will test and analyze customers’ behavior and help you to track the improvement in web traffic and clicks. Marketing technology solutions there are various types of analytics tools that you can use for this task. Mixpanel is one of them. This tool will help you track all the visitors’ activities and keep a record of them. I hope you will not suffer for choosing Technology Marketing Solutions anymore because you know what it is martech? What Is Martech Example? and also their applications. Now, let’s move to an exciting topic, and that is “What Is Adtech And Martech”. What Is Martech And Adtech I have covered all most everything regarding martech tools, martech roles, technology platform definition, marketing technology platforms and others. Now I will discuss martech and adtech. The difference between these terms lies in their names. Martech means marketing technology and adtech means advertising technology. Demand Side Platforms (DSP), Supply Side platforms (SSP), ad exchange, etc. are some examples of adtech. With these tools help, companies can focus on a target audience. They are employed to influence consumer behavior by promoting offerings. Martech or marketing technologies are used to execute a comprehensive digital marketing plan. Martech refers to all of the technology used from lead acquisition through the sales funnel until conversion. Some marketing technologies include email marketing tools, content marketing tools, web analytic tools, and social media management tools. These tools are designed to help businesses understand their audience in a better manner. You track sign-ups and conversions through multiple tools and then use that data to determine which topics are received better by your audience. Though martech and adtech are both designed to make the work of digital marketers easier and more straightforward, they are two different things. I will try to explain that to you shortly. Martech Systems & Services Marketing is relying more and more on technology. Because MarTech is getting more advanced and allows firms to keep up with the always-changing market nature, the marketing environment is constantly changing. To put it briefly, marketing technology is crucial to developing contemporary marketing. Marketing technology is crucial since it focuses on all aspects of execution demands. It makes it possible for marketers to scale their campaigns holistically through technology. Additionally, Marketing Technology Solutions are crucial since they enhance our ability to interact and communicate with colleagues and clients. The relationships you develop with your customers will benefit from a good snowball effect as these B2B and B2C relationships improve. Wrapping Up – What Is Martech? Why Need Digital Marketing Technology Stack? If you understand the relationship between technology and marketing strategy, then the digital marketing technology stack will not be a complex thing for you. While carefully and efficiently marketing your business might take time, MarTech solutions accelerate the process and increase the effectiveness of all marketing initiatives. Marketing technology assists you in achieving marketing objectives in a more efficient, precise, and user-friendly manner at every stage, from strategy to creative execution and everything in between. copy_text: Home Blog Search Engine Optimization What is technical SEO and why is it… Explainer Search Engine Optimization What is technical SEO and why is it important? R Reinforce Lab team Published 22 Feb 2025 Updated 13 Apr 2025 Are you wondering What is technical SEO and why is it important? You are in the right place for the answer. When we talk about “technical SEO,” we discuss ways to make a website’s pages appear more in search engine results pages. While technically optimizing a website, the goal is to make a website load faster, be more accessible for search engines to find, and be easier for people to understand. Technical SEO is part of on-page SEO, which focuses on improving your website’s features to get it to show up higher in search results. This article will focus on what is technical SEO and why is it important. What is technical SEO and why is it important? An Insight into Technical SEO Technical SEO is an integral part of any SEO strategy. There are a lot of different parts to checklists of technical SEO that help people evaluate and rank the content and structure of a website. When you do technical SEO, you make your website’s structure easier for search engines to crawl and index so that they don’t have to do a lot of work. It will also talk about sitemaps and how fast your site is. Also, learn about URL structure and schema and navigate your site. Because it changes your website’s code, even though structured data is about content, it is called technical SEO. Any on-site, technical, and non-content element of your website that is not part of another domain is included in technical SEO. It can also be defined as anything that makes optimizing your site’s indexing for search engine results easier. Being included in the index is more important than boosting one’s ranking. These factors are more than just a yes or no checkbox, and enhancing them can positively impact your total score. First of all, let us know about the essential components of technical SEO. Vital Components of Technical SEO End of the day, you want to improve your website’s search engine rankings, get more traffic to it, and make more sales. To reach that goal, you have to fix all of the flaws. If you ask us which of the following are important components of technical SEO, we will always go for all the points we have mentioned here: With the help of a crawl report, find out what’s wrong with your site and find out insight into crawling and indexing Start by running a crawl report on your site. Some of your site’s flaws can be found through a crawl report or a site review. The tool will tell you if there is a lot of the same content on your site, if the page takes a long time to load, or if there are no H1 or H2 tags. Many people ask, “why is a technical SEO audit important?”. It is because a monthly site audit is necessary to ensure the long-term success of your website. Performing regular SEO audits is crucial for ensuring your SEO strategy is current. The audit will reveal the issues, allowing you to fix them and reclaim lost visitors. It would help if you also remained careful about your post of not being a duplicate content Check the status codes of HTTPS to see if they work or not Search engines and users won’t get to it if your site still has URLs that start with HTTP. You’ll get HTTP status codes 4xx and 5xx from them instead. If your site doesn’t have HTTPS, it might not appear in the search results. SEMrush says that this is now a significant ranking factor. It looked at how hard it was to find specific keywords on search engines like Google, Bing, Firefox, and many more. XML sitemap Google rates web pages, not websites; therefore, XML Sitemaps are vital for SEO since they make it easier for the search engine to find your site’s pages. Having an XML Sitemap is a great way to boost your search engine rankings thus, we highly recommend it. Check how quickly the site loads It would help if you also kept an eye on how quickly your site loads regarding technical SEO issues. A report from SEMrush says that 23 percent of websites have slow page loads times. Site speed can affect two more critical ranking factors: bounce rate and time on page. This is because site speed is about how users feel when they visit. Having an SSL certificate installed on your website is now the norm. Your site’s security and trustworthiness are demonstrated to site visitors. You’ll also see an increase in your search engine ranks. Seeing how long it takes your site to load on a mobile device will help you figure out how long it takes your site to load. Make sure that your website is compatible with mobile devices To improve your web page’s search engine rankings and technical SEO, your site must be able to be viewed on a smartphone or tablet. Google’s Mobile-Friendly Test makes it easy to see if your site is suitable for people who use their phones. Then, type in your URL and see if it passes the test. The last step is to make sure your robots.txt file hasn’t been changed in a long time. A meta description should be long enough to make people want to read it Check to see if meta descriptions are the right length and don’t have the same information repeatedly. Even if your site doesn’t get traffic from search engine results pages (SERPs), you can still improve your CTR. Why is technical SEO important? Below, we have discussed the importance of implementing Technical SEO in your posts and website. We hope that we will know why technical SEO is essential by going through this. It Makes sure your audience sees you on a lot of different platforms As long as you write your material in a way that makes it easy for search engines to find, index, and show it, Google, Bing, and other search engines can do this very quickly. By making your audience more visible on many different platforms, you have a better chance of making more sales and getting more people to interact with your content. It would help with technical SEO for digital marketing to ensure that your website is easy to use and free of technical difficulties that hinder it from ranking and understanding by search engines. It has no broken links We’ve talked before about how annoying slow websites can be. Getting to a page that doesn’t exist may be more annoying than a lengthy page that doesn’t work. A 404 error page will be shown to visitors if they click on a internal link that takes them to a page that isn’t there. It looks like your carefully planned user experience has been ruined! Google has a better chance of ranking your site well in search results if it can easily read your content. This is a virtual extension of the previous argument. Featured snippets and “People also ask” sections are part of this. Ensures Better Display and Layout of Social Media As a result of this automation, you won’t have to worry about your material being put up on social media in the wrong way. In this case, your social media picture preview will use the available images on the page if you haven’t set up which image field will be used to show the preview on social media. If you automate a specific field on your social media accounts, you can control what people see when they return to your accounts. How technical SEO is important for enterprise ? To keep an eye on and keep up with organic rankings, enterprises should hire an SEO called “enterprise SEO.” they will work to ensure technical SEO for the website and blog posts. Large businesses will have more SEO problems because they already have a lot of pages, backlinks, and other things. Companies that are big and well-known tend to have a lot of brand recognition because of their size and popularity. You can’t delete or reroute pages linked to or have a lot of page authority because doing so would make them less critical. This is why it might be tempting to do this. In addition, you need to keep this information up to date and relevant. As you might expect, the more difficult it is to do this as the company grows more prominent. That is why Technical SEO is important for enterprises to keep their business up-to-date, and people will be able to find them easily. Wrapping Up Overall, a website’s technical SEO helps search engines find and index your website, which allows you to get more people to visit your site. Having a user-friendly site that loads quickly and is easy to use keeps people on your site longer. We hope you have understood by now why is technical SEO important and what goes into it. We all know that Google is the world’s largest search engine on the internet. 90% of all search queries are conducted globally using Google. Google has created a smart algorithm that can recognize the websites that provide a good user experience and also remove those websites that are engaged in spamming, plagiarism, etc. such activities. For websites that deliver helpful information and provide a good user experience, Google makes them rank on their search result and helps them get organic traffic. But this process of ranking is not that easy. To deal with the factors that will help your website to rank higher that’s SEO. SEO or Search Engine Optimization is the set of tactics that helps to optimize the user experience and increase a website or page’s position in the search engine results pages. Like Google, another world’s most famous search engine on the internet is YouTube. Do you know the best part? YouTube has its own search engine to make it simple for its viewers to find the channels and videos they are looking for. Those strategies that help rank your YouTube channels and videos rank higher are called YouTube SEO. SEO strategy for YouTube plays a significant role in optimizing your YouTube channels, videos, etc. To make it rank high in their own search engine and gather a good amount of website traffic.
