For Google it is ordinary SEO plus clear facts, answer-first pages with sourced evidence, a presence on the sites AI answers cite, and a monthly check of what the models say about you. No one can promise a place in AI answers. 01 LLM SEO, LLMO, GEO and AEO describe one family of work. Google says optimizing for AI search is still SEO. 02 Models know you from training and from retrieval. You can change retrieval-based answers faster than training. 03 Adding citations, quotations and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40% in a Princeton-led benchmark. It is a test, not a guarantee. 04 Ahrefs found cited content was 25.7% fresher than regular results across 17 million citations. That is a correlation. 05 SparkToro found under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice, so measure a rate, not a rank. 06 Google says llms.txt, chunking and special markup are not needed for Google Search. 07 Start with access, facts and answer-first pages, then build real third-party presence and measure monthly. LLM SEO is the work of making your brand and your pages easy for large language models to find, understand and cite when they answer questions. It is also called LLM optimization or LLMO. It is not a new trick. For Google, it is ordinary SEO plus a few extra jobs: clear facts, quotable pages, a good presence on other sites, and a way to check what the models say about you. This guide explains what LLM SEO is, how LLMs choose what to cite, and what the evidence shows. It also covers what Google says you can ignore, and gives a nine-step plan, a worked example and an honest answer on how long it takes. We cite only studies and documents we could read at the source, and we say when a finding is a correlation, a vendor view or a single test. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is LLM SEO? LLM SEO means improving how often and how accurately large language models mention your brand, recommend your products and cite your pages. The goal is not a rank. The goal is to be part of the answer when someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity or Google’s AI features about your category. A language model can know about you in two ways. The first is training: the model learned from text in its training data, collected before it was released, so what it says reflects what was on the web then. The second is retrieval: when the model needs fresh facts, it searches the web, reads some pages and writes an answer from them. Google calls the second method retrieval-augmented generation, or grounding, and describes it as relying on its core Search ranking systems to find relevant, up-to-date pages. Most of the work you can control today is about retrieval, because you can change a page this week but not a model that was trained last year. End of chapter 1 Next: LLM SEO, LLMO, GEO, AEO and AI SEO: what is the difference? → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min LLM SEO, LLMO, GEO, AEO and AI SEO: what is the difference? These names overlap, and different writers use them in different ways. The table shows the common use. Term Common meaning LLM SEO or LLMO Getting a brand and its pages mentioned and cited by large language models and chatbots GEO (generative engine optimization) The same goal, framed around generative search engines. See our GEO guide . AEO (answer engine optimization) Writing so that answer boxes and assistants can quote you. See AEO vs SEO . AI SEO A loose term for any of the above, and sometimes for using AI tools to do SEO Google takes a plain view. It says optimizing for generative AI search is optimizing for the search experience, and so it is still SEO. It also advises caution with third-party “AEO” or “GEO” advice. We use the terms as one family of work and write “LLM SEO” for the part that targets language models. Our comparison in GEO vs SEO covers what changes and what stays the same. End of chapter 2 Next: How is LLM SEO different from traditional SEO? → Reinforce Lab service · LLM Optimization Want LLM SEO set up and measured for you? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See LLM optimization → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 1 min How is LLM SEO different from traditional SEO? Traditional SEO aims to rank pages in search results and win clicks. LLM SEO aims to get your brand named and your pages cited inside an answer. They share a base, and a site that is weak at traditional SEO is rarely strong at LLM SEO. Area Traditional SEO LLM SEO Goal Rankings and clicks Mentions and citations in answers Query style Short keywords Longer, conversational prompts and follow-ups Authority signals Backlinks, content quality Backlinks and quality, plus brand mentions and consistent facts across other sites Content Pages that match intent Pages with clear headings, answer-first passages and sourced evidence Measurement Rank, traffic, conversions Mention rate, citation rate and share of voice across a fixed prompt set End of chapter 3 Next: How do LLMs choose what to cite? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min How do LLMs choose what to cite? Nobody outside the AI companies knows the exact rules, and they do not publish them. What the companies do say is limited. Google says its AI features use a technique called query fan-out: the model splits one question into several related searches and gathers pages for each. Its example is a question about fixing a lawn full of weeds, which fans out into searches on herbicides, chemical-free removal and prevention. So a page can be retrieved for a question it never named. From the documents we read, three things seem to matter. These are our reading and not a published formula: Retrievability. The page must be crawlable, indexed and readable in the HTML. For Google, a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. Other tools use their own crawlers or search indexes. Relevance and clarity. The page must answer the question, or one of the fan-out questions, in a passage that makes sense alone. Trust. The page and the brand should look reliable, with named sources, named authors, current facts and agreement from other sites. End of chapter 4 Next: What does the evidence say? → 05 Chapter 5 · 2 min What does the evidence say? There is less hard evidence than the volume of advice suggests. These are the main studies and documents we found, with their limits. Adding evidence can raise visibility, in a test. Researchers from Princeton, IIT Delhi and others built a benchmark called GEO-bench of 10,000 queries and tested nine ways to change content. They reported that adding citations, quotations from relevant sources and statistics boosted source visibility by up to 40% in their tests, and that the methods worked on Perplexity with gains of up to 37%. The effect varied by domain. It is a controlled study from 2024, published at the KDD 2024 conference, not a guarantee for your site. Fresher pages are cited more. Ahrefs analyzed 17 million citations across seven AI search platforms. It found that content cited in AI answers was 25.7% fresher than content in regular results, and that assistants showed a 13.1% preference for more recently updated content. That is a correlation from one vendor’s data set. Answers vary. SparkToro had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s AI features 2,961 times. There was less than a 1 in 100 chance of the same list of brands twice and about a 1 in 1,000 chance of the same order. So measure a rate across many prompts, not a rank. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript. In December 2024, Vercel reported that none of the major AI crawlers it tested rendered JavaScript, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity. Content that loads only in the browser may be invisible to them. That is a snapshot from one network, so test your own pages. End of chapter 5 Next: What does Google say you can ignore? → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min What does Google say you can ignore? Google’s guide to generative AI features has a section on myths. For Google Search, it says you do not need: llms.txt files or other special files and markup. Google says Search does not use them. It adds that making one is fine for other systems that use it, and will neither help nor harm your visibility in Google Search. See our llms.txt guide . “Chunking” content into tiny pieces. Google says there is no requirement to do this and no ideal page length. Rewriting content only for AI. Google says its systems understand synonyms and meaning, so you do not need every long-tail variation. Inauthentic mentions. Google says seeking them is not as helpful as it might seem. Special structured data. It is not required, though still useful for rich results. This is Google’s view of Google Search. Other tools may behave differently, and Google also says that no third-party tool has access to its internal ranking or AI systems. It is a good check against advice that sounds technical but has no source. End of chapter 6 Next: How do you optimize content for LLMs? → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min How do you optimize content for LLMs? Large language model optimization is mostly about writing clearly. Put the answer first, then the detail. Keep one topic per section and use a heading that matches the question. Name your facts, dates and sources. Keep paragraphs short. These habits also help people, which is why they are safe to adopt. What is an LLM SEO strategy? An LLM SEO strategy is a short plan: the questions your buyers ask, the pages that should answer them, the sources that back each answer and a routine to test how AI tools describe you. The nine steps below turn that into a plan. An AI search content strategy is the same idea applied to what you publish: fewer, better pages, each built to answer a real question. How do you write for AI search? Write the way you would explain the topic to a smart colleague. Say what it is, who it is for, how it works and what it costs. Avoid filler. Add a source or a number only when you can show where it came from. End of chapter 7 Next: A nine-step LLM SEO plan → 08 Chapter 8 · 3 min A nine-step LLM SEO plan Step 1: Make sure models can reach and read your pages Check that key pages are indexed, not blocked by robots.txt or your firewall, and show their main text in the raw HTML. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers. Anthropic says disabling Claude-SearchBot or Claude-User may reduce your visibility in Claude answers. Our robots.txt guide explains the file, and an AI search audit tests each bot. Step 2: Write a list of buyer prompts Write 10 to 15 questions in the words your buyers use. Include category questions, comparison questions and a few about your brand. This list is your keyword research for LLMs. It is different from classic keyword research because prompts are longer and more like speech. Semrush offers a Prompt Research feature in its AI toolkit, and you can also use sales calls, support tickets and Search Console queries. Step 3: Put the answer first Start each section with one or two sentences that answer the heading’s question. Then add detail. A passage that makes sense on its own is easier to quote. Do not break pages into tiny fragments for the sake of it, since Google says that is not needed. Just make each section clear. Step 4: Add evidence Back claims with a named statistic, a quote from an expert or a link to a source, each with a date. This is the one tactic that has controlled test evidence behind it. Use only figures you have read at the source and say what the study can and cannot show. Step 5: Fix your facts and your entity Keep one set of facts: your name, what you do, who you serve, where you work, prices or price ranges, and who runs the company. Make your site, LinkedIn page and directory listings match. A model that sees three different descriptions of you will repeat one of them, and not always the right one. Step 6: Keep important pages current Update pages whose facts change, such as pricing, features, rules and benchmarks. Show a real last-updated date and change something real when you update. Ahrefs’ data suggests fresher pages are cited more, though that is a correlation. Step 7: Build your presence on other sites Answers often rely on third-party sources: review sites, directories, news, community threads and comparison pages. Run your prompts, list the sites the answers cite, and ask which of them you could be on in an honest way. Do not buy fake reviews or post disguised ads. Google says inauthentic mentions are not as useful as they might seem. Step 8: Measure what you can Run your prompt list each month, three runs per prompt, and record mentions, citations, descriptions and competitors. Use Google’s Generative AI performance report in Search Console, which reports impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Use Bing Webmaster Tools’ AI Performance report for citations in Copilot. Our guide to checking if AI tools mention your brand and our list of AI brand visibility tools help with this step. Step 9: Repeat and keep the record Repeat the test each quarter and after big site changes. Keep every sheet. The point is to see a trend and to learn which changes helped. End of chapter 8 Next: Worked example: a service firm builds an LLM SEO plan → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Worked example: a service firm builds an LLM SEO plan This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine an eight-person firm that offers payroll services to restaurants. It writes 12 prompts, such as “payroll service for a small restaurant” and “payroll provider vs doing payroll in house”. It runs each three times in three tools, which gives 108 answers, and is named in 9, about 8%. The source map shows the answers citing two directory sites, a trade association page and a competitor’s guide. The firm is on none of them. Its own services page says “we help businesses grow” and gives no price or location. The plan has four jobs. It rewrites the services page so the first lines say who the firm serves, what it does and a price range. It adds one page with a clear answer to the in-house question, with two sourced statistics. It completes its directory profiles and asks three customers for honest reviews. It tests the same 108 runs after 60 days. The firm records the result whatever it is, because the point is a fair comparison, not a promise. End of chapter 9 Next: LLM SEO for service businesses → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min LLM SEO for service businesses Service firms have an advantage and a risk. The advantage is that buyers ask specific questions, such as “who does X in my city” or “how much does Y cost”. A page with a clear answer can win those. The risk is thin pages. A services page with vague claims gives a model little to quote. Include who you serve, where, what you do, a price range or the factors that set the price, and proof such as named reviews or credentials. Keep your directory and map listings accurate, because answers about local and service firms often rely on them. End of chapter 10 Next: Which LLM SEO tools help? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Which LLM SEO tools help? You can start with no paid tool: a spreadsheet, the AI tools, Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. SEO suites such as Ahrefs and Semrush offer AI visibility features, and stand-alone trackers exist. Test any tool against your hand results and treat a precise rank inside AI answers with caution. Our guide to AI brand visibility tools compares what they track and what they cost. End of chapter 11 Next: Do you need an LLM SEO agency? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min Do you need an LLM SEO agency? Not to start. The plan above can be run in-house. An agency helps when you lack the time, when the fixes need a developer, or when the source map shows work such as outreach that you cannot do alone. Ask what you will receive: the prompt list, raw answers, the source map, a ranked list of fixes and a date to repeat the test. Be wary of any agency that promises a place in AI answers, because no one can guarantee it. Our LLM optimization service and SEO and AI search audit follow this approach. End of chapter 12 Next: How long does LLM SEO take to work? → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min How long does LLM SEO take to work? No study we found gives a reliable time. Fixes to access and facts can show in retrieval-based answers within weeks, since OpenAI says a robots.txt change takes about 24 hours to apply for search. Gains from new content and outside mentions take longer, and training-based knowledge changes only when models are retrained. Treat any firm promise of a timeline as a red flag, and judge progress by your own repeated test. End of chapter 13 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Chasing a rank. The order of brands in answers changes from run to run. Adding files and markup first. Fix access, facts and content before you add anything special. Writing thin pages for every prompt. Google warns that making pages for each variation to manipulate AI answers breaks its scaled content abuse policy. Using unsourced statistics. An unsourced number is a risk to readers and to models. Ignoring other sites. Answers often come from third-party pages. Testing once. One answer is a clue, not a result. End of chapter 14 Next: Our interest in this topic → 15 Chapter 15 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells search and AI search services, including LLM optimization. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . You can get your free diagnostic , which tests your pages and prompts with a written plan. End of chapter 15 Next: Final thoughts → 16 Chapter 16 · 1 min Final thoughts LLM SEO is mostly good SEO with clearer facts, better evidence and a plan to check results. Start with access, then facts, then pages that answer questions with sources. Build a real presence on the sites the answers cite, and measure with a fixed prompt list. Ignore advice that has no source, including extra files, until the basics work. Back matter Glossary A to Z C Citation A link to your page shown as a source in an AI answer. E Entity A clearly named thing, such as a company, person or product, that a model can recognize. L LLM A large language model, the kind of AI behind ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. L LLM SEO (LLMO) Work that helps language models find, understand and cite your brand and pages. Q Query fan-out One question split into several related searches to build a fuller answer. R Retrieval When a model searches the web for fresh pages before it writes an answer. Questions FAQs What is LLM SEO? LLM SEO is improving how often and how accurately large language models mention your brand, recommend your products and cite your pages. For Google it is ordinary SEO plus clear facts, sourced evidence and a presence on sites that AI answers cite. What is LLM optimization (LLMO)? LLMO is another name for the same work. Writers also use GEO and AEO. Google says that, from its point of view, optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO. How is LLM SEO different from traditional SEO? Traditional SEO aims for rankings and clicks. LLM SEO aims to be named and cited in an answer. They share the same base: crawlable pages, clear content and trust. LLM SEO adds fact consistency, third-party mentions and measurement across AI tools. How do LLMs choose which sources to cite? The companies do not publish the rules. Google says its AI features use retrieval and query fan-out, where one question is split into related searches. In practice, pages that can be crawled, answer the question clearly, carry sources and are backed by other sites seem to do better. Does adding statistics and sources help? In one controlled test it did. Princeton-led researchers tested nine content changes on a 10,000-query benchmark and reported that adding citations, quotations and statistics raised visibility by up to 40%. It is a 2024 study and results varied by domain. Do I need an llms.txt file? Google says Search does not use llms.txt and that having one will neither help nor harm your Google visibility. Other services may read it, so adding one is optional. Fix access, facts and content first. How long does LLM SEO take to work? No study we found gives a reliable time. Access and fact fixes can show up in retrieval-based answers within weeks, while outside mentions and new content take longer. Judge progress by repeating the same prompt test. What are the best LLM SEO tools? You can start with no paid tool: a prompt spreadsheet, Search Console's Generative AI performance report and Bing Webmaster Tools' AI Performance report. SEO suites and stand-alone trackers help at scale. Test any tool against a hand baseline. Is LLM SEO useful for service businesses? Yes, when buyers ask specific questions such as who does a job in their area or what it costs. Clear pages with who you serve, where, what you do and a price range, plus accurate directory listings, give models something to quote. Do I need an LLM SEO agency? Not to start. Hire one when you lack time, need developer fixes or need outreach. Ask for the prompt list, raw answers, a source map and a ranked list of fixes, and be wary of promises of placement. What is large language model optimization? It is another name for LLM SEO: shaping your content so large language models can find, understand and cite it. It overlaps with GEO and AEO. How do you optimize content for LLMs? Lead with the answer, use question headings, keep one topic per section, name sources and facts, and keep pages current. Then test how AI tools describe you. How do you write for AI search? Use plain words, answer first, and back claims with named sources. Keep sections short and specific. lede: ChatGPT SEO explained both ways: how ChatGPT search picks sources, an eight-step plan to show up in it, how to use ChatGPT for SEO tasks safely, and a worked example.
copy_text: Home Blog AI Growth Systems ChatGPT SEO: How to Use It for SEO… Guide AI Growth Systems ChatGPT SEO: How to Use It for SEO and How to Show Up in It ChatGPT SEO explained both ways: how ChatGPT search picks sources, an eight-step plan to show up in it, how to use ChatGPT for SEO tasks safely, and a worked example. Jamil Ahmed Published 18 Oct 2026 Updated 16 Nov 2026 14 Chapters 12 Min read A to Z Glossary 01 Part 1: How does ChatGPT search choose what to show? 2 min 02 Part 2: How do you show up in ChatGPT? 4 min 03 How do you rank in ChatGPT and get cited? 1 min 04 How is ChatGPT search different from Google? 1 min 05 Part 3: How do you use ChatGPT for SEO? 2 min 06 Six prompts to start with for SEO tasks 1 min 07 Is ChatGPT bad for SEO? 1 min 08 What about ChatGPT SEO tools? 1 min 09 Does the same work help with Perplexity SEO and Gemini? 1 min 10 Do authority, backlinks and mentions still matter for ChatGPT? 1 min 11 Worked example: a small accounting firm tests ChatGPT 1 min 12 What are the common mistakes? 1 min 13 Our interest in this topic 1 min 14 Final thoughts 1 min Chapter 01 of 14 0% read Chapters 0% 01 Part 1: How does ChatGPT search choose what to show? 02 Part 2: How do you show up in ChatGPT? 03 How do you rank in ChatGPT and get cited? 04 How is ChatGPT search different from Google? 05 Part 3: How do you use ChatGPT for SEO? 06 Six prompts to start with for SEO tasks 07 Is ChatGPT bad for SEO? 08 What about ChatGPT SEO tools? 09 Does the same work help with Perplexity SEO and Gemini? 10 Do authority, backlinks and mentions still matter for ChatGPT? 11 Worked example: a small accounting firm tests ChatGPT 12 What are the common mistakes? 13 Our interest in this topic 14 Final thoughts About 12 min in total Short answer ChatGPT SEO means two things: using ChatGPT to speed up SEO tasks, and doing SEO so ChatGPT search names and cites you. To show up, allow OAI-SearchBot, be indexed in Bing and Google, answer questions first with sources, build honest mentions on sites it cites, and test with a fixed prompt list. To use it for SEO, treat output as a draft and check every fact. 01 ChatGPT SEO has two meanings: using ChatGPT for SEO work, and getting ChatGPT search to cite you. 02 OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers, and placement is never guaranteed. 03 ChatGPT search rewrites questions into short queries and sometimes uses search partners, so Bing and Google indexing both matter. 04 Citations, quotations and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40% in a Princeton-led test. It is a 2024 benchmark, not a promise. 05 SparkToro found under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice. Measure a rate across many runs. 06 ChatGPT has no search volume data. Google says to fact-check AI content, and warns that mass AI pages can be scaled content abuse. 07 Ahrefs reports Google sends about 345 times more traffic than ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity combined, so value is often in being named. “ChatGPT SEO” means two different things. The first is using ChatGPT as a tool to do SEO work faster, such as ideas, outlines, title tags and structured data. The second is doing SEO for ChatGPT: making your brand and pages easy for ChatGPT search to find and cite in its answers. This guide covers both. The short version is that ChatGPT helps with SEO tasks if you check its output, and showing up in ChatGPT depends on crawler access, being found in the search results it uses, clear answers with sources, and what other sites say about you. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher. We say when a figure is a test, a survey or one vendor’s data, and when something is our own recommendation. Nobody outside OpenAI knows exactly how ChatGPT picks sources, and OpenAI does not publish a ranking formula. 01 Chapter 1 · 2 min Part 1: How does ChatGPT search choose what to show? OpenAI’s Help Center describes the process in plain terms. When ChatGPT decides that a question needs fresh information, it can turn your question into one or more targeted search queries. It says ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers, and it names Microsoft in its privacy notes. It may also use your general location from your IP address, so “restaurants near me” can become “top restaurants” plus the city. After reviewing results, it may send further, more specific queries. OpenAI says ChatGPT ranks search results using multiple factors meant to help people find relevant, reliable information, and that placement is not guaranteed. It also warns that results and citations can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect. For publishers, it says to allow OAI-SearchBot to crawl the site and to make sure your host or CDN allows traffic from OpenAI’s published IP addresses. Three practical points follow from this: ChatGPT often searches with short rewritten queries, so ranking in regular search for those phrases helps you get read. The search partner’s index matters. Being indexed in Bing, as well as Google, is a sensible step. Location can change the answer, so test local prompts with a city in them. OpenAI also says that when a question looks like shopping, ChatGPT search may show product options drawn from structured data from third-party providers and other third-party content such as reviews. For sellers of products, this means complete, accurate product data and honest reviews on other sites matter as well as your own pages. End of chapter 1 Next: Part 2: How do you show up in ChatGPT? → 02 Chapter 2 · 4 min Part 2: How do you show up in ChatGPT? This is our recommended order. Steps 1 to 3 make you findable. Steps 4 to 7 make you worth citing. Step 1: Let OpenAI’s crawlers in Open yoursite.com/robots.txt and check that OAI-SearchBot is not blocked on the pages you want cited. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as navigational links, and that a robots.txt change can take about 24 hours to apply. Then check your CDN, firewall and bot protection, because they can block a bot that robots.txt allows. OpenAI publishes the IP ranges to allow. Keep the other OpenAI names straight. GPTBot is for model training, and allowing or blocking it is a separate choice. ChatGPT-User visits a page when a user’s question needs it, and OpenAI says robots.txt rules may not apply to it. Our robots.txt guide explains the file. Step 2: Get indexed in Bing and Google Because ChatGPT search draws on search partners, check that your key pages are indexed in both Bing and Google. Use Bing Webmaster Tools and Google Search Console, submit your sitemap and fix blocked or noindexed pages. Step 3: Rank for the short searches ChatGPT runs Take each long question your buyers ask and write the short search ChatGPT is likely to run: the category, a qualifier and a place. Then look at those phrases in Google and Bing. If you do not appear for them, ChatGPT is less likely to read your page, however good it is. This is our reading of how the process works, based on OpenAI’s description of query rewriting, and it is not a published rule. Step 4: Answer the question first, with evidence Write pages that answer the question in the first sentence or two, then add detail. Give facts a model can quote: prices or ranges, who it is for, how it works, how it compares. Back claims with named sources. A Princeton-led team tested nine content changes on a 10,000-query benchmark and reported that adding citations, quotations and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40%, and by up to 37% on Perplexity. It is a 2024 study and the effect varied by domain, but it is the best controlled evidence we have. Step 5: Build real mentions on other sites Answers often rely on third-party pages: review sites, “best of” lists, directories, forums and news. Run your prompts, list the sites ChatGPT cites, and ask how you can appear there honestly. Claim and complete profiles, earn real reviews, and contribute useful answers. Do not buy reviews or hide ads in forums. Google’s guidance for its own AI features says seeking inauthentic mentions is not as useful as it might seem, and the same sense applies here. Step 6: Keep your facts the same everywhere Use one name, one description, one set of prices and one set of locations across your site, directories and social profiles. A model that sees conflicting facts may repeat the wrong one or skip you. Step 7: Keep key pages fresh Ahrefs analyzed 17 million citations across seven AI search platforms and found that content cited in AI answers was 25.7% fresher than content in regular results. That is a correlation from one vendor’s data set, but it fits common sense: update pages when prices, features or rules change, and show a real update date. Step 8: Measure with a fixed prompt list Write 10 to 15 buyer questions without your brand name. Run each three times in ChatGPT with search on, in a fresh chat, and record whether you are named, whether your page is cited, how you are described and who else appears. Variation is large. SparkToro had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s AI features 2,961 times, and found less than a 1 in 100 chance of getting the same list of brands twice. So look at a rate across many runs, not a rank. Our guides to checking if AI tools mention your brand and AI brand visibility tools go deeper. Also look at traffic. Ahrefs reported that Google sends about 345 times more traffic to websites than ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity combined, and that ChatGPT accounts for over 80% of AI referral traffic. These are Ahrefs figures from 2025 and they will change, but they show that the main value today is often being named and trusted, with clicks a smaller part. End of chapter 2 Next: How do you rank in ChatGPT and get cited? → Reinforce Lab service · AI Search Optimization Want to see how ChatGPT describes your site? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See AI search optimization → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 1 min How do you rank in ChatGPT and get cited? ChatGPT does not have a ranking list like Google. You are either named or linked in the answer, or you are not. To get cited by ChatGPT, three things have to be true: its crawler can reach your page, the page is indexed where its search partners look, and the page gives a clear, specific, checkable answer to the question. The seven steps above cover each one. Products and brands you want named also need clear facts on your own site and mentions on other trusted sites. End of chapter 3 Next: How is ChatGPT search different from Google? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min How is ChatGPT search different from Google? Area Google Search ChatGPT search Output A list of links, sometimes with an AI summary A written answer with citations and a sources panel Query What the user typed Often rewritten into one or more targeted searches Crawler control Googlebot and Google’s controls OAI-SearchBot for search, GPTBot for training, ChatGPT-User for user visits Measurement Search Console shows clicks and impressions No OpenAI report for site owners that we found, so you test prompts and read analytics Placement Ranking position OpenAI says placement is not guaranteed The practical result is that you cannot track a position the way you track a rank. You track how often you are named and cited across a fixed list of prompts. End of chapter 4 Next: Part 3: How do you use ChatGPT for SEO? → 05 Chapter 5 · 2 min Part 3: How do you use ChatGPT for SEO? ChatGPT is a fast assistant for drafting and sorting. It is not a source of search data. Treat its output as a first draft that you check. The table shows common uses and the check that each needs. Task How ChatGPT helps What you must check Keyword ideas Expands a seed topic into related subtopics and questions It has no search volume data. Confirm in a keyword tool. Clustering and intent Groups a long list by topic and labels intent Check the live results, since intent is shown by what ranks. Outlines and briefs Drafts headings that cover a topic Add your own angle, examples and internal links. Title tags and meta descriptions Gives many options at once Count the characters yourself, and make sure they match the page. Structured data Writes JSON-LD for an article, product or FAQ Validate it, and make sure it matches the visible page. Redirect maps and patterns Helps match old and new URLs, and writes regex Test on a sample before you deploy. Content refresh ideas Compares your page with a list of subtopics and suggests gaps Check facts and sources yourself. FAQ and question lists Suggests questions your readers may ask Use real questions from sales calls and Search Console first. Good prompts give context: the audience, the page goal, the target keyword, the tone and the format of the answer you want. Ask for options, not one answer, and ask it to list what it is unsure about. End of chapter 5 Next: Six prompts to start with for SEO tasks → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min Six prompts to start with for SEO tasks These are examples. Fill in the brackets, and check every output. Topic map: “Act as an SEO strategist. For a [type of business] that sells to [audience], list 20 subtopics a buyer researches before buying, grouped by buying stage. Mark any you are unsure about.” Intent labels: “Label each keyword in this list as informational, commercial, transactional or navigational, and give a one-line reason.” Brief: “Write an outline for a page that answers [question] for [audience]. Put a direct answer in the first sentence of each section. List the facts I must source.” Title options: “Give 10 title tags under 60 characters for a page about [topic]. Include [keyword] and no hype words.” Structured data: “Write FAQPage JSON-LD for these questions and answers exactly as written. Do not add any content.” Gap check: “Here is my page and a list of questions buyers ask. Which questions does my page not answer?” Always ask the tool to say what it is unsure about, and never paste private client data into a tool you have not approved. End of chapter 6 Next: Is ChatGPT bad for SEO? → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min Is ChatGPT bad for SEO? Not by itself. Google says appropriate use of AI or automation is not against its guidelines, and that using AI does not give content any special gain. It says content is judged on whether it is helpful, original and trustworthy. The risk is how you use it. Google’s spam policy lists using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value for users as scaled content abuse. Google also warns that generative models predict likely words rather than retrieve facts, so outputs can be wrong, and it asks you to fact-check and review AI content, including titles, descriptions and structured data, before you publish. The safe rule is simple. Use ChatGPT to help you think and draft. Add what only you can: first-hand experience, real data, named sources and a point of view. Have a person check every fact. End of chapter 7 Next: What about ChatGPT SEO tools? → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min What about ChatGPT SEO tools? You will see “ChatGPT SEO tools” in three forms: custom GPTs, browser add-ons and features inside SEO suites. They can save time on drafting. They do not add data that ChatGPT lacks, such as search volume or backlinks, unless they connect to a real data source. Ask what data a tool uses before you pay for it. For tracking how you appear in ChatGPT, see our guide to AI brand visibility tools . End of chapter 8 Next: Does the same work help with Perplexity SEO and Gemini? → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Does the same work help with Perplexity SEO and Gemini? Largely, yes. Perplexity has its own crawler, PerplexityBot, which it says surfaces and links sites in its results, and a user-triggered fetcher that generally ignores robots.txt. Gemini and Google’s AI features rely on Google’s index. The base work, which is access, indexing, answer-first pages, evidence and third-party presence, helps all of them. Our guide to ranking in AI Overviews covers Google’s side. End of chapter 9 Next: Do authority, backlinks and mentions still matter for ChatGPT? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min Do authority, backlinks and mentions still matter for ChatGPT? Semrush’s guides to ChatGPT visibility say they do, and give a practical method. Ask ChatGPT questions in your niche, note which sites it cites most often, and aim for honest mentions and links from those sites, since links from sources ChatGPT frequently cites may carry more weight than links from unrelated sites. The same guide recommends building brand consensus off your site through third-party lists, reviews, Reddit and YouTube, and it notes a study that found recency bias in several ChatGPT models, so newer pages tended to be favored. These are a vendor’s recommendations, and OpenAI does not publish its ranking factors, so treat them as hypotheses to test with your own prompt list. The principle is sound: ChatGPT often reads what other sites say about you, so work on that as well as on your own pages. End of chapter 10 Next: Worked example: a small accounting firm tests ChatGPT → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Worked example: a small accounting firm tests ChatGPT This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine a four-person accounting firm in a mid-sized city. It writes 12 prompts, such as “accountant for a small restaurant in [city]” and “how much does bookkeeping cost for a small business”. It runs each three times in ChatGPT with search on, which gives 36 answers, and is named in 3. The answers cite a local directory, a “best accountants” article from a local news site and a competitor’s guide to bookkeeping costs. The firm is on the directory with an old phone number and is not in the article. Its own services page says “full-service accounting” and gives no prices or areas. Its plan has five parts. It fixes the phone number everywhere. It rewrites its services page to say who it serves, where and a price range. It adds one page with a sourced answer on bookkeeping costs. It asks the news site’s editor whether a list update is possible, and asks three clients for honest reviews on the directory. It repeats the same 36 runs after 60 days. The point is a fair comparison, not a promise. End of chapter 11 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Blocking OAI-SearchBot by accident. A security plugin or CDN setting often does it. Treating ChatGPT as a keyword tool. It does not know search volumes. Publishing unreviewed AI content. Google asks you to fact-check it, and scaled content abuse is a spam policy. Chasing a rank in answers. Lists change from run to run. Testing once. One answer is a clue, not a result. Ignoring Bing. ChatGPT search draws on search partners as well as its own crawler. Only fixing your own site. Answers often rely on third-party pages. End of chapter 12 Next: Our interest in this topic → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells search and AI search services. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . Our AI search optimization service follows the steps above, and you can get your free diagnostic to see how ChatGPT and other tools describe your site. End of chapter 13 Next: Final thoughts → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min Final thoughts Use ChatGPT as a quick assistant and check every output. To show up in it, let its crawler in, be indexed in Bing and Google, answer questions first with sources, build honest mentions on the sites it cites and test with a fixed prompt list. Nobody can promise a place in ChatGPT answers, but each step makes you easier to find, to trust and to quote. Back matter Glossary A to Z C ChatGPT search The part of ChatGPT that searches the web and shows answers with source links. C Citation A link to your page shown as a source in an AI answer. O OAI-SearchBot OpenAI's crawler that finds pages to show in ChatGPT search. P Prompt set A fixed list of buyer questions you run through the tool. Q Query rewriting ChatGPT turning a user's question into shorter search queries. S Scaled content abuse Making many pages mainly to manipulate search results, which Google treats as spam. Questions FAQs What is ChatGPT SEO? It means two things: using ChatGPT as a tool to do SEO tasks faster, and doing SEO so that ChatGPT search finds, names and cites your brand and pages in its answers. How do I use ChatGPT for SEO? Use it for drafts and sorting: keyword ideas and clusters, intent labels, outlines, title and meta options, JSON-LD, redirect patterns and FAQ ideas. It has no search volume data, so confirm keywords in a keyword tool and check every fact before you publish. How do I use ChatGPT for keyword research? Ask it to expand a seed topic, group keywords by intent and suggest questions, then validate each term in a keyword tool and in the live search results. ChatGPT does not have search volume or difficulty data. How does ChatGPT help with SEO? It speeds up first drafts of outlines, titles, meta descriptions and structured data, and helps sort long lists. It does not replace search data, expert knowledge or review. Google asks you to fact-check AI-assisted content. How do I do SEO for ChatGPT? Allow OAI-SearchBot, check your CDN and firewall, be indexed in Bing and Google, rank for short searches, answer questions first with sources, build honest third-party mentions, keep facts consistent and fresh, and test with a fixed prompt list. How do I rank in ChatGPT search? No one controls ChatGPT's ranking, and OpenAI says placement is not guaranteed. Make your pages crawlable and indexed, write clear sourced answers, and earn mentions on the review sites, lists and directories that ChatGPT cites for your questions. How do I get cited by ChatGPT? Be retrievable and worth citing: allow OAI-SearchBot, answer the question in the first sentence, add specific facts and named sources, and appear on third-party pages the answers already use. Test monthly, since answers vary run to run. Is ChatGPT bad for SEO? Not by itself. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines. The risk is publishing many unchecked pages, which Google's spam policy can treat as scaled content abuse, or publishing wrong facts. Add original value and review everything. Are there ChatGPT SEO tools worth using? Custom GPTs, add-ons and SEO suite features can save drafting time, but they add no data that ChatGPT lacks unless they connect to a real data source. Ask what data a tool uses, and test any tracker against a hand baseline. Does ChatGPT send much traffic? Less than Google. Ahrefs reported in 2025 that Google sends about 345 times more traffic to sites than ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity combined, and that ChatGPT is over 80% of AI referral traffic. Being named and trusted can matter beyond clicks. How do you rank in ChatGPT? There is no fixed rank. Let OpenAI's search crawler reach your pages, get them indexed in Bing and Google, and write clear answers with named sources. Then test your key questions in ChatGPT and record what it says. How do you get cited by ChatGPT? Make the page crawlable, answer the question directly with evidence, keep facts current and earn mentions on other trusted sites. Citations are not guaranteed, so test and repeat. What is Perplexity SEO? Perplexity answers questions by searching the web and citing sources. The same basics apply: crawlable pages, clear answers, accurate facts and mentions from trusted sites. Check Perplexity's own documentation for its crawler. An entity is a uniquely identifiable thing, not a keyword. The work is a fact sheet, a clear entity home, accurate Organization and Person markup, matching profiles, clear internal links and honest mentions on other sites. 01 An entity is a uniquely identifiable thing, such as a company, person or product. It is not a keyword. 02 Ahrefs studied 75,000 brands: branded web mentions correlated 0.664 with AI Overview visibility, backlinks 0.218. It is a correlation. 03 Google says Organization markup can help it disambiguate your organization. There are no required properties, and sameAs can list your profiles. 04 Google lists no extra markup requirement for its AI features, so use entity work to state facts clearly, not as a trick. 05 Knowledge panels are generated automatically. Focus on clear facts and independent coverage, not on chasing a panel. 06 Never fake Wikipedia or Wikidata entries. Build independent coverage first. 07 Test what ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity say about you each quarter and fix the sources that are wrong. Entity SEO is the work of making it clear what your brand, your people, your products and your topics are, and how they relate, so search engines and AI tools identify you correctly. An entity is a uniquely identifiable thing, such as a company, a person, a place or an idea. It is not a keyword. The practical work is plain: use one name and one description everywhere, state the facts on a clear home page, add accurate structured data, link related pages with clear anchors and earn honest mentions on other sites. This guide explains what entities are, why they matter for search and AI answers, how to find the entities for your site, and a nine-step plan with a sample of Organization markup. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we say when a finding is a correlation or when a claim is our own view. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is an entity in SEO? An entity is a thing or concept that is singular, unique, well defined and distinguishable from other things. Google’s Knowledge Graph and Wikidata are two large catalogs of them. Examples are a company such as Reinforce Lab, a person such as an author, a product, a city or a concept such as “robots.txt”. An entity has a name, a type, facts about it and links to other entities. Search Engine Journal’s Dixon Jones puts the difference between an entity and a keyword this way: an entity is a record in a database, with an identifier, while a keyword is a word or phrase. Many entities carry a label that looks like a keyword, which is why the two are often mixed up. Google’s Knowledge Panel Help says knowledge panels are information boxes that appear for entities in the Knowledge Graph, that they are generated automatically from information across the web, and that they update as information changes. End of chapter 1 Next: Entity SEO vs keyword SEO → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min Entity SEO vs keyword SEO Area Keyword SEO Entity SEO Unit of work A phrase people type A thing, and its facts and links to other things Question Does the page contain the phrase? Is it clear which thing the page is about? Main risk Missing a phrase Being confused with another thing, or described wrongly Typical tasks Titles, headings, copy Facts, structured data, internal links, profiles, mentions Measure Rankings and traffic Correct descriptions, knowledge panels, AI answers, branded search Both matter. Entity work does not replace keyword research. It adds a check on whether the systems reading your site can tell who you are. End of chapter 2 Next: Why do entities matter for SEO and AI search? → Reinforce Lab service · Technical SEO Want your entity facts and markup checked? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See technical SEO → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 2 min Why do entities matter for SEO and AI search? Search engines and language models both work with meaning, not only matching words. If your name matches another company, or your pages describe you in several ways, a system may attach the wrong facts to you or skip you. Three pieces of evidence help set expectations. Brand mentions correlate with AI visibility. Ahrefs studied 75,000 brands and found that branded web mentions had the strongest correlation with brand visibility in Google AI Overviews, at 0.664, against 0.218 for backlinks. The next two were branded anchors (0.527) and branded search volume (0.392). Ahrefs also found that 26% of brands had zero AI Overview mentions. This is a correlation, not proof of cause, and Ahrefs says so. The sample was domains with a Domain Rating above 40 and a top keyword of at least 800 searches a month, and the study covers Google AI Overviews only. Google uses organization data to tell organizations apart. Its Organization structured data documentation says adding the markup to your home page can help Google understand your organization’s details and disambiguate it in search results. It also says some properties influence the logo shown in Search results and in your knowledge panel. Google says AI features need no special markup. Google lists no extra technical requirements beyond being indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. So entity markup is not a trick for AI answers. It is a way to state facts clearly. There is a fair counter view. In a 2024 article titled “Stop overcomplicating things. Entity SEO is just SEO,” Ahrefs argues that you do not need to treat entity work as a separate discipline. We agree with part of that. Most of the plan below is ordinary good practice. We still find the entity lens useful, because it points to a short list of checks that many sites fail, such as an old company description on a directory or no clear About page. End of chapter 3 Next: How do you find the entities for your site? → 04 Chapter 4 · 2 min How do you find the entities for your site? Start with what you already know, then use tools to find what you missed. This answers a common question: how to find entities for SEO optimization. List your own entities. Your company, its legal and short names, your products and services, your leaders and authors, your locations and your main topics. Check what search shows. Search your brand and your topics. Note any knowledge panel, the “People also ask” questions and the related searches. These show the things Google links to your topic. Look at public catalogs. See whether Wikipedia or Wikidata has an entry for your topics. Note the standard names they use for each concept. Use the same names where they fit. Read what competitors cover. Open the top pages for your topic and list the people, tools, terms and concepts they mention. Our semantics check does this for every post we write. Use an entity tool. Google’s Cloud Natural Language API can list the entities it finds in a text. Run your own page through it and see whether the main entity is the one you meant. Ask AI tools. Ask “What is [brand]?” and “Who is [person]?” in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. Compare each answer with your facts. To find related entities, look at the terms and concepts that appear around your topic on several top pages, and at the questions people ask. Include the ones a reader would expect to see, and skip the rest. Do not stuff a page with names. End of chapter 4 Next: A nine-step entity SEO plan → 05 Chapter 5 · 3 min A nine-step entity SEO plan Step 1: Write your fact sheet Write one page of facts: your legal name, trading name, a one-sentence description, what you sell, who you serve, locations, founding date, leaders and official profile links. Every later step uses this sheet. Step 2: Build a clear entity home SEO practitioners describe an “entity home”: a main page that acts as the source of truth for an entity, which Helen Pollitt says search engines often look for. This is practitioner advice, not a Google rule. For a company, that is usually the About page or the home page. Put the facts from your sheet there in plain text. For each person who writes for you, build an author page with a short bio, credentials and profile links. Step 3: Add Organization structured data Google’s documentation says there are no required properties, and it recommends adding as many relevant ones as you can. Useful ones include name , alternateName , url , logo , description , address , contactPoint , legalName , foundingDate and sameAs . Google says to use the same name and alternate name that you use for your site name, and that sameAs can list pages about your organization on other sites, such as social or review profiles. Here is a short sample with a made-up company: {
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Example Co",
  "legalName": "Example Company Limited",
  "url": "https://www.example.com/",
  "logo": "https://www.example.com/logo.png",
  "description": "Example Co builds scheduling software for clinics.",
  "foundingDate": "2018",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://www.linkedin.com/company/example-co",
    "https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/example-co"
  ]
} The markup must match what the page shows. Validate it before you publish. Step 4: Mark up people and connect them Use Person markup for authors and leaders, with sameAs links to their real profiles, and connect each person to the organization with a property such as worksFor . Describe real relationships only. Step 5: Make your profiles match Compare your website, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, directories and review sites against your fact sheet. Fix old names, addresses, phone numbers and descriptions. AI answers often repeat an old directory line, so a wrong listing can cost more than a weak page. Step 6: Handle Wikipedia and Wikidata with care These catalogs feed knowledge systems, but you cannot simply add yourself. Wikipedia has notability rules, and self-promotional edits break its policies. If your company or a person meets the rules, an independent editor can write the entry from reliable sources. Otherwise, build the independent coverage first. Never create fake pages or sources. Step 7: Write pages that make the entity clear Define each core term in the first sentence of its page. Use the standard name for each concept, and use it the same way throughout. Place related entities in context, for example “Reinforce Lab” with its founder, “Jamil Ahmed”. Link related pages with descriptive anchor text, and keep one main topic for each page. Our guide to generative engine optimization shows how this carries into AI answers. Step 8: Earn real mentions Given the Ahrefs correlation, honest mentions on other sites matter. Good sources are press, industry sites, partner pages, reviews, podcasts and communities where you help people. Do not buy mentions or post fakes. Google’s guidance for AI features says seeking inauthentic mentions is not as helpful as it might seem. Step 9: Test and repeat Every quarter, ask AI tools what they say about your brand, your key people and your products, and compare with your fact sheet. Check your branded search results and any knowledge panel. Our guide on checking if AI tools mention your brand gives a 30-minute test, and our list of AI brand visibility tools covers tracking at scale. End of chapter 5 Next: How does entity SEO relate to topical authority? → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min How does entity SEO relate to topical authority? Search Engine Journal’s Helen Pollitt notes that the structure of a site can reinforce the relationships between entities. Classifying products or posts by their relationship to each other, and linking subtopics back to a main category, signals that the site has deep, structured expertise on a subject, in place of keyword targeting. This is the link between entity work and topical authority: a clear brand entity, a clear set of topic entities and pages that connect them with descriptive links. In practice, give each main topic one strong page, link the supporting pages to it, name the same concept the same way throughout, and use images with descriptive file names and alt text that name what they show. These are practitioner recommendations. Google does not publish a topical authority score, so judge the work by whether the pages answer questions and the facts are consistent. End of chapter 6 Next: Worked example: a company with a shared name → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min Worked example: a company with a shared name This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine a nine-person analytics firm called “Apex Data”. Another company, a data-center operator, uses a similar name. When the firm asks AI tools “What is Apex Data?”, two of three answers describe the data-center operator. The firm writes its fact sheet and puts a clear description on its About page, starting with “Apex Data is a nine-person analytics firm that builds dashboards for restaurants.” It adds Organization markup with its LinkedIn and Crunchbase profiles in sameAs . It fixes its directory listings, which gave an older name. It adds author pages for its two writers. It earns a feature in a restaurant trade publication and two customer reviews on a software review site. After 60 days it repeats its test. It keeps the results either way, because the goal is a fair comparison, not a promise. End of chapter 7 Next: How does entity SEO work for local and service firms? → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min How does entity SEO work for local and service firms? For a local or service firm, the main entities are the business, its locations and its people. Use the same business name, address format and phone number on your site, your Google Business Profile and every directory. Give each lawyer, doctor, consultant or engineer a page with credentials, and link each person to the services they provide. Add LocalBusiness or a more specific type in your markup if it fits, and keep the address in the markup the same as the address on the page. Check that your name does not collide with another business nearby, and if it does, add a clear descriptor, such as the type of work, in your profiles and your About text. End of chapter 8 Next: How does entity SEO work for online stores? → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min How does entity SEO work for online stores? For a store, products are the key entities. Search Engine Journal’s Helen Pollitt notes that identifying codes such as SKUs, ISBNs and GTINs help search engines see that products are different from each other, and that using them consistently across the site helps. Keep product names, brand names and categories the same across your pages, your feed and marketplaces. Link each product to its brand and category, and keep prices and availability current. Our technical SEO service includes this kind of data check. End of chapter 9 Next: How do you measure entity SEO? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min How do you measure entity SEO? There is no single score. Use a short list of checks and record them with dates: Accuracy test. Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity “What is [brand]?”, “Who runs [brand]?” and “What does [brand] sell?” three times each. Count answers with a material error. Consistency audit. Compare your fact sheet with your site, profiles and directories. Count mismatches and fix them. Branded search. Watch branded impressions and clicks in Search Console, and see which pages show for your brand name. Knowledge panel and rich results. Search your brand and note whether a panel appears, and whether its facts are right. Use Google’s Rich Results Test to check markup. Mentions. Track new, honest mentions on other sites, and check which sites AI answers cite for your category. AI impressions. In Search Console’s Generative AI performance report, check impressions for pages that state your core facts. Treat changes as signs, not proof. Answers vary from run to run, so repeat each test and compare rates over time. End of chapter 10 Next: Does entity SEO help with AI search? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Does entity SEO help with AI search? It can help models describe you correctly, because models learn about brands from text that mentions them. The Ahrefs data fits that idea, though it is a correlation. Remember the limits: Google says no special markup is required for its AI features, and no one outside the AI companies knows exactly how they choose sources. So use entity work to remove confusion, not to chase a trick. End of chapter 11 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Treating entities as keywords. Repeating a name many times does not clarify it. Using different names. A short name on the site and a legal name on a directory, with no link between them, makes a system unsure. Over-marking pages. Markup that does not match the page can be ignored or cause problems. Chasing a knowledge panel. Panels are generated automatically. Focus on clear facts and independent coverage. Faking Wikipedia or Wikidata entries. It breaks their rules and risks your reputation. Ignoring old listings. Wrong facts on third-party sites often feed wrong answers. Stopping after the markup. Mentions, profiles and clear pages do most of the work. End of chapter 12 Next: Our interest in this topic → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells search and AI search services. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . Our technical SEO service covers structured data, and you can get your free diagnostic . End of chapter 13 Next: Final thoughts → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min Final thoughts Entity SEO is mostly clarity. Know your entities, state the facts once and use them everywhere, mark them up accurately, link related pages clearly and earn honest mentions. Then test what search and AI tools say about you, fix what is wrong and repeat each quarter. Back matter Glossary A to Z E Entity A uniquely identifiable thing, such as a company, person, product or concept. E Entity home The main page on your site that states the facts about an entity. K Knowledge Graph Google's database of entities and the links between them. K Knowledge panel An information box Google shows for an entity in the Knowledge Graph. S sameAs A structured data property that lists pages about the same entity on other sites. S Structured data Code on a page that states facts in a format machines can read. Questions FAQs What is entity SEO? Entity SEO is making it clear what your brand, people, products and topics are, and how they relate, so search engines and AI tools identify you correctly. It focuses on facts, structured data, internal links, profiles and mentions. What are entities in SEO? Entities are uniquely identifiable things such as companies, people, places, products and concepts. Catalogs such as Google's Knowledge Graph and Wikidata record them with identifiers, facts and relationships. What is the difference between entities and keywords? A keyword is a word or phrase people type. An entity is a thing with an identifier and facts. Many entities have names that look like keywords, which is why they are confused. Both matter. How do I find entities for SEO optimization? List your own brand, products, people and topics. Then check knowledge panels, People also ask and related searches, Wikipedia and Wikidata, competitor pages, Google's Natural Language API and what AI tools say when asked about you. How do I find related entities for SEO? Look at the people, tools, terms and concepts that appear around your topic on several top pages and in the questions people ask. Include the ones a reader would expect, and avoid stuffing pages with names. Do I need schema markup for entity SEO? It helps but is not required. Google says Organization markup can help it disambiguate your organization and that no properties are required. Keep markup accurate, matched to the page and validated. Does entity SEO help with AI search? It can help models describe you correctly. Ahrefs found branded web mentions correlated 0.664 with AI Overview brand visibility across 75,000 brands, but that is a correlation. Google lists no special markup requirement for its AI features. How do I get a Google knowledge panel? Knowledge panels are generated automatically from information across the web for entities in the Knowledge Graph. You cannot order one. Publish clear facts, build independent coverage and keep profiles consistent. Is entity SEO just SEO? Partly. Ahrefs argued in 2024 that entity SEO is just SEO. Much of the work is ordinary good practice, but the entity lens gives a short checklist that many sites fail, such as old directory facts or no clear About page. Should I create a Wikipedia or Wikidata entry for my company? Only if it meets their notability rules, and ideally written by an independent editor from reliable sources. Self-promotional edits break their policies. Build independent coverage first and never create fake sources. Evidence Sources Ahrefs: An analysis of AI Overview brand visibility factors, 75K brands studied (May 2025) Google Search Central: Organization structured data Google Knowledge Panel Help: About knowledge panels Google Search Central: AI features and your website Google Search Central: Guide to optimizing for generative AI features on Google Search Search Engine Journal: Entities in SEO, what are they and why do they matter? (Dixon Jones, 2023) Search Engine Journal: What does entity optimization mean? title: What Is llms.txt? Should You Add One? | Reinforce Lab
meta: What is llms.txt, who reads it, and should you add one? What Google says and what two studies of 137,000 and 300,000 sites found, plus how to write one.
