Home Blog AI Growth Systems What Is llms.txt and Should You Add One? Guide AI Growth Systems What Is llms.txt and Should You Add One? What llms.txt is, who reads it, what two large studies show, whether to add one, how to write one with a sample file, how to test it and what to do first instead. Jamil Ahmed Published 23 Oct 2026 Updated 15 Nov 2026 16 Chapters 12 Min read A to Z Glossary 01 What is llms.txt? 1 min 02 What does an llms.txt file contain? 2 min 03 Who reads llms.txt? 2 min 04 Does llms.txt help you get cited by AI tools? 1 min 05 Why do audit tools and guides mention llms.txt? 1 min 06 How is llms.txt different from robots.txt and a sitemap? 1 min 07 What do the studies prove, and what do they not? 1 min 08 What about Markdown versions of your pages? 1 min 09 Should you add an llms.txt file? 1 min 10 How do you create an llms.txt file? 1 min 11 How do you test whether llms.txt does anything on your site? 1 min 12 What should you do before llms.txt? 1 min 13 Worked example: a software company with a docs site 1 min 14 What are the common mistakes? 1 min 15 Our interest in this topic 1 min 16 Final thoughts 1 min Chapter 01 of 16 0% read Chapters 0% 01 What is llms.txt? 02 What does an llms.txt file contain? 03 Who reads llms.txt? 04 Does llms.txt help you get cited by AI tools? 05 Why do audit tools and guides mention llms.txt? 06 How is llms.txt different from robots.txt and a sitemap? 07 What do the studies prove, and what do they not? 08 What about Markdown versions of your pages? 09 Should you add an llms.txt file? 10 How do you create an llms.txt file? 11 How do you test whether llms.txt does anything on your site? 12 What should you do before llms.txt? 13 Worked example: a software company with a docs site 14 What are the common mistakes? 15 Our interest in this topic 16 Final thoughts About 12 min in total Short answer llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file at the root of a website that gives language models a short guide to the site and links to its best pages. It is not a standard. Google says Search does not use it, Ahrefs found 97% of llms.txt files got no requests in a month, and SE Ranking found no link to citations. It is cheap to add, but do access, readable pages and clear answers first. 01 llms.txt is a proposal by Jeremy Howard from September 2024: a Markdown file at /llms.txt with a summary and links. It is not a web standard. 02 Google says Google Search does not use llms.txt, and that having one will neither help nor harm your Google visibility. 03 Ahrefs studied 137,210 domains in May 2026: 28% had a file and 97% of those received no requests. Fetches are not reads. 04 SE Ranking studied nearly 300,000 domains: 10.13% had a file and it found no link to AI citations. It is observational data. 05 The file may suit documentation sites, where coding tools could read it. That is an inference to test. 06 It does not allow or block crawlers. Use robots.txt for that. 07 Do access, HTML content, answer-first pages, consistent facts and honest mentions before llms.txt. llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file, written in Markdown and placed at the root of a website, that gives language models a short guide to the site and links to its most useful pages. It is not a web standard, and the evidence so far shows that few AI tools read it. Google says Google Search does not use it, a 2026 Ahrefs study found that 97% of llms.txt files received no requests in a month, and an SE Ranking study found no link between having the file and being cited. Adding one is cheap and harmless, but it should come after the basics that do move results. This guide explains what llms.txt is, who reads it, what the data shows, whether you should add one, and how to write one if you decide to. It includes a sample file, a way to test it and a worked example. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we state the limits of each study. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is llms.txt? The llms.txt file was proposed by Jeremy Howard in September 2024. The proposal calls for a Markdown file at /llms.txt on a website, or at a subpath such as /docs/llms.txt , that offers brief background, guidance and links to detailed pages. The idea is to give an AI model or agent a clean, short map of the site, so it does not have to wade through navigation, scripts and ads in ordinary HTML pages. The proposal also suggests that pages with information agents might need provide a clean Markdown version at the same address with .md added, and that sites use standard link relations to point to those files. The proposal was updated in 2026, so check the current text at llmstxt.org if you build one. End of chapter 1 Next: What does an llms.txt file contain? → 02 Chapter 2 · 2 min What does an llms.txt file contain? The proposed format is simple. It has these parts, in order: A heading of level one with the name of the site or project. This is the only required part. A quote block with a short summary of the site, containing the key facts needed to understand the rest of the file. Optional paragraphs or lists with more detail on how to read the files. Optional sections, each with a level-two heading, that hold lists of links. Each list item has a Markdown link and, if you like, a colon and a short note. An optional section named “Optional” for secondary links that an agent can skip when it needs less context. Here is a short sample for a made-up company: # Example Co

> Example Co makes scheduling software for medical clinics in the United States. Plans start at a fixed monthly price per location.

Key facts: founded in 2018, based in Austin, Texas. Support is available on weekdays.

## Product

- [Features](https://www.example.com/features/): What the software does and who it is for
- [Pricing](https://www.example.com/pricing/): Plans, prices and what each includes
- [Integrations](https://www.example.com/integrations/): Systems it connects to

## Help

- [Setup guide](https://www.example.com/help/setup/): Step-by-step setup for a new clinic
- [Security](https://www.example.com/security/): How patient data is protected

## Optional

- [Blog](https://www.example.com/blog/): Articles and updates End of chapter 2 Next: Who reads llms.txt? → Reinforce Lab service · AI Search Optimization Want the steps that do move AI visibility first? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See AI search optimization → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 2 min Who reads llms.txt? This is the key question, and the answer today is “very few tools.” We found three sources. Google says Google Search does not use it. In its guide to generative AI features, Google lists llms.txt files among things you do not need, because Google Search itself does not use them. It adds that creating one is fine for other services that use it, and will neither harm nor help your visibility in Google Search. Almost no one requests it. Ahrefs studied 137,210 domains in its Web Analytics product that received traffic in May 2026. It found that 28% published an llms.txt file, and that 97% of those files received no requests at all that month. Of the requests that did arrive, 96% came from bots. Among named AI tools, GPTBot made the most requests, and Claude Code was second. Ahrefs also found that AI bots never asked for llms.txt files that did not exist, so publishing one does not put you on an AI radar. Limits: Ahrefs customers skew technical, so the 28% adoption is an upper bound, a fetch does not prove a read, and the study did not check whether files followed the specification. No measurable link to citations. SE Ranking analyzed nearly 300,000 domains. It found llms.txt on 10.13% of them, with adoption about the same across low, mid and high traffic sites. It reported no correlation between having the file and how often a domain was cited by AI tools, and its model got slightly more accurate when it removed the llms.txt factor. Limits: it is an observational study of one dataset, it has no crawler logs, and the authors call the results context-dependent. It bounds the size of any effect and does not prove that no effect exists for any site. The two studies used different methods and data, and they point the same way. Neither one shows that major AI search tools use the file to decide what to cite. End of chapter 3 Next: Does llms.txt help you get cited by AI tools? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min Does llms.txt help you get cited by AI tools? We found no evidence that it does. OpenAI’s documentation tells site owners to allow OAI-SearchBot and to allow requests from its published IP addresses. It does not mention llms.txt as a factor. ChatGPT search, Google’s AI features and Perplexity retrieve pages through their own search systems, and a separate file that lists your best pages does not change which pages those systems retrieve. That is our reading, and the studies fit it, but no one outside the AI companies can say for certain. There is one group where the file may have more use: tools that read documentation. Ahrefs found that Claude Code was the second most frequent named AI fetcher of llms.txt files, ahead of the AI search bots. That suggests developer tools and coding agents may look for the file when working with documentation. This is an inference from request counts, so treat it as a lead to test on a documentation site, not as proof. End of chapter 4 Next: Why do audit tools and guides mention llms.txt? → 05 Chapter 5 · 1 min Why do audit tools and guides mention llms.txt? Because the idea spread faster than the evidence. Ahrefs reports that Google’s Chrome Lighthouse audit for llms.txt accounted for roughly 1 in 1,000 of the fetches it measured, and that about 12% of fetches came from the industry studying itself, such as GEO and AEO tools, llms.txt checkers and researchers. In other words, a good share of the traffic to these files comes from people and tools that check for them. That does not show that AI platforms use the file to answer questions. If a tool tells you that a missing llms.txt is a failing grade for AI visibility, ask for the source. Google lists no such requirement, and the two studies we read found no link to citations. A fair audit marks it as optional. End of chapter 5 Next: How is llms.txt different from robots.txt and a sitemap? → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min How is llms.txt different from robots.txt and a sitemap? The three files do different jobs, and only two of them are well established. File Job Who reads it robots.txt Tells crawlers which parts of a site they may fetch Search and AI crawlers that honor it, such as Googlebot, OAI-SearchBot and ClaudeBot XML sitemap Lists the URLs you want search engines to find Search engines such as Google and Bing llms.txt Offers a short guide and curated links for language models No major AI platform has committed to it. A few bots and tools fetch it. If a page is blocked in robots.txt, listing it in llms.txt does not open it. If a page is missing from your sitemap, listing it in llms.txt does not make a search engine index it. So the file cannot fix access or indexing problems. Those need their own checks. End of chapter 6 Next: What do the studies prove, and what do they not? → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min What do the studies prove, and what do they not? It helps to read the two studies with care, since each answers a different question. Ahrefs measured requests. It asked who fetches llms.txt files. The answer was almost no one in the month it studied. It could not say whether a fetch changed an answer, and it noted that its figures are ceilings on real use. SE Ranking measured an outcome. It asked whether domains with the file were cited more. It found no link. It could not look at crawler logs, so it could not say whether retrieval bots ever requested the files. A fair reading is that any effect is too small to see in that data. Neither covers the future. AI platforms may change what they read. The proposal itself was updated in 2026. If a major platform announces support, the advice here should change, and we would update this guide. The honest summary is that the file has no proven benefit today and a small, easy cost. End of chapter 7 Next: What about Markdown versions of your pages? → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min What about Markdown versions of your pages? The proposal goes further than a single file. It suggests that pages with information agents might need offer a clean Markdown copy, at the same address with .md added, and that sites point to those copies with standard link relations or HTTP headers. This helps most when a page is hard to read, for example when it is full of scripts, tabs or widgets. For ordinary articles that already render clean HTML, the benefit is smaller. If you try it, serve the same content as the page, since showing a model different facts from what people see risks trust problems. Test on a small set of pages first, and check logs to see whether anything fetches them. End of chapter 8 Next: Should you add an llms.txt file? → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Should you add an llms.txt file? Type of site Our view Why Developer documentation or API site Worth trying Coding tools and agents may read it, and docs are already structured Software company marketing site Optional Low cost, no proven effect. Do access, answers and facts first. Local or service business Low priority AI answers rely more on listings, reviews and clear pages Online store Low priority Product data, feeds and reviews matter more Publisher or blog Optional No evidence of a citation effect If you add one, the risks are small: a few hours of work, and the file can go out of date. A stale file that points to removed pages or old prices adds wrong facts to a place that tools may read. So add it only if someone will keep it current. End of chapter 9 Next: How do you create an llms.txt file? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min How do you create an llms.txt file? Pick your most useful pages. Choose 10 to 30 pages that explain who you are, what you offer, prices, help and key policies. Write the summary. One or two plain sentences with the key facts. Use the same name and description you use everywhere else. List the links. Group them under clear headings, with a short note for each that says what the page contains. Keep it short and true. Do not add claims you would not put on your site. Do not stuff it with keywords. Publish it at the root. Make it available at yoursite.com/llms.txt with a normal 200 response. Open it in a browser to check that it shows as plain text. Keep it current. Review it whenever you change prices, services or key pages. Many “llms.txt generator” tools can draft a file from your sitemap. Because the file is short, writing it by hand takes little time, and it lets you choose which pages matter. If you use a generator, read the output and remove pages you do not want promoted, such as thin or outdated ones. The file does not control access. It is not a replacement for robots.txt. To allow or block AI crawlers, use robots.txt and your firewall settings. Our robots.txt guide explains the file. End of chapter 10 Next: How do you test whether llms.txt does anything on your site? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min How do you test whether llms.txt does anything on your site? Treat it as an experiment with a clear test. Check your logs. After you publish, look at your server or CDN logs for requests to /llms.txt . Note the user agents. If nothing asks for it in a month, you have your answer for now. Run a prompt baseline first. Before you publish, run 10 to 15 buyer questions three times in ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and record whether you are named and cited. Repeat after 60 days. SparkToro found less than a 1 in 100 chance that the same prompt returns the same list of brands twice, so a change must be large and repeated to mean anything. Change one thing at a time. If you also rewrite pages in the same month, you cannot tell which change did what. Our guide to checking if AI tools mention your brand gives a 30-minute version of this test. End of chapter 11 Next: What should you do before llms.txt? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min What should you do before llms.txt? These steps have better support: Let search crawlers in. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers. Make pages readable in HTML. In December 2024, Vercel found that none of the major AI crawlers it tested rendered JavaScript. Answer questions first, with sources. A Princeton-led test of nine content changes found that adding citations, quotations and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40%. Keep your facts consistent across your site and your profiles. Earn honest mentions on the sites that AI answers cite. Our guides to generative engine optimization and ranking in AI Overviews cover these steps in detail. End of chapter 12 Next: Worked example: a software company with a docs site → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min Worked example: a software company with a docs site This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine a company with a marketing site and a separate documentation site for its API. Its docs site has 300 pages, and developers often ask coding assistants how to use it. The team first checks that crawlers can reach the docs, and that pages render as HTML. It then writes an llms.txt file for /docs/ with a two-sentence summary and 25 links in four groups: quick start, authentication, API reference and troubleshooting. It adds Markdown versions of the 25 pages. For the marketing site, it decides not to add a file yet, because it has no evidence that the file would help there. After 30 days the team reads its logs for requests to the docs file and notes which user agents asked. It also asks three coding assistants the same 10 setup questions before and after, and records whether the answers use the right steps. It keeps the sheet whatever the result. The file stays only if the logs and tests show that something uses it. End of chapter 13 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Expecting a ranking or citation boost. No study we found shows one. Treating it as robots.txt. It does not allow or block crawlers. Listing everything. A long file defeats the purpose of a short guide. Letting it go stale. Old prices and removed pages add wrong facts. Publishing a generator’s output without a check. Remove thin, old or private pages. Doing it before the basics. Access, readable pages and clear answers come first. End of chapter 14 Next: Our interest in this topic → 15 Chapter 15 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells search and AI search services. We keep an llms.txt file on our own test site as a low-cost experiment, and we do not expect it to move results. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . Our AI search optimization service focuses on the steps with better support, and you can get your free diagnostic . End of chapter 15 Next: Final thoughts → 16 Chapter 16 · 1 min Final thoughts llms.txt is a small, optional idea with little proof behind it so far. Google says it does not use the file, and two large studies found it either unread or unrelated to citations. If you run a documentation site, try it and test it. For most other sites, fix access, readable pages, clear answers and honest mentions first, and revisit llms.txt if the evidence changes. Back matter Glossary A to Z A Agent An AI tool that takes actions or reads pages on a user's behalf. C Citation A link to your page shown as a source in an AI answer. C Crawler A program that fetches web pages for a search index or an AI tool. L llms.txt A proposed Markdown file that gives language models a short guide to a site and links to its best pages. M Markdown A simple text format that uses symbols such as # and - for headings and lists. R robots.txt A file that tells crawlers which parts of a site they may fetch. Questions FAQs What is llms.txt? llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file, written in Markdown and placed at /llms.txt, that gives language models a short summary of a site and links to its most useful pages. Jeremy Howard proposed it in September 2024. It is not an official web standard. Is llms.txt a standard? No. It is a proposal published at llmstxt.org. No major AI platform has committed to reading it, and Google says Google Search does not use it. Does llms.txt work? We found no evidence that it improves citations. SE Ranking's analysis of nearly 300,000 domains found no link, and Ahrefs found that 97% of llms.txt files in a 137,210-domain sample received no requests in May 2026. Both have limits, so test it yourself. Do ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini read llms.txt? Evidence is thin. Ahrefs saw some requests from GPTBot and Claude Code, but a fetch is not a read, and AI bots did not look for missing files. Google says Search ignores it. OpenAI's documentation focuses on OAI-SearchBot access. How do I create an llms.txt file? Pick 10 to 30 useful pages, write a one or two sentence summary, list links under clear headings with short notes, keep it accurate, publish it at yoursite.com/llms.txt and update it when facts change. A generator can draft it, but read the output. Where do I put llms.txt? At the root of your site, for example yoursite.com/llms.txt, or at a subpath such as /docs/llms.txt to cover only that section. It should return a normal 200 response and show as plain text. Does llms.txt replace robots.txt? No. llms.txt guides content discovery, but it does not allow or block crawlers. Use robots.txt and your firewall settings for access. Will llms.txt hurt my SEO? Google says that having an llms.txt file will neither help nor harm your visibility in Google Search. The main risk is a stale file that lists wrong prices or removed pages. Should I use an llms.txt generator? You can, since the file is short and tools can draft it from your sitemap. Read the result and remove thin, old or private pages. Writing it by hand takes little time and lets you choose the pages that matter. Who should add llms.txt? Documentation and API sites are the best candidates, since coding tools may read it. For most marketing sites it is optional. Fix crawler access, readable HTML, answer-first pages, consistent facts and mentions first. In marketing it means making your content and brand easy for answer engines such as Google's AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity to understand, trust and cite. It builds on SEO: answer the question first, prove it with sources, keep facts consistent and current, earn honest mentions on other sites and measure with a fixed prompt list. 01 AEO means answer engine optimization: earning a place in answers from AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. 02 Forrester calls AEO significantly, but not fundamentally, different from SEO. Google says optimizing for AI search is still SEO. 03 G2 surveyed 1,169 B2B buyers: 79% said AI search changed their research and chatbots were the top shortlist influence at 17.1%. 04 Gartner forecast a 25% drop in search volume by 2026. It is a forecast, and we found nothing that confirms it. 05 Content marketing for AEO starts from a question map, answer-first pages, sourced evidence and regular refreshes. 06 Adding citations, quotations and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40% in a Princeton-led test. It is a 2024 benchmark. 07 Measure a rate across many runs. SparkToro found under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice. AEO stands for answer engine optimization. In marketing, AEO is the practice of making your content and brand easy for answer engines, such as Google’s AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, to understand, trust and use in their answers. The goal moves from “get the click” to “be named and cited when a buyer asks a question.” It builds on SEO. It does not replace it. This guide gives a plain definition, shows how AEO differs from SEO and GEO, and explains why it matters for marketers. It also covers how to use content marketing for AEO, a seven-step plan, how to measure it and a worked example. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we say when a figure is a survey, a forecast or one vendor’s data. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is AEO in marketing? What does it stand for? AEO means answer engine optimization. An answer engine is a tool that gives a direct answer to a question, instead of only a list of links. Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode, ChatGPT search, Gemini, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot are examples. Voice assistants and featured snippets work in a similar way. So when people ask “what is AEO in digital marketing”, the answer is this: it is the work of earning a place in those answers. You may also see “what is AEO and GEO in marketing”. GEO stands for generative engine optimization. The two terms overlap a great deal. AEO is often used for being the direct answer, including in snippets and voice. GEO is often used for being cited by generative AI tools. Many teams do one body of work and use both names. Our guide to AEO vs SEO and our guide to GEO vs SEO cover the details. End of chapter 1 Next: What is the meaning of AEO? A short definition → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min What is the meaning of AEO? A short definition AEO means answer engine optimization. It is the practice of shaping your content so that search engines and AI tools can take it as the direct answer to a question. In digital marketing, that means a clear answer first, then proof, then structure that a machine can read. The same letters mean something else in trade. In customs, AEO stands for Authorized Economic Operator, a status for trusted traders. If you searched for “AEO certification,” that is a different subject. This guide covers the marketing meaning. What is AEO and GEO in marketing? GEO means generative engine optimization. AEO aims to make your page the answer. GEO aims to get your brand cited or named in answers that AI tools write. Marketers often do both with the same pages. Read our guides to AEO vs SEO and GEO vs SEO for the differences. End of chapter 2 Next: What is AEO in digital marketing? → Reinforce Lab service · AI Search Optimization Want an AEO plan built on your buyers' questions? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See AI search optimization → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 1 min What is AEO in digital marketing? In digital marketing, AEO is short for answer engine optimization. The full form is “answer engine optimization.” It is the work of making your content easy for search answer boxes and AI tools to find, understand and quote. Some writers say “AEO and GEO” together. GEO, or generative engine optimization, is a close cousin that focuses on being mentioned in AI-written answers. The two share most of their tasks. One note on the letters. In trade and customs, AEO means Authorized Economic Operator. That is a different subject. This guide is about the marketing meaning. End of chapter 3 Next: How is AEO different from SEO? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min How is AEO different from SEO? Forrester describes AEO as significantly, but not fundamentally, different from SEO. Both shape what people see on and off your site, both span content and technical work, and both are hard to measure. That is a fair summary. The table shows the main differences in daily work. Area SEO AEO Goal Rankings and clicks Being named, cited and described correctly in answers Question style Short keywords Full questions, comparisons and follow-ups Content shape A page that matches intent A page with a direct answer, then proof and detail Off-site work Links Links, mentions, reviews and consistent profiles Measurement Rank, traffic, conversions Mention rate, citations, branded search, AI impressions Google takes a plain view. In its guide to generative AI features, it says that optimizing for generative AI search is optimizing for the search experience, and so it is still SEO. It advises care with third-party “AEO” or “GEO” advice. End of chapter 4 Next: Why does AEO matter for marketers? → 05 Chapter 5 · 1 min Why does AEO matter for marketers? Three kinds of evidence point the same way. They differ in quality, so we state the limits. Buyers use AI to research. G2 surveyed 1,169 B2B decision-makers in April 2025. It found that 79% said AI search had changed how they research, and 29% said they start with AI search more often than Google. Generative AI chatbots were the top source influencing vendor shortlists, at 17.1%. The sample is software buyers who answered G2’s survey, and G2 sells software review services. Clicks fall when an AI summary appears. The Pew Research Center tracked 900 US adults in March 2025. People clicked a regular result in 8% of visits to pages with an AI summary and 15% of visits to pages without one, and clicked a link inside the summary in 1% of visits. Google disputes the study’s method. A forecast says search volume will fall. In February 2024, Gartner predicted that traditional search engine volume would drop 25% by 2026, with search marketing losing share to AI chatbots and other virtual agents. It is a forecast, not a measurement. We did not find a source that confirms the figure, so treat it as a view that was current when it was made. The practical lesson is that being named in the answer matters, even when no click follows. That is why AEO measures mentions and citations as well as traffic. End of chapter 5 Next: How do answer engines choose what to cite? → 06 Chapter 6 · 1 min How do answer engines choose what to cite? The companies do not publish exact rules. What they say is limited. OpenAI says ChatGPT ranks search results using multiple factors meant to help people find relevant, reliable information, and that placement is not guaranteed. Google says its AI features use query fan-out, where one question is split into related searches, and that a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet to be a supporting link. From the documents we read, three things seem to matter. This is our reading and not a formula: Access: the page can be crawled, indexed and read in the HTML. Fit: the page answers the question, or a related one, in a passage that stands alone. Trust: the facts are clear and sourced, the author is named, and other sites agree with what you say. End of chapter 6 Next: Content marketing for AEO → 07 Chapter 7 · 2 min Content marketing for AEO Content marketing is where most teams do their AEO work. The shift is small in method and large in discipline. Start from questions, not topics, write the answer first, prove it, and keep it current. Here is how to adapt a normal content program. Start with a question map List 20 to 30 questions your buyers ask, from sales calls, support tickets, review sites, Search Console queries and “People also ask”. Group them by stage: awareness (“what is X”), consideration (“X vs Y”, “best X for Z”) and decision (“how much does X cost”, “how do I switch”). Mark which ones your site already answers well, and which it does not. Choose the content types that answer questions Content type Answers AEO tip Definition page or glossary entry “What is [term]?” A one or two sentence definition first, then detail How-to guide “How do I [task]?” Numbered steps and a short summary at the top Comparison page “[A] vs [B]”, “best [category]” A dated table and a verdict, with honest limits Pricing and cost page “How much does it cost?” State prices, or the factors that set them FAQ section Common follow-ups Use real questions in the buyer’s words Original data or research Questions with no good source yet State the method, sample and limits Case study “Does it work for someone like me?” Dates, a baseline and what else changed Write for people first Put the answer in the first sentence under each question heading, then add context, examples and sources. Keep paragraphs short and give each section one idea. Google warns that making separate pages for every small variation of a question, mainly to manipulate rankings or AI answers, breaks its scaled content abuse policy. So build fewer, better pages, and answer related questions inside them. Add evidence A Princeton-led team tested nine content changes on a 10,000-query benchmark. It reported that adding citations, quotations from relevant sources and statistics lifted visibility by up to 40%. That is a 2024 benchmark, and results varied by domain. It still supports a good habit: name the source, the date and the method for every number. Refresh and repeat Ahrefs analyzed 17 million citations across seven AI search platforms and found that content cited in AI answers was 25.7% fresher than content in regular results. That is a correlation from one vendor’s data. Still, review key pages each quarter, fix facts that changed and show a real update date. End of chapter 7 Next: What is an answer engine optimization strategy? → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min What is an answer engine optimization strategy? An answer engine optimization strategy is a short plan for which questions you want to answer, which pages will answer them and how you will check the results. It has three parts: a list of the questions your buyers ask, a clear answer for each on the right page, and a routine to test whether AI tools and answer boxes use you. The seven steps below turn that into a working plan. End of chapter 8 Next: A seven-step AEO plan → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min A seven-step AEO plan Check access. Make sure the search crawlers you want, such as Googlebot, Bingbot and OAI-SearchBot, are not blocked by robots.txt or your firewall. Our robots.txt guide explains the file. Run a baseline. Test your question list in several AI tools, three runs each, and record whether you are named, cited and described correctly. Fix your facts. Make your name, description, prices and locations match on your site and in directories. Write or rewrite the key pages with answer-first openings, clear headings and sourced evidence. Build real presence on other sites. Run your prompts, list the sites the answers cite, and ask how you can appear on them honestly, with profiles, reviews and useful contributions. Measure. Repeat the test monthly, and use free reports from Google and Bing. Refresh. Update pages when facts change, and review the plan each quarter. End of chapter 9 Next: How do you measure AEO? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min How do you measure AEO? No single number captures it. Use a small set of signs: Mention and citation rate across a fixed prompt list. SparkToro had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s AI features 2,961 times, and found less than a 1 in 100 chance of getting the same list of brands twice. So run each prompt several times and report a rate, not a rank. Google’s Generative AI performance report in Search Console, which shows impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Bing Webmaster Tools’ AI Performance report , which shows citations in Copilot and Bing’s AI summaries. Bing says its grounding queries are a sample. Branded search in Search Console, which may rise when you are named without a link. Leads and sales from pages you updated, tracked in analytics. Our guide to checking if AI tools mention your brand gives a 30-minute test. End of chapter 10 Next: What does AEO not require? → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min What does AEO not require? Much AEO advice online has no source. Google says that for Google Search you do not need llms.txt files or other special files, “chunking” content into tiny pieces, rewriting content just for AI, or special structured data. It also says no third-party tool has access to its internal ranking or AI systems. This is Google’s view of Google Search, and other tools may behave differently. Do the basics first, and test any extra step before you spend on it. End of chapter 11 Next: Worked example: a three-person B2B marketing team → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min Worked example: a three-person B2B marketing team This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine a team that sells HR software to mid-sized companies. It builds a map of 24 questions from sales calls. Its site answers six well, answers nine poorly and does not answer nine. The team tests the 24 questions three times in three tools, 216 answers in all, and is named in 14. The answers cite two review sites and a competitor’s comparison page. The team picks six questions, including “how much does HR software cost” and “[competitor] alternative”, and writes or rewrites six pages with answer-first openings, dated tables and two sourced statistics each. It also completes its profiles on both review sites. After 60 days it repeats the same 216 runs and compares the rate of mentions, then looks at the demo requests from the six pages. The result may be small or large. The plan makes it readable. End of chapter 12 Next: What does AEO look like for different businesses? → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min What does AEO look like for different businesses? Business Typical questions Focus B2B software and services “Best [category] for [role]”, “[A] vs [B]”, “how much does it cost” Comparison, pricing and use-case pages, review-site profiles, clear integration facts Online stores “Best [product] for [need]”, “is [brand] worth it” Complete product data, honest reviews, buying guides, consistent names and codes Local and service firms “Who does [job] near me”, “how much does [service] cost” Accurate listings, service pages with prices or ranges, named experts Publishers and educators “What is [term]”, “how does [thing] work” Clear definitions, named authors, sources and dates, original data In every case, start with the questions your own buyers ask. The test is whether a stranger who asks an AI tool that question would be told about you, and told the truth. End of chapter 13 Next: Which AEO tools help? → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min Which AEO tools help? You can begin with a spreadsheet and free tools: the AI tools themselves, Search Console’s Generative AI performance report, Bing Webmaster Tools and your analytics. SEO suites such as Ahrefs and Semrush offer AI visibility features, including prompt research, and stand-alone trackers run prompts on a schedule. Run a hand test first, so you can judge whether a tool’s numbers are right, and be careful with any tool that reports a precise rank inside AI answers. Our guide to AI brand visibility tools compares what they track and what they cost. End of chapter 14 Next: How long does AEO take, and what does it cost? → 15 Chapter 15 · 1 min How long does AEO take, and what does it cost? We found no independent data on typical timelines or fees. Access and fact fixes can change retrieval-based answers within weeks, while new content, reviews and outside mentions take longer. The cost depends on how many questions you cover, how much content you write, and whether you need technical fixes and outreach. If you hire help, compare proposals on deliverables, not on the monthly figure, and be wary of promises of placement. Nobody controls AI answers. End of chapter 15 Next: Does structured data matter for AEO? → 16 Chapter 16 · 1 min Does structured data matter for AEO? Vendor guides often list FAQ, how-to and article markup as AEO tactics. Google’s position is narrower. It says structured data is not required for its generative AI features and that no special schema.org markup is needed, though it still helps with rich result eligibility and clear facts. So use markup that matches your visible content, validate it, and do not expect it to earn a citation by itself. Put the effort first into the answer, the evidence and the facts. Then keep important pages fresh: Ahrefs found that content cited in AI answers was 25.7% fresher than content in regular results, a correlation from one vendor’s data, and the practical step is to review key pages on a schedule and show a real update date. End of chapter 16 Next: What can you do this week? → 17 Chapter 17 · 1 min What can you do this week? You do not need a big program to begin. In one week, you can do five things. On day one, write down 15 questions your buyers ask. On day two, run each three times in ChatGPT and Google, and save the answers in a sheet. On day three, check your robots.txt and firewall for blocks on search crawlers. On day four, compare your name, description and prices across your site and your top three profiles, and fix the mismatches. On day five, pick the one question where you lose most clearly, and rewrite the page that should answer it, with the answer in the first sentence and two sourced facts. Then repeat the same test in a month. That small loop teaches more than any report. End of chapter 17 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 18 Chapter 18 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Treating AEO as a separate trick. Most of it is good SEO with clearer answers and evidence. Making a page for every phrasing. Google calls mass pages made to manipulate results scaled content abuse. Using unsourced numbers. A figure with no source is a risk to readers and to models. Chasing a rank in AI answers. Lists change from run to run. Ignoring other sites. Answers often rely on reviews, lists and directories. Testing once. One answer is a clue, not a result. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . Our SEO content systems service and AI search optimization service follow the plan above, and you can get your free diagnostic . Start with your buyers’ questions, write the answer first, prove it with sources, keep facts consistent and current, and earn honest mentions on the sites that answers cite. It is the practice of shaping pages so they give clear, direct answers to the questions people ask. What is the AEO definition? AEO is the practice of structuring content and building trust so that answer engines, such as AI tools and search answer boxes, choose your content as the answer to a question. What is AEO marketing? AEO marketing is marketing work done to make your content the answer. It covers question research, direct answers on your pages, trust signals and tests of how AI tools and answer boxes describe your brand. What is an answer engine optimization strategy? A plan for the questions you will answer, the pages that answer them and the checks that show whether AI tools and answer boxes use your content. It means letting crawlers in, fixing firm facts, writing practice pages that answer first and cite the law, showing the lawyers behind them, keeping directory profiles honest and testing monthly what AI tools say. Every claim must stay inside your advertising rules, and no one can promise a place in AI answers. 01 GEO stands for generative engine optimization. For a firm it is good SEO plus clear facts, answer-first practice pages and honest third-party profiles. 02 Clio surveyed 1,000 US adults: 24% had used AI for a legal question and 46% would consult AI before contacting a lawyer. 03 ABA Model Rule 7.1 bars false or misleading communications. Every page an AI tool may quote must be accurate, current and supportable. 04 Citing statutes and sources helped visibility by up to 40% in a Princeton-led test. It is a 2024 benchmark, not a guarantee. 05 SparkToro found under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice, so measure a rate across many prompts. 06 Build city pages only where you have a real office or practice. Google warns against pages made to manipulate results. 07 This is general marketing information, not legal advice. Check your own bar rules. GEO for law firms means making your firm and your lawyers easy for AI tools to find, understand and name accurately when people ask legal questions. GEO stands for generative engine optimization. In practice it is good SEO plus clear firm facts, answer-first practice pages, strong lawyer bios, honest profiles on the sites AI answers cite, and a monthly check of what the tools say. It must also follow your advertising rules, because a false or misleading claim is a risk whether a person or an AI tool repeats it. This guide explains how GEO works for a firm, what the data shows, and a plan you can run. It includes a worked example and a short section on choosing an agency. This is general marketing information, not legal advice. Advertising rules differ by state and country, so check your own bar or regulator before you publish. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we say when a figure is a survey or a test. 01 Chapter 1 · 1 min What is GEO for law firms? Generative engine optimization is work that helps AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews cite and recommend your content. For a law firm it covers two kinds of questions. The first is informational: “how long do I have to file a claim”, “do I need a lawyer for a slip and fall”, “what does probate cost”. The second is a shopping question: “best family lawyer near me” or “what should I ask a divorce lawyer”. Our guide to generative engine optimization explains the general method. This article applies it to legal services, where trust, accuracy and ethics rules matter more than in most fields. End of chapter 1 Next: Why does it matter for law firms? → 02 Chapter 2 · 1 min Why does it matter for law firms? Clients are already using AI. Clio’s 2025 Legal Trends Report surveyed 1,000 US adults, a sample that matches the US population by age, gender, region, income and race. It found that 24% had already used AI to answer a legal question, and another 40% would consider it. 46% said they would consult AI before contacting a lawyer. Of those who had used AI for a legal question, 28% were directed by the AI to contact a lawyer, and in 12% of cases the AI convinced them their problem was not worth pursuing. Clio also found that more consumers say they would look for their next lawyer online. This is a survey of self-reported behavior by a software company, so read it as a direction, not an exact count. The same report notes that many consumers asked AI how to find “the best” lawyer. If AI tools are shaping how people shop, your firm needs to be named correctly in those answers. End of chapter 2 Next: What do the advertising rules say? → Reinforce Lab service · Generative Engine Optimization Want a compliant GEO plan for your firm? Reinforce Lab starts with a free diagnostic of your Google and AI search visibility and a 90-day plan. See generative engine optimization → Or get a free diagnostic first 03 Chapter 3 · 1 min What do the advertising rules say? In the US, ABA Model Rule 7.1 says a lawyer shall not make a false or misleading communication about the lawyer or the lawyer’s services. It adds that a communication is false or misleading if it contains a material misrepresentation of fact or law, or leaves out a fact needed to keep the statement from being misleading as a whole. States adopt their own versions, and many add rules on testimonials, specialist claims and past results. Check yours. For GEO, the practical meaning is simple. Everything on your site and your profiles can be quoted by an AI tool, so every claim must be accurate, current and supportable. That includes: No promise or implied guarantee of a result. No “best” or “top” claim you cannot support. Past results stated with the context your bar requires. No specialist or certified label that your jurisdiction does not allow. A lawyer reviews every page, including pages drafted with AI help. Never write GEO content that is designed to mislead a model. Even if it worked, it would put your license and your reputation at risk. End of chapter 3 Next: What does the evidence say about getting cited? → 04 Chapter 4 · 1 min What does the evidence say about getting cited? Evidence in the page helps, in a test. A Princeton-led team tested nine content changes on a 10,000-query benchmark. They reported that adding citations, quotations from relevant sources and statistics boosted visibility by up to 40%, with gains up to 37% on Perplexity. The effect varied by domain, and the study dates from 2024. For lawyers, the natural version is to cite the statute, the court rule or the agency page. Answers change from run to run. SparkToro had 600 volunteers run 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s AI features 2,961 times. There was less than a 1 in 100 chance of the same list of brands twice. So measure how often you appear across many prompts, and do not chase a rank. Crawl access can decide it. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. Security plugins and CDN settings sometimes block bots without anyone noticing. Google adds no special requirements. To be a supporting link in AI Overviews or AI Mode, a page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet, and Google lists no additional technical requirements. End of chapter 4 Next: An eight-step GEO plan for a law firm → 05 Chapter 5 · 3 min An eight-step GEO plan for a law firm Step 1: Let the right crawlers in Open your robots.txt and your security settings. Make sure Googlebot, Bingbot and OAI-SearchBot are not blocked on the pages you want cited. Whether you allow training bots is a separate choice. Our robots.txt guide explains the file. Step 2: Fix your firm facts Write one set of facts: the legal name, address format, main phone number, offices, practice areas, and the names and roles of your lawyers. Make your website, Google Business Profile, bar and directory listings, and social profiles match. An AI tool that sees three versions of your address may repeat the wrong one, or skip you. Step 3: Build practice pages that answer the question first For each practice area, answer what a client actually asks: who you represent, what the process looks like in your state, how long it usually takes, how fees work and what to do now. Put a direct answer in the first sentence under each heading, then add detail and exceptions. Name the state or country the answer covers, and the date it was checked. Law changes, and old advice can mislead. Step 4: Show who stands behind the content Give each lawyer a real bio page with bar admissions, courts, practice areas, education and published work. Link each practice page to the lawyers who handle that work, and add a named author or reviewer to legal articles. Google’s guidance for generative AI features says unique, expert-led content with a clear point of view matters more over time than tricks. Use LegalService markup for the firm and Person markup for each lawyer if you like. Google says special markup is not required for its AI features, but accurate markup can make the facts clearer. Step 5: Cite your sources Link to the statute, rule, court decision or government page that supports each factual claim, and quote the key text where it helps. This matches the tactic with the best test evidence, and it makes your page more useful to a reader who wants to check it. Step 6: Keep your profiles and reviews honest and current AI answers often draw on third-party sources, not only your site. Common ones for lawyers include your state bar’s public directory, legal directories, Google reviews and local press. Run your prompts, list the sites the answers cite, and claim and complete the profiles that matter. Ask real clients for honest reviews, and follow your bar’s rules on how you ask. Never post fake reviews. Step 7: Build local pages only where they are real Create a city or county page only where you have an office or regularly handle matters, and make it useful: local courts, procedures, how to meet you. Google warns that making many pages to manipulate rankings or AI answers breaks its scaled content abuse policy, and pages that only swap a city name add risk and no value. Step 8: Measure monthly Write 15 to 25 prompts your clients would use, split by practice area and city. Run each three times in ChatGPT, Google and Perplexity, and record whether your firm is named, whether your site is linked, which sources the answers cite and which competitors appear. Use Search Console’s Generative AI performance report for Google impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Our guides on checking if AI tools mention your brand and AI brand visibility tools explain how to do this. End of chapter 5 Next: What should a practice page contain? → 06 Chapter 6 · 2 min What should a practice page contain? A practice page works for people and for AI tools when each part answers one clear question. Use this outline and adapt it to your practice area and your state. Section What it answers Tip Opening answer What this area of law covers and whom you help One or two plain sentences, then detail How the process works The usual steps and who is involved Name the state, court or agency and the date you checked Time limits and key rules Deadlines and rules that matter Cite the statute or rule, and say when it changed if it did Fees and costs How you charge and what affects the price A range or the factors, if your rules allow it What to do now Safe first steps for a client Keep it general and add a notice that it is not legal advice Your lawyers Who handles this work Link to bios with admissions and experience FAQs The questions clients ask on calls Use the client’s words, and answer in the first sentence The fee question matters. Marketers who work with small firms say one of the first questions a prospective client asks an AI tool is what a lawyer will cost, and a page that answers it has a better chance of being cited. That is a practitioner view, not a measured result. Answer it only as far as your rules and your practice allow. End of chapter 6 Next: What do clients ask AI about lawyers? → 07 Chapter 7 · 1 min What do clients ask AI about lawyers? Clients ask two kinds of questions, and each needs a different page. Information questions: “how long does probate take”, “what happens at a first DUI hearing”, “can my landlord keep my deposit”. These are answered by practice pages and plain guides. Be careful to give general information and to say it is not legal advice. Shopping questions: “best personal injury lawyer in my city”, “what to ask a divorce lawyer before hiring”. These are answered by third-party sources, reviews and lists, and by your own pages on how to choose a lawyer. Write that page honestly, with questions a client should ask any firm, and include what you do. Clio found that many consumers asked AI how to find “the best” lawyer. If an AI tool typically lists key questions to ask, prepare strong, honest answers to each on your site. End of chapter 7 Next: How is GEO different from local SEO for law firms? → 08 Chapter 8 · 1 min How is GEO different from local SEO for law firms? Local SEO aims to put your firm in the map pack and local results. It rests on your Google Business Profile, reviews, consistent name, address and phone number, and local pages. GEO builds on those same facts, and adds work on how AI tools describe you: answer-first pages, lawyer credentials, sourced claims and the third-party sites that AI answers cite. If your local SEO is weak, fix it first, because many AI answers about local services rely on the same listings. Our local SEO service covers that base. End of chapter 8 Next: Does GEO work for every practice area? → 09 Chapter 9 · 1 min Does GEO work for every practice area? The method is the same, but the risks and the questions differ. Personal injury, family, immigration, criminal defense and estate planning all attract AI questions, and each has its own rules on advertising, results and confidentiality. Practice areas with strict rules on solicitation or testimonials need more care. Competition also differs by city and by area, so test your own prompts to see which firms and sources the tools name before you plan content. End of chapter 9 Next: What about Bing, ChatGPT and attorney markup? → 10 Chapter 10 · 1 min What about Bing, ChatGPT and attorney markup? OpenAI says ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers, and its notes name Microsoft, so check that your key pages are indexed in Bing as well as Google. Bing Webmaster Tools lets you submit a sitemap and see AI citations in its AI Performance report. For markup, one law-firm guide recommends LegalService for the firm and Person for each lawyer, with sameAs links to the lawyer’s state bar profile and legal directories, kept consistent with what the page shows. Google says no special markup is required for its AI features, so treat markup as a way to state facts clearly and not as a trick. A short audit for a firm is to check four things: crawler access, Bing and Google indexing, matching facts across the site and profiles, and a bio page for every lawyer with admissions and focus areas. End of chapter 10 Next: Worked example: a six-lawyer family law firm → 11 Chapter 11 · 1 min Worked example: a six-lawyer family law firm This is an illustration, not a client result. Imagine a firm with offices in two cities. Its site has one page called “Family Law” with 300 words, no author, and an address that differs on its site and its directory listings. The team runs 18 prompts three times in three tools, 162 answers in all. The firm is named in 11, about 7%. The answers cite two directories and a local news site where the firm is not listed, and one competitor’s guide to custody rules. The plan has five parts. The firm fixes its address everywhere. It splits the family page into five pages, such as divorce process and custody, each with an answer-first opening, the state statute cited and a reviewer byline. It adds bios for all six lawyers. It completes its two directory profiles, and asks former clients for honest reviews in line with its bar’s rules. After 60 days it repeats the same 162 runs. Whatever the result, the firm keeps the sheet. The aim is a fair comparison, not a promise of leads. End of chapter 11 Next: How do you choose a GEO agency for a law firm? → 12 Chapter 12 · 1 min How do you choose a GEO agency for a law firm? Choose an agency that knows legal advertising rules and says so in writing. Ask who will review claims for compliance, how past results and testimonials are handled, and whether a lawyer at your firm approves each page. Ask for the prompt list, the raw answers, a source map and a ranked fix list. Be wary of any promise of a place in AI answers, because the AI companies do not publish how they choose. Our generative engine optimization service follows this method, and our professional services work covers firms like yours. End of chapter 12 Next: What are the common mistakes? → 13 Chapter 13 · 1 min What are the common mistakes? Thin practice pages. One short page for each practice area gives a model little to quote. Unreviewed AI content. A lawyer must check every page for accuracy and for advertising compliance. Inconsistent firm facts. Different addresses and names across sites cause confusion. City pages with swapped names. They add risk and no value. Chasing a rank in AI answers. The order changes from run to run. Ignoring third-party sources. The answer may rely on a directory you have not claimed. Skipping the rules. Superlatives, guarantees and unclear results can breach your bar’s rules. End of chapter 13 Next: Our interest in this topic → 14 Chapter 14 · 1 min Our interest in this topic Reinforce Lab sells SEO and AI search services, including to professional services firms. We are a marketing firm, not a law firm, and nothing here is legal advice. Nothing is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure . You can get your free diagnostic , which tests your site and a prompt list with a written plan. End of chapter 14 Next: Final thoughts → 15 Chapter 15 · 1 min Final thoughts For a law firm, GEO starts with trust. Get crawlers in, fix your facts, write practice pages that answer first and cite the law, show the lawyers behind them, and earn honest profiles on the sites AI answers cite. Keep every claim inside your advertising rules, test monthly, and judge the work by what clients ask and who calls. Back matter Glossary A to Z E Entity A clearly named thing, such as a firm or a lawyer, that an AI tool can recognize. G GEO Generative engine optimization: work that helps AI tools cite and recommend your content. L LegalService markup Structured data that describes a law firm to search engines. M Model Rule 7.1 The ABA rule against false or misleading communications about a lawyer's services. Questions FAQs What is GEO for law firms? GEO, or generative engine optimization, helps AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews find, understand and accurately name your firm when people ask legal questions. For a firm it adds clear facts, answer-first practice pages, strong lawyer bios and honest profiles to good SEO. Why does GEO matter for lawyers? Clients use AI before they call. Clio's 2025 survey of 1,000 US adults found 24% had used AI for a legal question and 46% would consult AI before contacting a lawyer. If tools shape the shortlist, your firm needs to be described correctly in the answer. Do the advertising rules apply to AI answers? They apply to what you publish. ABA Model Rule 7.1 bars false or misleading communications about a lawyer's services, and states add rules on results, testimonials and specialist claims. An AI tool may repeat your page, so keep every claim accurate and supportable. How can my law firm appear in ChatGPT? Let OAI-SearchBot crawl your pages, keep firm facts consistent, publish answer-first practice pages that cite the law, show lawyer credentials and keep directory profiles complete. OpenAI says sites that opt out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. Do I need schema markup for AI search? Not as a requirement. Google lists no extra technical requirements for AI Overviews beyond being indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. Accurate LegalService and Person markup can make your facts clearer, but it does not guarantee a citation. Should my firm have city pages? Only where you have an office or regularly handle matters, and only if each page is useful, with local courts, procedures and how to meet you. Google warns that making pages mainly to manipulate results breaks its scaled content abuse policy. How do I check if AI tools mention my firm? Write 15 to 25 client questions by practice area and city, run each three times in ChatGPT, Google and Perplexity, and record whether you are named, linked and described correctly. SparkToro found answers rarely repeat, so look at rates across many runs. How long does GEO take for a law firm? We found no reliable study. Access and fact fixes can show up in retrieval-based answers within weeks, while reviews, mentions and new content take longer. Judge progress by repeating the same prompt test. Can a law firm pay to be cited by AI tools? We found no paid placement for organic AI answers. Be wary of any agency that promises one. Focus on accurate pages, honest profiles and the sources the answers already cite. How do I choose a GEO agency for a law firm? Choose one that understands legal advertising rules and has a lawyer at your firm approve each page. Ask for the prompt list, raw answers, a source map and a ranked fix list, and avoid promises of placement.
