Back matter Glossary A to Z H Human gate A point where a named person must approve before work moves on. O Orchestration tool Software that moves data and triggers actions between other tools. S Shadow mode Running an AI step alongside the person who does the task today, and comparing outputs before it touches live work. S Source pack A set of dated, checked sources given to a writer or an AI tool for a draft. S System of record The main database for a type of data, such as the CRM for contacts. W Workflow The path work takes from request to finished result, with steps, owners and statuses. Questions FAQs What is marketing workflow automation? It is software, increasingly with AI, that moves marketing work between steps by rules: request, brief, draft, review, publish and report. AI adds drafting, summarizing, classifying and checking that rules alone cannot do. How is marketing workflow automation different from marketing automation? Marketing automation usually means customer-facing flows such as welcome emails and cart reminders. Workflow automation is about how your own team works, such as intake, briefs, approvals, publishing and reporting. A good plan treats them together. Where should a marketing team start with AI workflow automation? Map one process that already hurts and mark where work waits or repeats. Pick steps that are frequent, rule-based, internal and low risk, such as intake, routing, reminders, reporting data pulls and first drafts, and keep human gates on anything customer-facing. What marketing workflows can be automated with AI? Campaign intake and briefs, content production stages, review routing, lead routing, repurposing a published piece, pre-launch checks of links and tracking, report drafting and SEO operations alerts. Each needs a named human gate. How much should AI be allowed to do on its own? Use an autonomy ladder: suggest, draft, act with approval, then act and report. Most marketing tasks should stay at levels one to three. Move up one level at a time, and only where the record shows few errors. How do you use AI in marketing reporting safely? Let AI write the narrative, never the numbers. Pull figures from an export or API, have a person verify each figure and causal claim, and avoid pasting screenshots into a chat in place of data. Are marketing teams ready for AI? Surveys of large companies suggest many are not. Gartner's 2026 CMO survey found 70% say their marketing processes are not mature enough to scale AI, and only 30% report mature readiness. Start small and measure. How do you measure marketing workflow automation? Track cycle time from request to live, waiting time at each gate, rework rate, AI error rate found at review, cost per asset, whether the team uses the workflow and business results such as qualified leads. What tools do you need for marketing workflow automation? Usually a work management tool for tasks and statuses, an orchestration tool such as Zapier, Make or n8n to move data, and your CRM and email platform as the system of record. Audit tools you own first, since Gartner found 49% average utilization. What are the risks of AI in marketing workflows? Wrong or unsupported claims, privacy and consent problems, brand and legal risk, speeding up one step and shifting the bottleneck, and no audit trail. Reduce them with source packs, human gates, shadow mode and logs. How do you automate marketing with AI? Pick one repeatable task, write the steps as you do them today, and automate the steps a rule can handle. Add AI for drafting or sorting, and keep a person approving anything public or costly. What is the difference between AI agents and automation? Automation follows steps you set in advance. An AI agent decides some of its own steps. Start with automation for well-defined tasks and use an agent only when the steps cannot be written down. What is AI automation for marketing? It is using AI inside automated marketing workflows, for tasks such as sorting leads, drafting copy or summarizing reports, with rules and human review around it.
